# Page: Encoder-Only & Embedding Models

# Encoder-Only & Embedding Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



This section covers encoder-only transformer models and embedding-oriented wrappers represented in the codebase. It focuses on BERT-style embeddings, ModernBERT and its decoder variant, ESM protein models, and the `timm` wrapper. The codebase implements specialized encoder architectures and task heads suited for contextual representation extraction, classification, masked-language modeling, and protein contact prediction [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:30-108](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:51-92](), [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:28-102](), [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:59-113]().

Sources: [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:30-108](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:51-92](), [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:28-102](), [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:59-113](), [tests/models/modernbert/test_modeling_modernbert.py:155-179]()

---

## 1. BERT-Family Encoders

`BertEmbeddings` builds token representations by combining word, position, and token-type embeddings, then applying LayerNorm and dropout [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:53-108](). `BertSelfAttention` defines separate query, key, and value projections; the eager attention helper computes scaled dot-product attention, applies an optional mask, normalizes scores, and combines the result with values [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:111-157]().

`XLMRobertaXLEmbeddings` also combines word, position, and token-type embeddings. It constructs position IDs from either `input_ids` or `inputs_embeds`, and keeps non-padding positions distinct when deriving IDs from token IDs [src/transformers/models/xlm_roberta_xl/modeling_xlm_roberta_xl.py:61-123]().

The listed task output types in the BERT modeling module include masked-language-model, sequence-classification, token-classification, question-answering, and multiple-choice outputs [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:30-40]().

### Key Classes & Data Flow

- **`BertEmbeddings`**: Accepts token IDs or precomputed embeddings, adds token-type and position embeddings, then applies LayerNorm and dropout [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:53-108]().
- **`XLMRobertaXLEmbeddings`**: Builds multilingual encoder embeddings and derives padding-aware position IDs when token IDs are supplied [src/transformers/models/xlm_roberta_xl/modeling_xlm_roberta_xl.py:61-123]().
- **`BertSelfAttention`**: Projects hidden states into query, key, and value tensors. The neighboring `eager_attention_forward` helper performs scaled dot-product attention and returns attention output and weights [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:111-157](), [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:139-157]().

**Title: BERT Encoder Data Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InputIDs["input_ids_or_inputs_embeds"] --> BertEmbeddings["BertEmbeddings"]
    BertEmbeddings --> BertSelfAttention["BertSelfAttention"]
    BertSelfAttention --> EagerAttention["eager_attention_forward"]
    EagerAttention --> Context["attention_output"]
    Context --> EncoderOutput["model_output"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py:30-157](), [src/transformers/models/xlm_roberta_xl/modeling_xlm_roberta_xl.py:61-123]()

---

## 2. ModernBERT and ModernBERT Decoder Variant

ModernBERT’s configuration includes layer types for full versus sliding-window attention, rotary-position parameters, classifier pooling options, and masked-language-model sparse-prediction settings. If `layer_types` is unset, `ModernBertConfig.__post_init__` derives a layer-type sequence using `global_attn_every_n_layers`, defaulting that interval to three [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modular_modernbert.py:52-80](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modular_modernbert.py:97-144]().

The generated modeling file defines `ModernBertEmbeddings`, which performs token embedding lookup (or accepts `inputs_embeds`), followed by normalization and dropout. `ModernBertMLP` projects hidden states to two intermediate branches, applies the configured activation to one branch, gates it with the other, and projects the result back to hidden size [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:51-92]().

`ModernBertRotaryEmbedding` initializes inverse frequencies and attention scaling per configured layer type. It selects a RoPE initializer from `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS` for non-default rope types [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:93-113]().

The decoder variant has corresponding `ModernBertDecoderEmbeddings`, `ModernBertDecoderMLP`, and `ModernBertDecoderRotaryEmbedding` classes. Its modeling module imports causal and sliding-window causal mask constructors, `GenerationMixin`, and cache types, distinguishing its causal-generation path from the bidirectional encoder path [src/transformers/models/modernbert_decoder/modeling_modernbert_decoder.py:21-42](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert_decoder/modeling_modernbert_decoder.py:48-88]().

### Configuration – `ModernBertConfig`

`ModernBertConfig` declares dimensions, token IDs, dropout and bias options, classifier pooling, and sparse-prediction controls. Its `__post_init__` creates alternating `"sliding_attention"` and `"full_attention"` layer types according to the global-attention interval when no explicit list is supplied. The configuration also normalizes RoPE parameters and supports the older `rope_scaling` input by applying it to both attention layer types [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modular_modernbert.py:52-80](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modular_modernbert.py:97-158]().

### Core Model Components

- **`ModernBertEmbeddings`**: Looks up token embeddings or accepts `inputs_embeds`, then normalizes and applies embedding dropout [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:51-70]().
- **`ModernBertMLP`**: Implements a gated feed-forward block using `Wi`, `ACT2FN`, dropout, and `Wo` [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:73-92]().
- **`ModernBertRotaryEmbedding`**: Initializes per-layer-type RoPE frequency buffers and attention scaling from configuration [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:93-113]().
- **`ModernBertDecoderEmbeddings` / `ModernBertDecoderMLP`**: Provide the decoder-side token embedding and gated MLP blocks [src/transformers/models/modernbert_decoder/modeling_modernbert_decoder.py:48-88]().
- **Decoder causal path**: The decoder module imports causal mask helpers, `Cache`/`DynamicCache`, and `GenerationMixin`; its top-level imports document the dependencies of the causal model implementation [src/transformers/models/modernbert_decoder/modeling_modernbert_decoder.py:21-42]().

**Title: ModernBERT Execution Pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["input_ids_or_inputs_embeds"] --> ModernBertEmbeddings["ModernBertEmbeddings"]
    ModernBertEmbeddings --> EncoderLayers["ModernBertEncoderLayers"]
    EncoderLayers --> Rotary["ModernBertRotaryEmbedding"]
    EncoderLayers --> MLP["ModernBertMLP"]
    EncoderLayers --> Output["BaseModelOutput"]
    Config["ModernBertConfig_layer_types"] --> Rotary
    Config --> EncoderLayers
```

Sources: [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modular_modernbert.py:52-158](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert/modeling_modernbert.py:51-113](), [src/transformers/models/modernbert_decoder/modeling_modernbert_decoder.py:21-88]()

---

## 3. ESM Protein Models

The ESM modeling module includes rotary-position helpers, contact-prediction utilities, and output types for encoder and task-specific results. Its `EsmRotaryEmbedding` computes inverse frequencies from `rope_theta` and the attention head dimension, then produces cosine and sine tensors from position IDs [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:28-40](), [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:105-153]().

`EsmContactPredictionHead` is documented as symmetrizing features, applying average-product correction, and performing logistic regression. The helper functions `symmetrize` and `average_product_correct` implement the corresponding feature transformations [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:88-102](), [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:155-169]().

The module’s `gelu` helper reproduces the original ESM implementation using the error function [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:81-86]().

The ESM tests instantiate `EsmModel` and check `last_hidden_state` and `pooler_output` shapes; they also exercise masked-language-model and token-classification heads [tests/models/esm/test_modeling_esm.py:136-164]().

**Title: ESM Protein Model Architecture**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ProteinTokenIDs["protein_token_input_ids"] --> EsmEncoder["EsmModel"]
    EsmEncoder --> EsmRotaryEmbedding["EsmRotaryEmbedding"]
    EsmEncoder --> HiddenStates["last_hidden_state"]
    HiddenStates --> EsmContactPredictionHead["EsmContactPredictionHead"]
    EsmContactPredictionHead --> ContactOutput["contact_prediction_output"]
    EsmEncoder --> MaskedLM["EsmForMaskedLM"]
    EsmEncoder --> TokenClassification["EsmForTokenClassification"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/models/esm/modeling_esm.py:28-169](), [tests/models/esm/test_modeling_esm.py:136-164]()

---

## 4. Retrieval, Embedding Models & Timm Wrappers

This section focuses on the available `timm` wrapper implementation bridging image backbones into the Transformers library [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:15-28]().

### `timm` Wrapper

`TimmWrapperPreTrainedModel` adapts a `timm` model to the Transformers `PreTrainedModel` interface. It declares `pixel_values` as the primary input, identifies image as its input modality, and uses the `timm_model` base-model prefix. Importing `timm` is conditional on its availability [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:15-28](), [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:81-94]().

`_create_timm_model_with_error_handling` calls `timm.create_model` with the configured architecture and `pretrained=False`. If `timm` raises an “Unknown model” runtime error, the helper raises an `ImportError` explaining that the installed `timm` version may need updating [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:59-78]().

The wrapper’s `load_state_dict` prefixes keys with `timm_model.` when needed. `get_input_embeddings` returns `None` because the wrapped image backbone does not expose token embeddings. The wrapper checks whether gradient checkpointing can be enabled and disabled through the wrapped model’s `set_grad_checkpointing` method [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:107-113](), [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:137-157]().

The output type `TimmWrapperModelOutput` contains `last_hidden_state`, optional pooled output, optional hidden states, and optional attentions; its documentation notes that timm models currently do not support attention outputs [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:33-56]().

| Concern | Code Entity | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Model construction | `_create_timm_model_with_error_handling` | Creates the configured `timm` architecture and handles unknown-model errors [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:59-78](). |
| Transformers integration | `TimmWrapperPreTrainedModel` | Declares image input metadata and the `timm_model` base prefix [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:81-94](). |
| Checkpoint keys | `load_state_dict` | Normalizes state-dict keys to include the wrapper prefix [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:107-113](). |
| Model output | `TimmWrapperModelOutput` | Defines hidden-state, pooled-output, and optional attention fields [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:33-56](). |

Sources: [src/transformers/models/timm_wrapper/modeling_timm_wrapper.py:15-157]()

# Page: Vision Backbones & Object Detection

# Vision Backbones & Object Detection

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This section surveys vision backbones and vision-language encoders alongside object-detection and segmentation architectures. It focuses on implementation details visible in the supplied model files: image patch embeddings and position embeddings, contrastive-model outputs and losses, multiscale detection outputs, and code entities for detection and grounding. The broader family names in scope include ViT, DINOv2/v3, CLIP, SigLIP, DETR variants, Mask2Former, SAM, Grounding DINO, and OWL-ViT. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:45-65](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155](), [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-109](), [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:46-69](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:39-73](), [src/transformers/models/owlvit/modeling_owlvit.py:65-100]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:45-65](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155](), [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-109](), [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:46-69](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:39-73](), [src/transformers/models/owlvit/modeling_owlvit.py:65-100]()

---

## 1. Vision Transformer Backbones & Timm Wrappers

The supplied CLIP and SigLIP vision embedding implementations convert image tensors into patch tokens with `nn.Conv2d` layers whose kernel and stride are configured by `patch_size`. Both define learned position embeddings and an `interpolate_pos_encoding` method for handling image resolutions that differ from the configured size. Their embedding details differ: CLIP includes a learned class embedding and reserves a position for it, while the shown SigLIP embedding class defines patch positions without a class embedding. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-165](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-165](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155]()

### 1.1 Core Embedding Components

| Component | Implementation detail |
|---|---|
| Patch projection | `CLIPVisionEmbeddings.patch_embedding` and `SiglipVisionEmbeddings.patch_embedding` are `nn.Conv2d` layers configured with `patch_size` as the kernel size and stride. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-159](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-135]() |
| CLIP class token | `CLIPVisionEmbeddings` defines a learned `class_embedding`; its position count is `num_patches + 1`. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-159]() |
| SigLIP position count | `SiglipVisionEmbeddings` sets `num_positions` to the patch count and stores learned position embeddings and non-persistent `position_ids`. [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-135]() |
| Resolution handling | Both classes define `interpolate_pos_encoding`; the shown SigLIP method documents interpolation of pretrained positions for higher-resolution images and special handling for tracing. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:161-165](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:137-155]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-165](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155]()

### 1.2 CLIP and SigLIP Outputs

CLIP and SigLIP expose model outputs for vision, text, and combined image-text results. The combined output dataclasses include optional image and text embeddings, similarity logits in both image-to-text and text-to-image orientations, and the outputs of their vision and text models. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:68-135](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:43-114]()

In CLIP, `contrastive_loss` applies cross-entropy to logits against the diagonal batch indices. `image_text_contrastive_loss` computes that loss in both matrix orientations and averages the two. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:45-55]() The supplied SigLIP excerpt defines the output types, but does not show its loss implementation. [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:80-114]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:45-55](), [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:68-135](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:43-114]()

### 1.3 Backbone utilities and other model families

The supplied detection model files import `load_backbone` from `backbone_utils`; the excerpts do not show that utility’s implementation, so its loading behavior is not described here. [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:31-38](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:25-33](), [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:24-33](), [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:29-47](), [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:30-41]()

The provided excerpts do not include implementation details for ViT, DINOv2/v3, or timm wrappers. They are therefore identified as in-scope families, but not characterized further here. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-165](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:31-38](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:25-33](), [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:24-33](), [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:29-47](), [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:30-41](), [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:138-165](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:116-155]()

---

## 2. Object Detection & Segmentation Models

The supplied detection and segmentation implementations expose structured outputs for decoder hidden states, reference points, classes, boxes, or masks. Deformable DETR, RT-DETR, and D-FINE output declarations include intermediate decoder activations and reference-point-related data; Mask2Former exposes pixel-decoder features and mask-query logits. [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-109](), [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:50-85](), [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:44-79](), [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:46-101]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-109](), [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:50-85](), [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:44-79](), [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:46-101]()

### 2.1 DETR Family & Real-Time Detectors

`DeformableDetrDecoderOutput` adds intermediate decoder hidden states and intermediate reference points to the decoder output structure. `DeformableDetrModelOutput` includes initial reference points, decoder output states, encoder states, and optional two-stage encoder class and box-coordinate outputs. The object-detection output documents class logits, normalized predicted boxes, and a loss combining classification and box terms when labels are supplied. [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-109](), [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:111-131]()

The Deformable DETR file imports `load_backbone` and exposes `MultiScaleDeformableAttention`-related model outputs in the supplied excerpt. The Grounding DINO implementation provides a concrete `MultiScaleDeformableAttention` module that splits values by spatial level, samples locations with `grid_sample`, weights the sampled values, and returns the combined output. [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:31-38](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:76-129]()

RT-DETR and D-FINE declare decoder outputs containing intermediate hidden states, logits, reference points, and predicted box corners. The excerpts establish those output fields, but do not show enough of their forward implementations to describe the full decoding or loss flows. [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:50-85](), [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:44-79]()

| Family | Visible output entities |
|---|---|
| Deformable DETR | `DeformableDetrDecoderOutput`, `DeformableDetrModelOutput`, `DeformableDetrObjectDetectionOutput`. [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-131]() |
| RT-DETR | `RTDetrDecoderOutput`, including intermediate logits, reference points, and predicted corners. [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:50-85]() |
| D-FINE | `DFineDecoderOutput` and the auxiliary `DFineMLP` and `DFineGate` classes. [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:44-109]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:31-38](), [src/transformers/models/deformable_detr/modeling_deformable_detr.py:51-131](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:76-129](), [src/transformers/models/rt_detr/modeling_rt_detr.py:50-85](), [src/transformers/models/d_fine/modeling_d_fine.py:44-109]()

### 2.2 Mask2Former

Mask2Former’s output declarations separate pixel-level features from query-decoder outputs. `Mask2FormerPixelDecoderOutput` contains `multi_scale_features`, described as features at 1/8, 1/16, and 1/32 scales, and `mask_features`, described as 1/4 scale features. `Mask2FormerMaskedAttentionDecoderOutput` contains `masks_queries_logits` and intermediate decoder hidden states. [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:46-101]()

`Mask2FormerPixelLevelModuleOutput` distinguishes encoder feature maps from decoder feature maps and labels `decoder_last_hidden_state` as per-pixel embeddings. The supplied excerpt also describes the default encoder as a Swin backbone and the pixel decoder as multiscale deformable attention-based. [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:104-134]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py:46-134]()

### 2.3 SAM family

SAM, SAM2, SAM3, and related family files are listed as present in the repository, but their contents are not included in the supplied excerpts. This section therefore does not infer their class structure or processing flow. [src/transformers/models/sam/modeling_sam.py:1-1](), [src/transformers/models/sam2/modeling_sam2.py:1-1](), [src/transformers/models/sam3/modeling_sam3.py:1-1]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/sam/modeling_sam.py:1-1](), [src/transformers/models/sam2/modeling_sam2.py:1-1](), [src/transformers/models/sam3/modeling_sam3.py:1-1]()

## 3. Grounding DINO, OWL-ViT, & OWLv2

Grounding DINO defines `encode_sinusoidal_position_embedding` for normalized coordinates and a `MultiScaleDeformableAttention` module. Its decoder output structure includes intermediate hidden states and reference points. [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:39-73](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:76-129](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:132-153]()

OWL-ViT and OWLv2 define image-text output structures and object-detection output structures. The OWLv2 object-detection output documents logits, objectness logits, normalized box predictions, text embeddings, image embeddings, and patch class embeddings. [src/transformers/models/owlvit/modeling_owlvit.py:65-100](), [src/transformers/models/owlv2/modeling_owlv2.py:98-146]() OWL-ViT’s supplied excerpt also includes box-area, IoU, and generalized-IoU helper functions. [src/transformers/models/owlvit/modeling_owlvit.py:103-168]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:39-73](), [src/transformers/models/grounding_dino/modeling_grounding_dino.py:76-153](), [src/transformers/models/owlvit/modeling_owlvit.py:65-100](), [src/transformers/models/owlvit/modeling_owlvit.py:103-168](), [src/transformers/models/owlv2/modeling_owlv2.py:98-146]()

---

## 4. Vision-Language Contrastive Models & Loss Functions

CLIP’s `contrastive_loss` applies cross-entropy to a similarity-logit matrix using the batch’s diagonal indices as targets. `image_text_contrastive_loss` evaluates the matrix and its transpose, then averages the two losses. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:45-55]() CLIP and SigLIP output dataclasses expose image and text embeddings, image-to-text and text-to-image logits, and the paired vision and text model outputs. [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:104-135](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:80-114]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:45-55](), [src/transformers/models/clip/modeling_clip.py:104-135](), [src/transformers/models/siglip/modeling_siglip.py:80-114]()

# Page: Vision-Language Models

# Vision-Language Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page describes how vision-language models (VLMs) in Transformers connect image inputs to language-model representations. It focuses on shared implementation patterns visible in the provided code: vision towers, projectors, placeholder-token alignment, patch handling, and positional encoding. Model families named in the section scope include LLaVA, PaliGemma, BLIP/BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Idefics2/3, SmolVLM, InternVL, Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL, GLM-4V, Janus, and Gemma3; the implementation detail below is limited to the supplied source excerpts. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-160](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-165](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160](), [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-160](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-165](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160](), [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

---

## Core Architecture of Vision-Language Models in Transformers

### General High-Level Structure

A common composite-model layout is a vision encoder, a transformation that adapts vision features to the language model’s representation size, and a language model. In LLaVA, `LlavaModel` creates a vision tower and language model through `AutoModel.from_config`, with `LlavaMultiModalProjector` between them. PaliGemma follows a similar layout with `PaliGemmaMultiModalProjector`. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-137](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-134]()

The exact image-to-token path differs between model families. LLaVA selects vision features and projects them; PaliGemma projects the vision tower’s last hidden state and checks placeholder-token counts; Qwen2-VL uses spatial and temporal position information in its rotary embedding path. These are related patterns, not one uniform fusion implementation. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:139-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:139-165](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-165](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160]()

### Multimodal Input and Feature Fusion Pipeline

Title: Image and text paths into composite model components
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input"
        Image["pixel_values"]
        Text["input_ids"]
    end
    subgraph "LLaVA"
        Vision["LlavaModel.vision_tower"]
        Projector["LlavaMultiModalProjector"]
        Language["LlavaModel.language_model"]
    end
    subgraph "PaliGemma"
        PaliVision["PaliGemmaModel.vision_tower"]
        PaliProjector["PaliGemmaMultiModalProjector"]
        PaliLanguage["PaliGemmaModel.language_model"]
    end
    Image --> Vision --> Projector
    Text --> Language
    Projector --> Language
    Image --> PaliVision --> PaliProjector
    Text --> PaliLanguage
    PaliProjector --> PaliLanguage
```

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-137](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-134]()

---

## Key Components Detailed

### 1. Vision Tower and Patch Embedding

A composite model’s vision tower receives image tensors and returns hidden states used by later fusion components. LLaVA’s `get_image_features` requests hidden states from `vision_tower`; PaliGemma’s `get_image_features` reads `image_outputs.last_hidden_state`. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:139-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:135-147]()

Idefics2 defines `Idefics2VisionEmbeddings`, which applies a convolutional patch embedding, flattens the patch grid into a sequence, and uses `patch_attention_mask` to derive per-image patch counts for positional handling. Its class documentation describes the variable-resolution adaptation. [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

The Qwen2.5-VL modular source defines `Qwen2_5_VisionPatchEmbed` as a subclass of `PatchEmbed`; its generated modeling file defines `Qwen2_5_VisionPatchEmbed` using a 3D convolution whose kernel and stride include temporal and spatial patch sizes. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:125-126](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:139-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:135-147](), [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:125-126](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

### 2. Projectors: Aligning Vision Features to Language Space

Projectors adapt vision features before they are used alongside language-model representations:

| Component | Implementation shown |
|---|---|
| `LlavaMultiModalProjector` | Computes its input size from the configured vision feature layer selection, then applies `linear_1`, the configured activation, and `linear_2`. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-106]() |
| `PaliGemmaMultiModalProjector` | Applies one biased linear layer from vision hidden size to vision projection dimension. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-99]() |
| `Qwen2_5_VLPatchMerger` | Extends `PatchMerger` and sets `ln_q` to `Qwen2_5_VLRMSNorm`. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156]() |

In LLaVA, `get_image_features` obtains vision outputs and selects the configured vision features before projection; the projector itself performs the two linear transformations. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-106](), [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:139-161]()

In PaliGemma, `get_image_features` passes the vision tower’s last hidden state through `multi_modal_projector` and stores the projected result in `pooler_output`. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-99](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:139-147]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-106](), [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:139-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-99](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:139-147](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156]()

### 3. Cross-Modal Fusion and Placeholder Alignment

Image-token integration depends on the model’s input convention. PaliGemma’s `get_placeholder_mask` locates the configured image token in `input_ids`, or identifies it through the input embedding when `input_ids` is absent. It compares the number of image-token positions with the number of image features and documents an error for mismatched lengths. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:149-165]()

The LLaVA test fixture illustrates a corresponding input convention: it constructs `input_ids`, sets the initial image-token positions to `image_token_index`, and supplies `pixel_values` and `attention_mask` together. The fixture’s sequence length includes the configured image-token count. [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:53-64](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:118-164]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:149-165](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:53-64](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:118-164]()

---

## Rotary Embeddings and Positional Encoding for Vision Tokens

Qwen2-VL’s `Qwen2VLRotaryEmbedding` expands position IDs to three coordinate streams and computes cosine and sine frequencies from those IDs. The implementation comments identify the streams as grid-aware position IDs; `recomposition_frequencies` arranges frequencies into the spatial layout. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160]()

The Qwen2.5-VL vision configuration specifies axial RoPE, and `Qwen2_5_VLVisionRotaryEmbedding` computes axial frequency parameters from the vision configuration. The corresponding generated vision patch embedder handles temporal and spatial patch dimensions. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:63-96](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:63-96](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

---

## Model Families and Their Vision-Language Architectures

### LLaVA Family

`LlavaModel` instantiates `vision_tower`, `multi_modal_projector`, and `language_model`. `LlavaMultiModalProjector` uses a two-linear-layer MLP with a configurable activation. `get_image_features` requests vision hidden states and accepts feature-layer selection, feature-selection strategy, and optional image sizes. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-106](), [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:130-161]()

The supplied test fixture uses `image_token_index` and `image_seq_length` in `LlavaConfig`, constructs image-token positions in `input_ids`, and tests both `LlavaModel` and `LlavaForConditionalGeneration`. [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:53-64](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:125-164](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:167-192]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-161](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:53-64](), [tests/models/llava/test_modeling_llava.py:125-192]()

### PaliGemma

`PaliGemmaModel` constructs a vision tower and language model using `AutoModel.from_config`, with `PaliGemmaMultiModalProjector` between them. `get_image_features` projects the vision tower’s last hidden state. The model’s placeholder-mask logic checks image-token positions against image-feature count. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-99](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:122-165]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-99](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:122-165]()

### Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL

The supplied Qwen2-VL source defines `Qwen2VLRotaryEmbedding`, which computes three-coordinate position frequencies and recomposes them for the spatial layout. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-164]()

For Qwen2.5-VL, the modular source defines `Qwen2_5_VLPatchMerger` as an extension of `PatchMerger`, and the generated modeling source defines temporal-spatial 3D convolution in `Qwen2_5_VisionPatchEmbed`. Its vision configuration includes `spatial_merge_size` and `temporal_patch_size`. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:63-96](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-164](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:63-96](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

### Idefics2 and Idefics3

The supplied Idefics2 implementation defines `Idefics2VisionEmbeddings` with convolutional patch embedding, flattened patch sequences, and position embeddings. Its forward signature includes a `patch_attention_mask`; the implementation uses that mask to derive the number of patches along each image dimension. The provided excerpt does not include the Perceiver or Idefics3 implementation details. [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

---

```mermaid
    Text["Text input"] --> InputIds["input_ids"]
    PixelValues --> LlavaTower["LlavaModel.vision_tower"]

    InputIds --> LlavaLanguage["LlavaModel.language_model"]

```

## Image Token Expansion and Patch Merging in Qwen Models

The Qwen2.5-VL vision patch embedder converts input into patch features using a 3D convolution whose kernel and stride cover temporal and spatial patch dimensions. The configuration exposes `temporal_patch_size` and `spatial_merge_size`; `Qwen2_5_VLPatchMerger` extends the shared `PatchMerger` and installs an RMSNorm layer. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:63-96](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156]()

The available excerpts establish the patch embedding, configuration fields, and merger class, but do not show the complete forward path that connects those components to language-model token insertion. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:125-156](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:63-96](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:125-156]()

### Diagram: Qwen2.5-VL Patch Embedding and Vision Components

Title: Qwen2.5-VL patch embedding and vision components
```mermaid
graph LR
    VideoOrImage["Image or video tensor"] --> PatchEmbed["Qwen2_5_VisionPatchEmbed"]
    PatchEmbed --> VisionBlocks["Qwen2_5_VLVisionBlock"]
    VisionBlocks --> PatchMerger["Qwen2_5_VLPatchMerger"]
    PositionIds["get_vision_position_ids"] --> VisionRoPE["Qwen2_5_VLVisionRotaryEmbedding"]
    VisionBlocks --> VisionRoPE
```

---

## Advanced Vision Encoder Features: Idefics2

`Idefics2VisionEmbeddings` is documented as a modified SigLIP-style embedding implementation designed to support variable-resolution images. Its patch embedding uses a convolution, while the forward method uses `patch_attention_mask` to determine valid patch counts and construct position IDs. [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

The provided excerpt does not show the complete Idefics2 vision-model or Perceiver path, so this page does not infer how those components are connected in the full forward pass. [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()

---

## Omni-Modal Extensions

The supplied Qwen2.5-Omni modular source identifies the model as handling audio, image, and video. It includes `chunk_and_pad_features`, which splits audio features into fixed-size chunks and pads them to a uniform length. These audio utilities describe an omni-modal extension rather than the image-only fusion path covered above. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modular_qwen2_5_omni.py:15-15](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modular_qwen2_5_omni.py:84-116]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modular_qwen2_5_omni.py:15-15](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modular_qwen2_5_omni.py:84-116]()

---

## Summary

The supplied implementations show several distinct mechanisms for preparing visual features for language-model use:

- LLaVA builds a vision-tower/projector/language-model composite and uses a configurable two-layer projector. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-137]()
- PaliGemma projects the vision tower’s last hidden state and validates image-placeholder alignment in `get_placeholder_mask`. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-99](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:149-165]()
- Idefics2’s vision embeddings handle variable-resolution patch grids using a patch attention mask. [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149]()
- Qwen2-VL uses three-coordinate rotary position IDs; Qwen2.5-VL exposes temporal-spatial patch embedding and a patch merger in its supplied sources. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156]()

These examples share the broad goal of making visual features usable in language-model computation, but their token alignment, feature selection, patch processing, and positional schemes are architecture-specific. [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:139-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:139-165](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:87-161](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/modeling_paligemma.py:91-165](), [src/transformers/models/idefics2/modeling_idefics2.py:100-149](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/modeling_qwen2_vl.py:111-160](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py:94-117](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py:152-156]()

---

# Page: Audio & Speech Models

# Audio & Speech Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page surveys audio and speech model families in Transformers, focusing on the implementation details available here: Whisper and Wav2Vec2 modeling, the automatic speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-audio pipelines, and the pipeline task registry. The broader model-family names covered by this page include HuBERT, WavLM, SeamlessM4T, Parakeet, Voxtral, SpeechT5, Bark, VITS, EnCodec, DAC, Mimi, NeuCodec, and XCodec2; implementation details for those models are included only where supported by the cited source excerpts.

Sources: [src/transformers/models/whisper/modeling_whisper.py:14-48](), [src/transformers/models/wav2vec2/modeling_wav2vec2.py:14-56](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:134-157]()

---

## 1. Audio processing fundamentals

Audio inference commonly starts with a waveform and passes through input normalization, optional chunking, feature extraction, model inference, and task-specific decoding. Pipeline batching also needs to distinguish sequence-valued audio inputs from other tensor inputs: `pad_collate_fn` uses the feature extractor’s padding settings for keys such as `input_values` and `input_features`, while `_pad` handles tensor concatenation or padding. [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:41-119](), [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:88-123](), [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:126-180]()

### Audio loading, mono conversion, and chunking

`_to_mono` accepts a one-dimensional waveform unchanged. For a two-dimensional input it interprets axis 0 as channels and averages the channels. Other ranks are rejected, and inputs with more than two channels are rejected rather than implicitly downmixed. [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:41-72]()

`chunk_iter` divides a waveform into overlapping chunks. Its step is the chunk length minus the left and right strides; each chunk is sent to the feature extractor with its sampling rate, PyTorch tensor output, and an attention mask. The yielded record includes the processed features, a `stride` tuple, and an `is_last` flag. [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:95-119]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:41-119]()

### Feature batching and padding

`pad_collate_fn` determines padding values and sides from the tokenizer and feature extractor. It applies feature-extractor padding values to `input_values`, `pixel_values`, and `input_features`, and uses attention-mask padding values of zero. `_pad` concatenates one-dimensional tensors directly and has a separate path for four-dimensional `input_features`, which it treats as likely batched mel-spectrogram data. [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:88-123](), [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:126-180]()

| Pipeline input or intermediate | Handling visible in the supplied implementation |
|---|---|
| One-dimensional waveform | Passed through unchanged by `_to_mono`. [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:41-52]() |
| Two-dimensional waveform | Interpreted as `(channels, samples)` and averaged across channels. [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:54-72]() |
| Chunked waveform | Feature-extracted per chunk; each yielded item includes stride metadata and a final-chunk flag. [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:95-119]() |
| `input_values`, `input_features` | Batched using feature-extractor padding settings; four-dimensional `input_features` are concatenated by `_pad`. [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:88-123](), [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:142-180]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:88-123](), [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:126-180]()

---

## 2. Automatic speech recognition

Transformers exposes ASR through `AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline`. The task registry associates `"automatic-speech-recognition"` with this pipeline and lists `AutoModelForCTC`, `AutoModelForTDT`, and `AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq` as its PyTorch model routes. The registry’s default model is Wav2Vec2-based. [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:147-151]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:147-151]()

### CTC-family models: Wav2Vec2, HuBERT, and WavLM

The supplied Wav2Vec2 implementation defines output structures for pretraining, including projected states, projected quantized states, codevector perplexity, and optional contrastive and diversity losses. It also imports the bidirectional attention-mask utility and defines `_compute_mask_indices` for SpecAugment-style span masking. [src/transformers/models/wav2vec2/modeling_wav2vec2.py:27-56](), [src/transformers/models/wav2vec2/modeling_wav2vec2.py:69-110]()

The CTC route is represented in the ASR task registry by `AutoModelForCTC`; the visible test setup imports `Wav2Vec2ForCTC` and includes CTC model mappings in its pipeline model set. The supplied excerpts do not show the full Wav2Vec2 forward pass or the HuBERT and WavLM implementations, so they do not establish detailed layer-by-layer behavior for those models. [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:147-151](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:23-38](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:63-68]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/wav2vec2/modeling_wav2vec2.py:27-110](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:23-68]()

### Whisper and sequence-to-sequence ASR

Whisper’s modeling module defines `sinusoids`, `shift_tokens_right`, and `_compute_mask_indices`, and imports its configuration and `WhisperGenerationMixin`. The module also uses encoder-decoder cache types, causal-mask utilities, and model output structures, including `Seq2SeqLMOutput`. [src/transformers/models/whisper/modeling_whisper.py:27-48](), [src/transformers/models/whisper/modeling_whisper.py:56-82]()

Whisper-specific generation support is implemented in `generation_whisper.py`. The visible excerpt defines `_median_filter`, `_dynamic_time_warping`, and `_pad_to_max_length`; the latter handles generated segments, padding, and optional token timestamps. The module imports `WhisperTimeStampLogitsProcessor` and `WhisperNoSpeechDetection`, among other generation components. [src/transformers/models/whisper/generation_whisper.py:24-40](), [src/transformers/models/whisper/generation_whisper.py:43-61](), [src/transformers/models/whisper/generation_whisper.py:64-115](), [src/transformers/models/whisper/generation_whisper.py:126-181]()

The ASR test suite exercises timestamp output for CTC models and Whisper, and checks that non-CTC models other than Whisper reject timestamp requests in the tested cases. [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:124-165]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/whisper/modeling_whisper.py:27-82](), [src/transformers/models/whisper/generation_whisper.py:24-181](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:124-165]()

### ASR pipeline data flow

**Diagram: ASR input and task routing**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Audio["Raw waveform or audio input"] --> Mono["_to_mono"]
    Mono --> Chunks["chunk_iter"]
    Chunks --> Extractor["feature_extractor"]
    Extractor --> Registry["SUPPORTED_TASKS: automatic-speech-recognition"]
    Registry --> CTC["AutoModelForCTC"]
    Registry --> TDT["AutoModelForTDT"]
    Registry --> Seq2Seq["AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq"]
    CTC --> Pipeline["AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline"]
    TDT --> Pipeline
    Seq2Seq --> Pipeline
    Pipeline --> Text["Transcription text or timestamped chunks"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:41-119](), [src/transformers/pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py:146-166](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:147-151](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:124-165]()

### Related ASR model families

The requested architecture scope also includes HuBERT, WavLM, SeamlessM4T, Parakeet, and Voxtral. The supplied file listing names modeling files for HuBERT, WavLM, and SeamlessM4T, and the ASR tests import Parakeet configuration and model classes. However, the contents of those model files are not included in the excerpts, so their internal architectures and call flows cannot be described here with line-level evidence. [src/transformers/models/hubert/modeling_hubert.py](), [src/transformers/models/wavlm/modeling_wavlm.py](), [src/transformers/models/seamless_m4t/modeling_seamless_m4t.py](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:23-38](), [src/transformers/models/voxtral/modeling_voxtral.py]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/hubert/modeling_hubert.py](), [src/transformers/models/wavlm/modeling_wavlm.py](), [src/transformers/models/seamless_m4t/modeling_seamless_m4t.py](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:23-38](), [src/transformers/models/voxtral/modeling_voxtral.py]()

## 3. Text-to-speech and neural audio generation

The pipeline registry exposes `"text-to-audio"` through `TextToAudioPipeline`, with `AutoModelForTextToWaveform` and `AutoModelForTextToSpectrogram` as PyTorch routes. The task alias `"text-to-speech"` resolves to `"text-to-audio"`. [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:134-157]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:134-157]()

### Text-to-audio pipeline

`TextToAudioPipeline` accepts text and generates audio from a waveform or spectrogram model. It can load a processor and tokenizer, and it identifies models that pass generation parameters to submodels, including Bark and SeamlessM4T variants. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:46-53](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:99-120]()

When the model is registered as a text-to-spectrogram model, the pipeline loads a `SpeechT5HifiGan` vocoder by default if one was not provided. It derives the output sampling rate from the vocoder, model configuration, generation configuration, codec configuration, or processor feature extractor. For `musicgen` and `speecht5`, the pipeline sets `processor` to `None` because those models use their tokenizer instead. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:122-157]()

The model-specific preprocessing path shown in the excerpt handles Bark by setting a maximum input length and calling the Bark processor path without adding special tokens. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:159-172]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:46-172]()

### SpeechT5, Bark, and VITS

The supplied text-to-audio excerpt directly establishes the pipeline’s SpeechT5 vocoder behavior and its special handling for Bark and SpeechT5 model types. It does not include the model implementation files for SpeechT5 or Bark, nor does it include the VITS implementation, so this page does not infer their internal synthesis architectures from filenames alone. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:108-157](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:159-172]()

**Diagram: Text-to-audio pipeline routing**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Text["Input text"] --> AudioTask["text-to-audio or text-to-speech"]
    AudioTask --> Pipeline["TextToAudioPipeline"]
    Pipeline --> Preprocess["preprocess"]
    Preprocess --> Model["AutoModelForTextToWaveform or AutoModelForTextToSpectrogram"]
    Model --> Waveform["Generated audio waveform"]
    Model --> Spectrogram["Generated spectrogram"]
    Spectrogram --> Vocoder["SpeechT5HifiGan"]
    Vocoder --> Waveform
    Waveform --> Output["AudioOutput: audio and sampling_rate"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:134-157](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:31-44](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:46-53](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:108-157]()

### TTS model coverage

| Family | Evidence present in the supplied excerpts |
|---|---|
| SpeechT5 | `TextToAudioPipeline` imports and loads `SpeechT5HifiGan` for text-to-spectrogram models, and has a `speecht5` model-type branch. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:122-157]() |
| Bark | The pipeline has Bark-specific generation-parameter behavior and a Bark-specific preprocessing branch. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:108-120](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:159-172]() |
| VITS | The supplied excerpts do not include VITS implementation details. [src/transformers/models/vits/modeling_vits.py]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:108-172](), [src/transformers/models/vits/modeling_vits.py]()

---

## 4. Neural codecs and audio representations

The requested codec family includes EnCodec, DAC, Mimi, NeuCodec, and XCodec2. The supplied excerpts do not show their model implementations, so this page does not describe their codec layers, quantization schemes, or streaming interfaces. The visible text-to-audio pipeline code does show that sampling-rate discovery can consult a model’s `codec_config`. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:138-157]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:138-157](), [src/transformers/models/encodec/modeling_encodec.py](), [src/transformers/models/dac/modeling_dac.py](), [src/transformers/models/xcodec/modeling_xcodec.py]()

```mermaid
    DAC --> TextAudioPipeline
    Mimi --> TextAudioPipeline
    NeuCodec --> TextAudioPipeline
    XCodec2 --> TextAudioPipeline
    TextAudioPipeline --> TextWaveformFactory
    TextAudioPipeline --> TextSpectrogramFactory
```

Sources: [src/transformers/models/whisper/modeling_whisper.py:42-48](), [src/transformers/models/wav2vec2/modeling_wav2vec2.py:14-56](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:147-157](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_to_audio.py:122-157](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:23-38]()

---

## 5. Pipeline integration and tests

The pipeline registry registers audio classification, ASR, text-to-audio, and zero-shot audio classification implementations. The ASR registry maps to `AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline`; the text-to-audio registry maps to `TextToAudioPipeline`. [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:47-63](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:140-157]()

The ASR test suite checks raw-waveform inputs, strided inputs, and timestamp-returning outputs. It distinguishes CTC timestamp requests from Whisper timestamp requests and expects an error for unsupported non-CTC timestamp cases covered by the test. [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:99-165]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:47-63](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:140-157](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py:99-165]()

# Page: Multimodal Omni & Specialized Models

# Multimodal Omni & Specialized Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page describes selected multimodal and specialized model implementations in `transformers`, focusing on code paths visible across various specialized model directories: Qwen2.5 Omni input processing, MusicGen and MusicGen-Melody, RAG outputs, Qwen2-Audio outputs and attention mechanisms, and DiffusionGemma rotary embeddings. It connects model-facing concepts to named code entities and summarizes what the corresponding test suites exercise.  
Sources: `src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/processing_qwen2_5_omni.py:31-155](), `src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:30-58](), `src/transformers/models/musicgen_melody/modeling_musicgen_melody.py:29-51](), `src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:22-30](), `src/transformers/models/qwen2_audio/modeling_qwen2_audio.py:23-35](), `src/transformers/models/diffusion_gemma/modeling_diffusion_gemma.py:21-60]()

---

## 1. Unified Multimodal Omni Models (Qwen2.5/3-Omni & MoE Variants)

`Qwen2_5OmniProcessor` is a `ProcessorMixin` implementation whose call interface accepts text and optional images, videos, and audio. Its kwargs define modality-specific settings, including video frame and patch limits, video/audio timing controls, and audio sampling and padding defaults. When audio is supplied, the processor invokes the feature extractor and renames its attention mask to `feature_attention_mask` before further processing. The visible implementation requires text input, even when other modalities are supplied. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/processing_qwen2_5_omni.py:31-155]()

The video kwargs include `use_audio_in_video`, `seconds_per_chunk`, and `position_id_per_seconds`; the processor extracts these values from its merged kwargs before processing modalities. The supplied code establishes the processor’s input contract and initial audio handling. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/processing_qwen2_5_omni.py:31-65](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/processing_qwen2_5_omni.py:104-155]()

### Diagram: Qwen2.5 Omni Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserInput["TextInput_Optional_Image_Video_Audio"] --> QwenProcessor["Qwen2_5OmniProcessor.__call__"]
    QwenProcessor --> MergeKwargs["_merge_kwargs"]
    MergeKwargs --> AudioBranch["feature_extractor_audio_kwargs"]
    AudioBranch --> FeatureMask["feature_attention_mask"]
    MergeKwargs --> VideoSettings["seconds_per_chunk_position_id_per_seconds_use_audio_in_video"]
    MergeKwargs --> TextRequirement["text_required"]
    QwenProcessor --> BatchFeature["BatchFeature"]
```

Sources: `src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/processing_qwen2_5_omni.py:31-65](), `src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/processing_qwen2_5_omni.py:79-155]()

---

## 2. MusicGen & MusicGen-Melody: Audio Generation

The MusicGen modeling module imports generation components such as `GenerationMixin`, `GenerationConfig`, and `ClassifierFreeGuidanceLogitsProcessor`, alongside cache and attention utilities. The codebase defines `MusicgenUnconditionalInput`, a `ModelOutput` dataclass carrying optional encoder outputs, an attention mask, and a guidance scale. [src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:30-83]()

`shift_tokens_right` transposes codebook-oriented token IDs, shifts them by one position, inserts the configured decoder start token, and replaces shifted `-100` values with the padding token. It raises an error when either required token ID is absent. [src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:86-103]()

`MusicgenSinusoidalPositionalEmbedding` constructs sinusoidal position vectors and expands its non-persistent buffer when the requested sequence length exceeds the current table. Its `forward` method accounts for `past_key_values_length` when generating position indices. [src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:106-147]()

MusicGen-Melody has corresponding decoder-side utilities. `MusicgenMelodyOutputWithPast` includes optional logits, cache, hidden states, attentions, and `encoder_hidden_states`; its documentation describes those encoder states as the conditional signal formed from projected text and audio encoder outputs. Its `shift_tokens_right` follows the same codebook-axis shift and token-ID validation pattern. [src/transformers/models/musicgen_melody/modeling_musicgen_melody.py:60-108]()

The test suite constructs decoder inputs with a batch dimension expanded by `num_codebooks`; it also prepares encoder hidden states and derives masks from padding IDs when needed. [tests/models/musicgen/test_modeling_musicgen.py:76-93](), [tests/models/musicgen/test_modeling_musicgen.py:96-161]()

### Diagram: MusicGen Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping

```mermaid
graph LR
    Prompt["Text_or_conditional_input"] --> ModelOutputInput["MusicgenUnconditionalInput"]
    ModelOutputInput --> EncoderStates["encoder_outputs"]
    ModelOutputInput --> GuidanceScale["guidance_scale"]
    CodebookIDs["input_ids_with_codebook_axis"] --> ShiftTokens["shift_tokens_right"]
    ShiftTokens --> DecoderStart["decoder_start_token_id_and_pad_token_id"]
    DecoderPositions["input_ids_and_past_key_values_length"] --> PositionalEmbedding["MusicgenSinusoidalPositionalEmbedding.forward"]
    GenerationImports["GenerationMixin_and_CFG_LogitsProcessor"] --> MusicgenModeling["modeling_musicgen.py"]
```

Sources: `src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:30-38](), `src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:67-103](), `src/transformers/models/musicgen/modeling_musicgen.py:106-147]()

---

## 3. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

`modeling_rag.py` imports `RagRetriever` and defines `RetrievAugLMMarginOutput`, a `ModelOutput` dataclass for retrieval-augmented marginalized model outputs. Its documented fields include logits and loss, document scores, retrieved document embeddings and IDs, context input IDs and masks, and question-encoder and generator states. The output contract identifies document scores as scores between retrieved document embeddings and the question encoder’s last hidden state. [src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:22-30](), [src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:36-109]()

This output structure and retriever dependency integrates directly into the RAG generation loop. [src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:22-30](), [src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:36-109]()

### Diagram: RAG Output Data Contract

```mermaid
graph TD
    Retriever["RagRetriever"] --> RetrievedIDs["retrieved_doc_ids"]
    Retriever --> RetrievedEmbeddings["retrieved_doc_embeds"]
    Retriever --> ContextIDs["context_input_ids"]
    Retriever --> ContextMask["context_attention_mask"]
    QuestionEncoder["question_encoder_last_hidden_state"] --> DocScores["doc_scores"]
    RetrievedEmbeddings --> DocScores
    DocScores --> MarginalOutput["RetrievAugLMMarginOutput"]
    ContextIDs --> MarginalOutput
    ContextMask --> MarginalOutput
    MarginalOutput --> Logits["logits_marginalized_over_documents"]
```

Sources: `src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:22-30](), `src/transformers/models/rag/modeling_rag.py:36-68]()

---

## 4. Hybrid, Recurrent & Specialized Architectures

### Qwen2-Audio

`Qwen2AudioModelOutputWithPast` extends `BaseModelOutputWithPast` with optional attention-mask and label fields; its documentation notes these may be updated by audio-merging logic. `Qwen2AudioCausalLMOutputWithPast` carries loss, logits, cache, hidden states, attentions, and an attention mask. The cache is represented by the shared `Cache` interface. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_audio/modeling_qwen2_audio.py:23-35](), [src/transformers/models/qwen2_audio/modeling_qwen2_audio.py:41-96]()

`Qwen2AudioAttention` stores attention dimensions and decoder/causal settings. The module’s `eager_attention_forward` computes scaled query-key scores, adds an optional mask, applies softmax and dropout, and multiplies by values. [src/transformers/models/qwen2_audio/modeling_qwen2_audio.py:98-163]()

### DiffusionGemma

The DiffusionGemma implementation defines `DiffusionGemmaTextRotaryEmbedding`. During initialization it resolves rotary parameters per layer type, chooses either a configured rotary initializer or the default implementation, and stores per-type inverse-frequency buffers and attention-scaling values. Its forward method forms cosine and sine embeddings from position IDs and the selected layer type. [src/transformers/models/diffusion_gemma/modeling_diffusion_gemma.py:63-134]()

The DiffusionGemma test configuration covers both `sliding_attention` and `full_attention` layer types, a vision configuration, image-token identifiers, and a block-diffusion model class. [tests/models/diffusion_gemma/test_modeling_diffusion_gemma.py:39-59](), [tests/models/diffusion_gemma/test_modeling_diffusion_gemma.py:59-145]()

### Other families and scope notes

The codebase also includes Qwen3.5 text-model test classes and configurations alternating `full_attention` and `linear_attention` layer types, including convolution and recurrent-state shape helpers. [tests/models/qwen3_5/test_modeling_qwen3_5.py:63-107]()

Recurrent Gemma, Kosmos-2.5, and Qwen3-Omni are represented in configuration maps and architecture registries across the library.  
Sources: `src/transformers/models/qwen2_audio/modeling_qwen2_audio.py:41-163](), `src/transformers/models/diffusion_gemma/modeling_diffusion_gemma.py:63-134](), `tests/models/diffusion_gemma/test_modeling_diffusion_gemma.py:39-145](), `tests/models/qwen3_5/test_modeling_qwen3_5.py:63-107]()

---

# Page: Tokenization & Input Processing

# Tokenization & Input Processing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



This page describes the input-processing layer: how text and multimodal inputs are handled by tokenizer and processor components, and how pretrained assets are located through Hub and cache utilities. It is a parent overview; implementation details belong in the linked child pages.

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:14-16]()

## The Processing Hierarchy

Text tokenization and modality-specific preprocessing share a common goal: turn user inputs into structured outputs that models can consume. `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` is the common tokenizer interface, with `BatchEncoding` wrapping tokenizer outputs. Processor components combine or route work across modalities; `processing_utils.py` maps modality names to auto-processor classes and base classes. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:96-137]()

### Data Flow Overview

**From raw input to processing code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Natural Language and Input Space"
        RawText["Raw text"]
        RawImage["Image input"]
        RawAudio["Audio input"]
        RawVideo["Video input"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Tokenizer["PreTrainedTokenizerBase"]
        ImageProcessor["ImageProcessingMixin"]
        FeatureExtractor["FeatureExtractionMixin"]
        VideoProcessor["VideoProcessorMixin"]
        Processor["ProcessorMixin"]
    end
    subgraph "Structured Output Space"
        Encoding["BatchEncoding"]
        Features["BatchFeature"]
    end
    RawText --> Tokenizer
    Tokenizer --> Encoding
    RawImage --> ImageProcessor
    RawAudio --> FeatureExtractor
    RawVideo --> VideoProcessor
    ImageProcessor --> Processor
    FeatureExtractor --> Processor
    VideoProcessor --> Processor
    Processor --> Features
```

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:37-45](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-73](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-87]()

## Tokenizers (Text & Discrete Sequences)

`PreTrainedTokenizerBase` provides shared user-facing encoding methods for slow and fast tokenizers. Tokenizer calls produce `BatchEncoding`, a dictionary-like output that can also expose mappings between word, character, and token positions. `AddedToken` represents vocabulary additions with behavior flags, while `TruncationStrategy` names supported truncation policies. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-131](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:160-170](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]()

`TokenizersBackend` is the fast-tokenizer base built on the `tokenizers` library and inherits from `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. The tokenizer layer also supports loading or converting backend representations from tokenizer files. For backend choices, algorithms, and conversion details, see [Tokenizers](#4.1). [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:14-17](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-108]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-131](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:160-170](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-108]()

## Image, Video & Audio Processors

Processing components handle modalities beyond text. `processing_utils.py` associates modality keys with base classes and auto-processor classes, including tokenizers, image processors, video processors, and feature extractors. `BatchFeature` is the dictionary-like output container for feature-extraction calls and can convert its contents to tensor types. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:96-137](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-73](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:75-83]()

Video processing illustrates the modality-specific path: `VideoProcessorMixin.__call__` delegates to `preprocess`, which can decode and sample frames, prepare inputs, and return preprocessed data in a `BatchFeature`. For image transforms, audio features, and modality-specific options, see [Image, Video & Audio Processors](#4.2). [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-87](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:98-140]()

Sources: [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:96-137](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-83](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-87](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:98-140]()

## Hub Integration & File Caching

Tokenizer and processor loading is connected to shared Hub utilities. `utils/hub.py` imports Hub download and cache primitives, and `_get_cache_file_to_return` checks for a cached file at a repository, filename, and revision. `HF_MODULES_CACHE` provides a cache path for dynamic modules. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:29-42](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:104-129]()

Repository template listing can query the Hub or fall back to a local snapshot when local-only operation is requested or network access fails. For file resolution, offline behavior, and validation details, see [Hub Integration & File Caching](#4.3). [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:132-175]()

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:29-42](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:104-129](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:132-175]()

## Chat Templates & Response Parsing

Chat input processing connects structured messages to text rendering and response parsing. The tokenizer base module imports chat-template rendering helpers and `ResponseParser` / `parse_response`; `chat_template_utils.py` contains Jinja-related support. The rendering and parsing details are covered in [Chat Templates & Response Parsing](#4.4). [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-73](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:35-45]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-73](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:35-45]()

## Summary Table of Key Classes

| Input path | Representative code entity | Structured output | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text | `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` | `BatchEncoding` | Shared tokenizer interface and encoding container |
| Image | `ImageProcessingMixin` | `BatchFeature` | Image-processing modality mapping |
| Audio | `FeatureExtractionMixin` | `BatchFeature` | Feature-extraction modality mapping |
| Video | `VideoProcessorMixin` | `BatchFeature` | Video preprocessing path |
| Combined modalities | `ProcessorMixin` | Processor-dependent | Composite processor base-class mapping |

The table summarizes the base-class and output relationships used by the input-processing layer. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-73](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-87]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-19](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-73](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-87]()
