# Page: Tokenizers

# Tokenizers

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the tokenizer interfaces and backend choices represented in the codebase: the shared `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`, the `BatchEncoding` result container, `AddedToken`, Rust-backed tokenizers, the Mistral Common integration, and examples of BPE and tiktoken-related tokenizer inputs. It also identifies what the provided files show—and do not show—about SentencePiece and `convert_slow_tokenizer`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:16-18]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-127]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:14-17]()[src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:45-57]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:16-18](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-127](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:14-17](), [src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:45-57]()

---

## Core Abstractions

The shared tokenizer base, backend implementations, and encoded-output container separate common user-facing behavior from backend-specific tokenization. The available excerpts establish these roles at a high level; they do not expose the full method implementations of the base class. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:16-18]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:16-18](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97]()

### PreTrainedTokenizerBase

`PreTrainedTokenizerBase` is described as the common base for slow and fast tokenization classes. Its role is to host user-facing encoding methods and shared special-token logic. The excerpt also defines common input type aliases, including `TextInput`, `PreTokenizedInput`, and `EncodedInput`, and names the tokenizer configuration and special-token metadata files. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-18]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:139-156]()

`TruncationStrategy` defines `ONLY_FIRST`, `ONLY_SECOND`, `LONGEST_FIRST`, and `DO_NOT_TRUNCATE`; it is documented as the set of choices for the `truncation` argument to `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.__call__`. The provided excerpt does not include the implementation of `__call__` or the details of how each strategy is applied. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:160-170]()

| Code entity | Role shown in the codebase |
|---|---|
| `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` | Common base for slow and fast tokenizers; host for user-facing encoding methods and special-token logic. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-18]() |
| `TextInput`, `PreTokenizedInput`, `EncodedInput` | Type aliases for text, pre-tokenized text, and encoded integer sequences. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:139-145]() |
| `TruncationStrategy` | Enum of truncation choices documented for `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.__call__`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:160-170]() |
| `SPECIAL_TOKENS_MAP_FILE`, `ADDED_TOKENS_FILE`, `TOKENIZER_CONFIG_FILE` | Names of tokenizer metadata files used by the base module. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:150-153]() |
| `FULL_TOKENIZER_FILE` | Name of the serialized fast-tokenizer file, `tokenizer.json`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:155-157]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-18](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:139-170](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:150-157]()

### BatchEncoding

`BatchEncoding` subclasses `UserDict` and is documented as the output container for `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.__call__`, `encode_plus`, and `batch_encode_plus`. It holds tokenizer outputs such as tokens and attention masks, and provides utilities for mapping between word/character space and token space. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]()

The base module conditionally imports the `tokenizers` library’s `Encoding` class as `EncodingFast` when that dependency is available (or during type checking). This establishes the fast-encoding type used by the module, but the supplied excerpt does not show the full `BatchEncoding` implementation or its alignment-method bodies. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-101]()

Tests demonstrate that `BatchEncoding` can convert list-shaped values to NumPy or PyTorch tensors and can add a batch axis for single examples. They also test word-to-token alignment on an encoding returned by a tokenizer. [tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_utils.py:80-87]()[tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_utils.py:116-145]()

| Concern | Evidence in the codebase |
|---|---|
| Dictionary-like output | `BatchEncoding` derives from `UserDict`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]() |
| Word/character-to-token mapping | The class documentation describes these utilities; tests exercise `word_to_tokens`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]()[tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_utils.py:80-87]() |
| Tensor conversion | Tests exercise `convert_to_tensors` for NumPy and PyTorch, including `prepend_batch_axis`. [tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_utils.py:116-145]() |
| Fast encoding association | The base module conditionally imports `EncodingFast`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-101]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-101](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208](), [tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_utils.py:80-87](), [tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_utils.py:116-145]()

### AddedToken

`AddedToken` represents a token added to a tokenizer and carries behavior options. When `tokenizers` is available, the base module imports `AddedToken` from that package; otherwise it defines a fallback dataclass. The fallback stores `content`, `single_word`, `lstrip`, `rstrip`, `special`, and `normalized`; when `normalized` is omitted, it defaults to the inverse of `special`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-125]()

The fallback also exposes its instance state through `__getstate__` and returns its content from `__str__`. These details apply to the fallback definition shown in the excerpt; the excerpt does not establish that the external `tokenizers.AddedToken` implementation has identical internals. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:127-131]()

| Field | Meaning indicated by the fallback definition |
|---|---|
| `content` | Token string. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:117-125]() |
| `single_word` | Single-word behavior option. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:117-125]() |
| `lstrip`, `rstrip` | Whitespace-stripping behavior options. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:117-125]() |
| `special` | Whether the token is marked special. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:117-125]() |
| `normalized` | Whether normalization applies; defaults to `not special` when unspecified. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:113-125]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-131]()

### TruncationStrategy

`TruncationStrategy` is an `ExplicitEnum` with four values. The docstring ties the enum to the `truncation` argument of `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.__call__`; the codebase enumerates the values but does not show the implementation that consumes them. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:160-170]()

| Value | Declared meaning |
|---|---|
| `ONLY_FIRST` | Truncate the first sequence. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:166]() |
| `ONLY_SECOND` | Truncate the second sequence. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:167]() |
| `LONGEST_FIRST` | Truncate the longest sequence first. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:168]() |
| `DO_NOT_TRUNCATE` | Do not truncate. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:169]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:160-170]()

## Tokenizer Hierarchy and Data Flow

At the code level, shared tokenizer behavior is rooted in `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. `TokenizersBackend` is a fast-tokenizer base that inherits from it and wraps the Hugging Face `tokenizers` library; the Mistral Common backend also imports and uses shared base types such as `BatchEncoding` and `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-18]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97]()[src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:26-35]()

Diagram: Tokenizer interfaces and backend entities
```mermaid
graph TD
    RawText["TextInput"]
    PreTokenized["PreTokenizedInput"]
    SharedBase["PreTrainedTokenizerBase"]
    SlowPython["PreTrainedTokenizer"]
    FastBase["TokenizersBackend"]
    RustTokenizer["tokenizers.Tokenizer"]
    MistralBackend["MistralCommonBackend"]
    Output["BatchEncoding"]
    FastEncoding["EncodingFast"]

    RawText --> SharedBase
    PreTokenized --> SharedBase
    SharedBase --> SlowPython
    SharedBase --> FastBase
    FastBase --> RustTokenizer
    FastBase --> Output
    MistralBackend --> SharedBase
    MistralBackend --> Output
    RustTokenizer --> FastEncoding
```
Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:15-18](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:100-101](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:14-17](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97](), [src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:26-35]()

---

## Slow vs. Fast Tokenizers

### Slow Tokenizers

The fast-tokenizer module points readers to `tokenization_utils.py` for slow Python tokenizers. The codebase does not include that module’s full implementation in these snippets, so specific claims about slow-tokenizer performance, internal algorithms, or supported metadata are not established here. Tests import `PreTrainedTokenizer` and exercise tokenizer implementations. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:14-17]()[tests/test_tokenization_common.py:32-40]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:14-17](), [tests/test_tokenization_common.py:32-40]()

### Fast Tokenizers

`TokenizersBackend` is the fast-tokenizer base in `tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py`. It inherits from `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` and is documented as wrapping the Hugging Face `tokenizers` library. Its shared responsibilities include tokenization and special-token methods, pretrained-tokenizer loading and saving, and unified handling of added tokens across underlying vocabularies. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97]()

The module imports Rust-backed tokenizer entities such as `TokenizerFast`, `EncodingFast`, and BPE/Unigram models. Its file constants identify `tokenizer.json` as the tokenizer file, while the backend’s `convert_to_native_format` method is documented as constructing a native tokenizer from available serialization files, including `tokenizer.json`, SentencePiece models, Tekken JSON, or vocab/merges files. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-38]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:54-64]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-108]()

`convert_to_native_format` has a direct-load path for an existing `tokenizer.json` under specified class conditions. Another path reads tokenizer JSON and extracts post-processor, padding, and truncation configuration; its minimal-vocabulary optimization applies only to selected model types and falls back to `TokenizerFast.from_file` for Unigram and cases where the model type is absent. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-152]()

| Fast-backend entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `TokenizersBackend` | Shared fast-tokenizer base derived from `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-97]() |
| `TokenizerFast` | `tokenizers.Tokenizer` imported by the backend module. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-34]() |
| `EncodingFast` | `tokenizers.Encoding` imported by the backend module. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-31]() |
| `BPE`, `Unigram` | Model types imported from `tokenizers.models`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-34]() |
| `tokenizer.json` | Serialized tokenizer file identified by `TOKENIZER_FILE`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:54-58]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-38](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:54-64](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:85-108](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:111-152]()

## Specialized Tokenizer Backends

### SentencePiece Backend

The codebase shows SentencePiece-related integration points. In the fast backend, `SpmConverter` is imported from `convert_slow_tokenizer`; the fast backend also documents `convert_to_native_format` as accepting SentencePiece model files among its possible source formats. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:38-39]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-108]()

The fast backend’s JSON-loading logic distinguishes Unigram models, noting that an empty vocabulary cannot initialize Unigram correctly and that those models fall back to loading the full tokenizer file. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:127-148]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:38-39](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-108](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:127-148]()

### Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)

The backend imports the `BPE` model from `tokenizers.models` and lists BPE as one of the supported trainer-model mappings. Whisper provides a concrete BPE-backed example: `WhisperTokenizer` subclasses `TokenizersBackend`, sets `model = BPE`, and names `vocab.json`, `merges.txt`, and `tokenizer.json` among its tokenizer files. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-34]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:75-82]()[src/transformers/models/whisper/tokenization_whisper.py:32-37]()[src/transformers/models/whisper/tokenization_whisper.py:163-205]()

Diagram: Whisper BPE tokenizer code path
```mermaid
graph LR
    Vocab["vocab.json"]
    Merges["merges.txt"]
    Whisper["WhisperTokenizer"]
    Backend["TokenizersBackend"]
    BPEModel["tokenizers.models.BPE"]
    TokenizerJSON["tokenizer.json"]
    Batch["BatchEncoding"]

    Vocab --> Whisper
    Merges --> Whisper
    TokenizerJSON --> Whisper
    Whisper --> Backend
    Backend --> BPEModel
    Backend --> Batch
```
Sources: [src/transformers/models/whisper/tokenization_whisper.py:32-37](), [src/transformers/models/whisper/tokenization_whisper.py:163-205](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:27-34](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:201-208]()

### tiktoken

The fast backend defines `TIKTOKEN_VOCAB_FILE` as `tokenizer.model`, records `tiktoken.model` as a legacy filename, and includes the vocabulary filename in `VOCAB_FILES_NAMES`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:54-64]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:75-82]()

The Llama tokenizer test exercises loading a tokenizer from a repository containing a tiktoken-style model file using both `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` and `LlamaTokenizer.from_pretrained`, then checks encode/decode round-tripping. [tests/models/llama/test_tokenization_llama.py:41-54]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:54-64](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:75-82](), [tests/models/llama/test_tokenization_llama.py:41-54]()

### Mistral Common Backend

`tokenization_mistral_common.py` imports shared types such as `AddedToken`, `BatchEncoding`, and `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. When `mistral_common` is available, it imports protocol types, validation and special-token types, `MistralTokenizer`, `Tekkenizer`, and tokenizer-file helper functions. [src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:26-57]()

The module defines a mapping from the shared special-token names `bos_token`, `eos_token`, `pad_token`, and `unk_token` to the corresponding `mistral_common` `SpecialTokens` values. Encoding documentation in this module also describes padding, truncation, maximum length, stride, and tensor-return options. [src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:59-65]()[src/transformers/tokenization_mistral_common.py:74-118]()

Diagram: Mistral Common integration points
```mermaid

    Tekkenizer["Tekkenizer"]
    SpecialTokens["SpecialTokens"]
    FileHelpers["get_one_valid_tokenizer_file"]
    Backend["MistralCommonBackend"]
```

## convert_slow_tokenizer Utility

The fast-backend module imports `SpmConverter` from `convert_slow_tokenizer`, establishing a SentencePiece-related converter integration point. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:38-39]()

The fast backend also exposes `convert_to_native_format`, which builds a native `tokenizers.Tokenizer` from available serialization files. Its branches handle tokenizer JSON input and recover backend configuration such as post-processing, padding, and truncation. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-108]()[src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:111-152]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:38-39](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:103-108](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:111-152]()

# Page: Image, Video & Audio Processors

# Image, Video & Audio Processors

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes how Transformers represents and coordinates image, video, and audio preprocessing. It focuses on `ProcessorMixin`, modality-specific processing interfaces, `BatchFeature`, input normalization, video frame sampling, and the boundaries of audio feature extraction. The available source excerpts define `VideoProcessorMixin` rather than a class named `BaseVideoProcessor`; the distinction is noted below. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:89-159](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-100](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-83]()

Sources: [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:89-159](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-100](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-83]()

---

## Core abstractions and class hierarchy

Processing is organized around components for each modality. `ProcessorMixin` supports multimodal processor composition, while `BatchFeature` provides a dictionary-like representation for processed outputs. The modality registry in `processing_utils.py` maps component attributes to auto-processor classes and base-class names. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:92-137](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-83]()

| Name | Role | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `ProcessorMixin` | Common processor type used by multimodal processor implementations; its type is also used by the processor type variable. | [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:89-90]() |
| `ImageProcessingMixin` | The image-processor base-class name used in the modality-to-base-class registry. Its implementation is not included in the supplied source excerpt. | [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137]() |
| `VideoProcessorMixin` | Video-processing class shown in the supplied implementation. It extends `BaseImageProcessor`, declares video-oriented defaults, and routes calls to `preprocess`. | [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-100]() |
| `BaseVideoProcessor` | This name does not appear in the supplied video-processing excerpt; the class shown there is `VideoProcessorMixin`. | [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-100]() |
| `FeatureExtractionMixin` | Audio-processor and feature-extractor base-class name used by the modality registry. Its implementation is not included in the supplied excerpt. | [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137]() |
| `BatchFeature` | `UserDict` subclass for feature-extractor and processor outputs, with optional conversion of its contents to tensors. | [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-83]() |

### Lazy modality lookup

`MODALITY_TO_AUTOPROCESSOR_MAPPING` is backed by `_LazyAutoProcessorMapping`. On lookup, the mapping imports the auto-processor module for the requested modality and returns the named class. This defers those imports and avoids circular imports. The shown mapping covers image, video, feature-extractor, audio-processor, and tokenizer attributes. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:96-124]()

`_get_modality_for_attribute` determines a modality by searching for a registered modality name within an attribute name. The registry separately associates modalities with their base-class names, including `ImageProcessingMixin`, `FeatureExtractionMixin`, and `VideoProcessorMixin`. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-159]()

Sources: [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:89-159](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-100](), [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-83]()

---

## Data flow and processing pipelines

### From raw input to model-ready data

The shared shape of the processing path is: normalize modality inputs, apply modality-specific work, and return model-facing fields. For video, the implementation makes this order explicit: validate keyword arguments, decode and optionally sample frames, prepare the video inputs, standardize preprocessing kwargs, then call `_preprocess`. [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:98-140]()

| Modality | Input and normalization shown in the sources | Processing result or field |
|---|---|---|
| Image | `ImageInput` accepts PIL images, NumPy arrays, Torch tensors, and lists of those types. `make_list_of_images` normalizes a single image or batch to a list and checks dimensionality. | Image processors commonly expose model-facing pixel values; the supplied test mixin identifies `pixel_values` as its default image input name. [src/transformers/image_utils.py:83-85](), [src/transformers/image_utils.py:167-202](), [tests/test_processing_common.py:127-143]() |
| Video | `VideoInput` includes frame lists, arrays, tensors, paths, and URLs. `make_batched_videos` normalizes video inputs, while `VideoProcessorMixin.preprocess` decodes and samples before preparing frames. | The video processor declares `pixel_values_videos` as its model input name. [src/transformers/video_utils.py:61-76](), [src/transformers/video_utils.py:185-204](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-87](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:119-140]() |
| Audio | `AudioInput` includes NumPy arrays, Torch tensors, and sequences of either. `audio_utils.py` describes its functions as waveform feature-extraction utilities and imports optional decoding libraries when available. | The processor test mixin distinguishes raw audio values (`input_values`) from computed features such as Mel spectrograms or STFT (`input_features`). [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:45-63](), [tests/test_processing_common.py:138-143]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/image_utils.py:83-85](), [src/transformers/image_utils.py:167-202](), [src/transformers/video_utils.py:61-76](), [src/transformers/video_utils.py:185-204](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-140](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:45-63](), [tests/test_processing_common.py:127-143]()

---

## `ProcessorMixin`: orchestration for multimodal processing

`ProcessorMixin` is the common processor type used by multimodal processor implementations. For example, `PaliGemmaProcessor` inherits from it and accepts an image processor and tokenizer; `LlavaOnevisionProcessor` also inherits from it and accepts image, tokenizer, and video components. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:89-90](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:22-28](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:62-93](), [src/transformers/models/llava_onevision/processing_llava_onevision.py:20-21](), [src/transformers/models/llava_onevision/processing_llava_onevision.py:38-83]()

The modality registry provides a shared naming convention for processor components. For example, `image_processor`, `video_processor`, `feature_extractor`, `audio_processor`, and `tokenizer` resolve to their corresponding auto-processor classes through lazy imports. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:96-137]()

Sources: [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:89-137](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:22-93](), [src/transformers/models/llava_onevision/processing_llava_onevision.py:20-83]()

---

## Image processing: inputs, resizing, and normalization

### Input forms and batch normalization

`ImageInput` accepts PIL images, NumPy arrays, Torch tensors, and lists of those forms. The image utilities define `ChannelDimension` values `channels_first` and `channels_last`; `is_scaled_image` checks whether a NumPy image appears to have already been scaled to `[0, 1]`, treating `uint8` separately. [src/transformers/image_utils.py:83-90](), [src/transformers/image_utils.py:156-164]()

`make_list_of_images` converts an individual image to a one-element list and handles array-like inputs with either the expected number of dimensions for one image or one extra dimension for a batch. [src/transformers/image_utils.py:167-212]()

Sources: [src/transformers/image_utils.py:39-90](), [src/transformers/image_utils.py:156-212](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:26-87]()

---

## Video processing: `VideoProcessorMixin` and frame sampling

The supplied implementation defines `VideoProcessorMixin`, which extends `BaseImageProcessor`, sets `model_input_names` to `["pixel_values_videos"]`, and makes `__call__` delegate to `preprocess`. [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-97]()

### `preprocess` sequence

`VideoProcessorMixin.preprocess`:
1. Validates supplied kwargs against the processor’s `valid_kwargs` and the `return_tensors` option, then validates their types.
2. Fills missing kwargs from the processor instance.
3. Extracts input-format, RGB-conversion, sampling, device, and video-metadata options.
4. Creates a sampling callback from `self.sample_frames` when `do_sample_frames` is enabled.
5. Calls `_decode_and_sample_videos`, then `_prepare_input_videos`.
6. Standardizes and validates remaining preprocessing kwargs, calls `_preprocess`, and optionally adds `video_metadata` to the output. [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:98-140]()

Sources: [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:76-140](), [src/transformers/video_utils.py:61-113](), [src/transformers/video_utils.py:185-195]()

---

## Audio feature extraction: `FeatureExtractionMixin` and `BatchFeature`

The modality registry identifies both `audio_processor` and `feature_extractor` with the base-class name `FeatureExtractionMixin`. `audio_utils.py` describes its signal-processing functions as pure NumPy utilities intended to support all frameworks without unnecessary dependencies. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:45-63]()

Sources: [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:126-137](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:45-63](), [src/transformers/audio_utils.py:176-192](), [tests/test_processing_common.py:138-143]()

---

## `BatchFeature`: shared output container

`BatchFeature` subclasses `UserDict` and holds outputs from feature-extractor padding and feature-extractor-specific call methods. Its constructor accepts a data dictionary, an optional tensor type, and keys to exclude from tensor conversion. [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-99]()

Sources: [src/transformers/feature_extraction_utils.py:58-156](), [tests/test_processing_common.py:127-143](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:125-135]()

---

## Multimodal processor composition

Model-specific processors combine modality components with model-specific token and layout rules:
- `PaliGemmaProcessor` inherits from `ProcessorMixin`, stores an image processor and tokenizer, ensures the tokenizer has an image token, and adds extra location/segmentation tokens. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:35-36](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:62-93]()
- `LlavaOnevisionProcessor` inherits from `ProcessorMixin` and accepts image, tokenizer, and video components. [src/transformers/models/llava_onevision/processing_llava_onevision.py:38-83]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:35-36](), [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:62-135](), [src/transformers/models/llava_onevision/processing_llava_onevision.py:38-115]()

---

## Integration example: `PaliGemmaProcessor`

`PaliGemmaProcessor` illustrates a processor that combines text and image processing. Its initializer requires an image processor with `image_seq_length`, obtains or registers an image token with the tokenizer, adds extra tokens, and passes components to `ProcessorMixin`. [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:62-93]()

Sources: [src/transformers/models/paligemma/processing_paligemma.py:62-157]()

## Testing infrastructure

`ProcessorTesterMixin` supplies common processor-test conventions. Its modality specifications associate text with a tokenizer, images with an image processor, videos with a video processor, and audio with a feature extractor or audio processor. [tests/test_processing_common.py:75-103]()

# Page: Hub Integration & File Caching

# Hub Integration & File Caching

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the Hub and file-caching behavior within the Hugging Face Transformers library: shared Hub API setup, cache lookup helpers, template listing, dynamic-module cache setup and import discovery, and the places where processors and Auto factories connect to these utilities. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:46-63](), [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:33-42]()

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:46-63](), [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:33-42]()

---

## Core Caching Mechanism

`src/transformers/utils/hub.py` provides Hub-related utilities and imports `hf_hub_download`, `snapshot_download`, and `try_to_load_from_cache` from `huggingface_hub`. The module defines `_get_cache_file_to_return`, which checks for an existing cached file with `try_to_load_from_cache`; it returns the cached path when present and not marked `_CACHED_NO_EXIST`, otherwise returns `None`. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:29-42](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:116-129]()

### Key Components

- **`hf_api()`**: Returns a shared `HfApi` instance configured with `library_name="transformers"` and the Transformers version. It initializes the singleton on first call. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:75-90]()
- **`DownloadKwargs`**: Declares optional Hub-download arguments, including `cache_dir`, `force_download`, `local_files_only`, `token`, `revision`, and `subfolder`. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:93-102]()
- **`_get_cache_file_to_return(...)`**: Calls `try_to_load_from_cache` with repository/file identifiers and cache/revision arguments. Returns a path only when the lookup succeeds and the result is not `_CACHED_NO_EXIST`; otherwise returns `None`. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:116-129]()
- **`list_repo_templates(...)`**: Lists `.jinja` files under `additional_chat_templates/` through `hf_api().list_repo_tree` when network access is allowed. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:132-175]()

### Cache Lookup Flow

**Diagram: Cache lookup and template-listing entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Request["File or template lookup"] --> CacheHelper["_get_cache_file_to_return"]
  CacheHelper --> TryCache["try_to_load_from_cache"]
  TryCache --> Found{"Cached path available and not _CACHED_NO_EXIST"}
  Found -->|"Yes"| ReturnPath["Return cached path"]
  Found -->|"No"| NoneResult["Return None"]
  Request --> TemplateList["list_repo_templates"]
  TemplateList --> NetworkChoice{"local_files_only is false"}
  NetworkChoice -->|"Yes"| RepoTree["hf_api().list_repo_tree"]
  RepoTree -->|"Hub error or network issue"| Snapshot["hf_api().snapshot_download local_files_only=True"]
  NetworkChoice -->|"No"| Snapshot
  Snapshot --> TemplatesDir["additional_chat_templates directory"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:116-129](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:132-175]()

### Integration Call Sites

`processing_utils.py` imports `cached_file`, `hf_api`, and `resolve_revision` from its utilities, and `video_processing_utils.py` imports `cached_file`, `hf_api`, and `resolve_revision` from `utils.hub`. [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:46-63](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:31-46]()

Sources: [src/transformers/processing_utils.py:46-63](), [src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py:31-46]()

---

## Offline Mode & Environment Management

### Offline-Aware Template Listing

`list_repo_templates` accepts `local_files_only`. When it is false, it tries the Hub repository tree first. It re-raises gated-repository, repository-not-found, and revision-not-found exceptions; for Hub HTTP errors, `OfflineModeIsEnabled`, and network errors, it falls back to a local snapshot lookup. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:132-174]()

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:29-56](), [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:132-174]()

### Cache Locations and Dynamic Modules

`HF_MODULES_CACHE` is initialized from the `HF_MODULES_CACHE` environment variable, falling back to a `modules` directory beneath `huggingface_hub.constants.HF_HOME`. `TRANSFORMERS_DYNAMIC_MODULE_NAME` is set to `"transformers_modules"`. [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:104-110](), [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:36-42]()

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:104-110](), [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:36-42]()

---

## Safetensors Conversion Utility

A test comment notes that the expected number of unexpected keys differs between a PyTorch checkpoint and a safetensors checkpoint [tests/models/auto/test_modeling_auto.py:103-114](). 

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/hub.py:14-16](), [tests/models/auto/test_modeling_auto.py:103-114]()

---

## Dynamic Module Loading for `trust_remote_code=True`

`dynamic_module_utils.py` provides utilities to dynamically load objects from the Hub. It imports `HF_MODULES_CACHE`, `TRANSFORMERS_DYNAMIC_MODULE_NAME`, `cached_file`, and `extract_commit_hash`. [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:14-14](), [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:33-43](), [src/transformers/models/auto/auto_factory.py:24-35]()

### Cache Initialization

- **`init_hf_modules()`**: Returns early if `HF_MODULES_CACHE` is already on `sys.path`. Otherwise it appends the directory to `sys.path`, creates it, and creates a top-level `__init__.py` if needed. [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:85-99]()
- **`create_dynamic_module(name)`**: Calls `init_hf_modules()`, resolves the requested path beneath the module cache, recursively creates missing parent modules, and ensures an `__init__.py` exists. [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:101-121]()

### Import Discovery

- **`get_relative_imports(module_file)`**: Reads a module file and uses regular expressions to find `import .module` and `from .module import ...` forms. [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:123-141]()
- **`get_relative_import_files(module_file)`**: Repeatedly discovers relative imports and maps them to sibling `.py` paths until no new imports remain. [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:144-173]()
- **`get_imports(filename)`**: Extracts non-relative library imports. [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:176-186]()

Sources: [src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py:85-186]()

---

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Language["User-facing operation"]

    Remote["Prepare dynamic Python modules"]
  end
  subgraph Entities["Code entities"]
    CacheHelper["_get_cache_file_to_return"]
    CacheBackend["try_to_load_from_cache"]
    TemplateFunction["list_repo_templates"]
    Api["hf_api"]
    ModuleInit["init_hf_modules"]
    ModuleCreate["create_dynamic_module"]
    RelativeImports["get_relative_imports"]
    ImportFiles["get_relative_import_files"]
    AutoFactory["auto_factory.py"]
  end
  Load --> CacheHelper
  CacheHelper --> CacheBackend
  Templates --> TemplateFunction
  TemplateFunction --> Api
  Remote --> ModuleInit
  ModuleInit --> ModuleCreate
  ModuleCreate --> RelativeImports
  RelativeImports --> ImportFiles
  AutoFactory -->|"imports remote-code helpers"| ModuleInit
```

# Page: Chat Templates & Response Parsing

# Chat Templates & Response Parsing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the path between structured conversations and model text: Jinja-based chat formatting, `apply_chat_template`, tool and JSON-schema helpers, and the `chat_parsing` response parser. Chat models process token sequences; templates encode message structure into those sequences, while response parsing reconstructs structured fields and tool calls from generated text. [docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:23-29]()

Sources: [docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:23-29]()

---

## 1. Jinja Chat Templates & `apply_chat_template`

A chat is commonly represented as a list of dictionaries with `role` and `content` fields. A tokenizer’s chat template formats that history according to the format expected by the model; different models can use different control tokens even when they share a base model. [docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:23-29]()[docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:74-84]()

`apply_chat_template` can return the formatted sequence as text or tokenize it. With `add_generation_prompt=True`, the formatted prompt can include a prefix marking the start of an assistant response. The documentation recommends using `tokenize=True` when possible; if formatting to text and tokenizing separately, disable additional special-token insertion to avoid duplicating tokens already supplied by the template. [docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:84-109]()[docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:125-132]()

The implementation connects the tokenizer base class to template-rendering utilities: `tokenization_utils_base.py` imports `render_jinja_template`, `mark_control_tokens`, `encode_marked_chat`, and related helpers from `chat_template_utils.py`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-73]()

### Data Flow of Chat Template Application

The diagram maps the user-facing conversation and tool inputs to the template-related code entities. The documented interface accepts structured messages and can produce either formatted text or tokenized input. [docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:74-109]()

**Diagram: `apply_chat_template` from conversation to model input**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        ChatHistory["messages: role and content dictionaries"]
        ToolInput["tools: callable or schema input"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Apply["PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template"]
        Render["render_jinja_template"]
        Formatted["formatted prompt"]
        Tokenized["tokenized input"]
        ChatHistory --> Apply
        ToolInput --> Apply
        Apply --> Render
        Render --> Formatted
        Formatted --> Tokenized
    end
```

Sources: [docs/source/en/chat_templating.md:74-109](), [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-73]()

The code also imports `ResponseParser` and aliases `parse_response` as `_template_parse_response` in `tokenization_utils_base.py`, showing that tokenizer-facing chat functionality is wired to the response-parsing package as well as to template rendering. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-73]()

Sources: [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-73]()

---

## 2. Tool & JSON Schema Helpers (`chat_template_utils.py`)

`chat_template_utils.py` contains type-hint and docstring parsing support used to describe tools. It defines `TypeHintParsingException` and `DocstringParsingException`, and regular expressions for extracting a function description, its `Args:` block, and its `Returns:` block. [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:57-82]()

The schema type mapper handles Python primitives and containers, including `int`, `float`, `str`, `bool`, `None`, `list`, `tuple`, and `dict`. When the relevant optional backends are available, it also maps image and tensor types. `_get_json_schema_type` applies these mappings. [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:84-103]()

`_parse_type_hint` recursively handles unions, literals, lists, and tuples. For unions, it represents simple types with a `type` entry and more complex types with `anyOf`; a union containing `None` is marked nullable. Literal values become an `enum`. [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:105-169]()

The helper tests demonstrate `get_json_schema(fn)` producing a function schema with a name, description, parameter properties, and a required-parameter list. They also cover bare containers, unions, nullable values, defaults, and nested lists. [tests/utils/test_chat_template_utils.py:24-60]()[tests/utils/test_chat_template_utils.py:62-90]()[tests/utils/test_chat_template_utils.py:92-179]()[tests/utils/test_chat_template_utils.py:181-207]()

### Natural-language tool description to schema entities

**Diagram: Python function annotations and docstrings to tool schema**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Function["Python function"]
        Annotation["parameter type hints"]
        Docstring["description and Args documentation"]
        Function --> Annotation
        Function --> Docstring
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Schema["get_json_schema"]
        TypeParser["_parse_type_hint"]
        TypeMap["_get_json_schema_type"]
        SchemaOutput["function schema"]
        Exception["TypeHintParsingException or DocstringParsingException"]
        Annotation --> TypeParser
        TypeParser --> TypeMap
        Docstring --> Schema
        Function --> Schema
        Schema --> SchemaOutput
        TypeParser --> Exception
    end
```

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:57-103](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:105-169](), [tests/utils/test_chat_template_utils.py:24-60]()

---

## 3. Response Parsing Architecture (`chat_parsing/`)

The tokenizer base module imports `ResponseParser` and `parse_response` from `transformers.utils.chat_parsing`. [src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:65-66]() The parser tests import `ResponseParser`, `parse_response`, `_coerce`, `_schema_types`, and `load_response_template`, and describe the parser as a declarative response-template parser. [tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:14-29]()

The tests express response formats as templates with a `start_anchor` and named `fields`. Field specifications can describe delimiters or patterns, content formats such as text or JSON, and transformations for the extracted value. Examples cover response text, reasoning text, and tool calls with function names and arguments. [tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:32-79]()[tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:82-104]()[tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:127-175]()

The fixtures also show that a template can configure repeated tool-call regions, regex-based opening markers, inline XML-like content, and alternative anchors. These are fixture examples rather than a complete inventory of parser capabilities. [tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:57-79]()[tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:82-104]()[tests/utils/test_chat_parsing.py:127-175]()

# Page: Text Generation

# Text Generation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The `transformers` text-generation subsystem provides a shared interface for generating sequences from text-decoder, text-to-text, speech-to-text, and vision-to-text models. This parent page summarizes how generation configuration, decoding, KV caching, and related components fit together; detailed implementation guidance is linked to the child pages. [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-108]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-108]()

---

## System Overview

`generate()` uses a `GenerationConfig` to select generation behavior. The configuration documents greedy decoding, multinomial sampling, beam search, beam sampling, and assisted decoding; `GenerationMode` represents these modes in code. Generation also draws on cache implementations, logits processors, stopping criteria, and candidate generators. [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:60-80](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:81-119]()

---

## Text Generation Execution Flow

The diagram connects user-facing generation concepts to identifiers used in the codebase. It is a high-level relationship map, not a call-order specification.

**Diagram: Text Generation Concepts and Code Entities**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Prompt["User prompt"] --> Choice["Choose decoding behavior"]
        Choice --> Result["Generated sequence"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Generate["generate()"] --> Config["GenerationConfig"]
        Config --> Mode["GenerationMode"]
        Mode --> Dispatch["GENERATION_MODES_MAPPING"]
        Dispatch --> Sample["_sample"]
        Dispatch --> Beam["_beam_search"]
        Dispatch --> Assisted["_assisted_decoding"]
        Sample --> Cache["Cache implementations"]
        Beam --> Cache
        Assisted --> Candidate["CandidateGenerator"]
        Cache --> Result
        Candidate --> Result
    end

    Prompt -.-> Generate
    Result -.-> Result
```

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:134-152](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-55](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-27]()

---

## Core Components Overview

### 1. GenerationMixin & Decoding Strategies

The generation interface uses configuration to determine a decoding mode. In the dispatch mapping, sampling and greedy modes map to `_sample`, beam modes map to `_beam_search`, and assisted generation maps to `_assisted_decoding`. Assisted generation can use candidate generators, including an assistant-model-based implementation. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-152](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-40](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:73-94]()

For details, see [GenerationMixin & Decoding Strategies](#5.1).

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-152](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-40](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:73-94]()

---

### 2. KV Cache Implementations

Caches hold model state used during generation. The cache layer interface includes operations for updating key/value states, querying sequence and mask sizes, resetting, and reordering for beam search. `DynamicLayer` grows its stored key/value tensors as new states are added; the generation utilities import several cache types, including `DynamicCache`, `StaticCache`, `QuantizedCache`, and `EncoderDecoderCache`. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-27](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:48-69](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-100](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-153](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37]()

For details, see [KV Cache Implementations](#5.2).

Sources: [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-27](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:48-69](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-100](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-153](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37]()

---

### 3. Logits Processors, Stopping Criteria & Watermarking

`LogitsProcessorList` applies a sequence of processors to model scores. Generation utilities import processors and stopping criteria as separate components; the broader generation API also includes watermarking and streamers. These components provide hooks for controlling token scores, termination, and output handling. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-68](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:70-98](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:81-119](), [tests/generation/test_utils.py:96-112]()

For details, see [Logits Processors, Stopping Criteria & Watermarking](#5.3).

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-68](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:70-98](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:81-119](), [tests/generation/test_utils.py:96-112]()

---

### 4. Continuous Batching

The generation utilities import `ContinuousMixin`, connecting continuous-batching functionality to the generation subsystem. Its manager, scheduling, paged-cache, backend, and offloading details are covered in the child page. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:82-82]()

For details, see [Continuous Batching](#5.4).

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:82-82]()

---

# Page: GenerationMixin & Decoding Strategies

# GenerationMixin & Decoding Strategies

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes how generation strategy names and configuration relate to the generation code entities in Transformers. It covers the visible `GenerationMixin` imports and dispatch mapping, the `GenerationConfig` and `GenerationMode` definitions, the candidate-generator interface, and the logits-processing and cache abstractions connected to generation [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-119]().

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-119](), [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-150]()

## Overview of `generate()` and decoding-mode dispatch

### Entry point and mode mapping

`GenerationMixin` is the generation mixin imported by generation tests, and `src/transformers/generation/utils.py` imports the cache, candidate-generator, generation-configuration, logits-processing, and stopping-criteria types used by its generation implementation [tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:80-81](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-119]().

The module-level `GENERATION_MODES_MAPPING` maps `GenerationMode.SAMPLE` and `GenerationMode.GREEDY_SEARCH` to `_sample`, `GenerationMode.BEAM_SEARCH` and `GenerationMode.BEAM_SAMPLE` to `_beam_search`, and `GenerationMode.ASSISTED_GENERATION` to `_assisted_decoding`. It maps the legacy DoLa, contrastive-search, group-beam-search, and constrained-beam-search modes to named `transformers-community` custom-generation identifiers [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154]().

`GenerationConfig` documents the common mode combinations: one beam and no sampling for greedy decoding; one beam with sampling for multinomial sampling; multiple beams without sampling for beam search; multiple beams with sampling for beam-search sampling; and assisted decoding when an assistant model or prompt-lookup token count is supplied [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-108]().

| Configuration or mode | Strategy described by the code | Mapping shown in `GENERATION_MODES_MAPPING` |
|---|---|---|
| `num_beams=1`, `do_sample=False` | Greedy decoding | `GREEDY_SEARCH` → `_sample` |
| `num_beams=1`, `do_sample=True` | Multinomial sampling | `SAMPLE` → `_sample` |
| `num_beams>1`, `do_sample=False` | Beam-search decoding | `BEAM_SEARCH` → `_beam_search` |
| `num_beams>1`, `do_sample=True` | Beam-search multinomial sampling | `BEAM_SAMPLE` → `_beam_search` |
| Assistant model or `prompt_lookup_num_tokens` | Assisted decoding | `ASSISTED_GENERATION` → `_assisted_decoding` |

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154]()

### Diagram: Generation strategy names mapped to code entities

The diagram connects user-facing strategy choices to the `GenerationMode` members and the method names or custom-generation identifiers in the mapping [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154](), [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Greedy["Greedy decoding"]
        Sampling["Multinomial sampling"]
        Beam["Beam search"]
        BeamSample["Beam-search sampling"]
        Assisted["Assisted decoding"]
        Contrastive["Contrastive search"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        GreedyMode["GenerationMode.GREEDY_SEARCH"]
        SampleMode["GenerationMode.SAMPLE"]
        BeamMode["GenerationMode.BEAM_SEARCH"]
        BeamSampleMode["GenerationMode.BEAM_SAMPLE"]
        AssistedMode["GenerationMode.ASSISTED_GENERATION"]
        ContrastiveMode["GenerationMode.CONTRASTIVE_SEARCH"]
        SampleMethod["_sample"]
        BeamMethod["_beam_search"]
        AssistedMethod["_assisted_decoding"]
        ContrastiveCustom["transformers-community/contrastive-search"]
    end
    Greedy --> GreedyMode
    Sampling --> SampleMode
    Beam --> BeamMode
    BeamSample --> BeamSampleMode
    Assisted --> AssistedMode
    Contrastive --> ContrastiveMode
    GreedyMode --> SampleMethod
    SampleMode --> SampleMethod
    BeamMode --> BeamMethod
    BeamSampleMode --> BeamMethod
    AssistedMode --> AssistedMethod
    ContrastiveMode --> ContrastiveCustom
```

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154](), [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108]()

## `GenerationConfig` and `GenerationMode`

### `GenerationConfig`

`GenerationConfig` is the configuration class for generation tasks. Its documented scope includes text-decoder, text-to-text, speech-to-text, and vision-to-text generation. Fields still set to `None` can be filled from default generation parameters during generation [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-120]().

The visible field documentation groups parameters for output length and strategy selection. It recommends `max_new_tokens` for controlling the number of generated tokens independently of prompt length, while retaining `max_length` for backward compatibility. It also documents `min_length`, `min_new_tokens`, beam-search `early_stopping`, `max_time`, and `stop_strings` [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:122-147]().

The configuration class documents strategy selection through `do_sample` and `num_beams`, and the module defines the corresponding `GenerationMode` values [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-95](), [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:148-150]().

### `GenerationMode`

`GenerationMode` is an `ExplicitEnum` containing non-beam modes (`CONTRASTIVE_SEARCH`, `GREEDY_SEARCH`, `SAMPLE`, `ASSISTED_GENERATION`, and `DOLA_GENERATION`) and beam modes (`BEAM_SEARCH`, `BEAM_SAMPLE`, `CONSTRAINED_BEAM_SEARCH`, and `GROUP_BEAM_SEARCH`) [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-94]().

The presence of a mode in the enum does not imply that the mode maps to an in-process decoding method in the shown mapping: contrastive search, DoLa, group beam search, and constrained beam search map to `transformers-community` identifiers in `GENERATION_MODES_MAPPING` [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154]().

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-150](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154]()

## Decoding strategies

### Greedy decoding and sampling

The generation configuration documentation distinguishes greedy decoding from multinomial sampling by the `do_sample` and `num_beams` combinations. The dispatch mapping sends both `GREEDY_SEARCH` and `SAMPLE` to `_sample` [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-108](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-147]().

The generation-strategies documentation describes greedy search as selecting the most likely next token and sampling as randomly selecting a token from the vocabulary probability distribution [docs/source/en/generation_strategies.md:27-54]().

### Beam search

The configuration documentation identifies beam search when `num_beams>1` and `do_sample=False`, and beam-search multinomial sampling when both multiple beams and sampling are enabled. The dispatch mapping sends `BEAM_SEARCH` and `BEAM_SAMPLE` to `_beam_search` [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-108](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:146-147]().

The strategy guide describes beam search as maintaining multiple candidate sequences and selecting based on overall probability [docs/source/en/generation_strategies.md:73-80]().

### Contrastive search and legacy/custom modes

`GenerationMode.CONTRASTIVE_SEARCH` is present in the enum, but `GENERATION_MODES_MAPPING` associates it with the `transformers-community/contrastive-search` identifier rather than a local method name [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:83-94](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:149-154]().

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-108](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154](), [docs/source/en/generation_strategies.md:27-110]()

## Custom generation methods

Custom generation methods can provide specialized behavior, including custom handling for uncertainty, rollback, special tokens, or KV caches. The generation-strategies guide describes repository-provided custom generation code as an extension of custom modeling code and states that using it requires `trust_remote_code=True` [docs/source/en/generation_strategies.md:99-110]().

Sources: [docs/source/en/generation_strategies.md:99-126](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:149-154]()

## Assisted and speculative decoding

### Candidate-generator contract

`CandidateGenerator` is the base class for candidate generators used during assisted generation. Its `get_candidates()` interface accepts `input_ids` and returns candidate token sequences, optionally accompanied by logits. Its `update_candidate_strategy()` interface accepts the current IDs, model scores, and the number of matches between candidates and model predictions [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-70]().

The generation module imports multiple concrete candidate-generator types, including `AssistedCandidateGenerator`, `AssistedCandidateGeneratorDifferentTokenizers`, `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator`, `EarlyExitCandidateGenerator`, `MTPCandidateGenerator`, `PromptLookupCandidateGenerator`, `SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator`, and `UniversalSpeculativeDecodingGenerator` [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:60-74]().

### Assistant-model candidate generation

`AssistedCandidateGenerator` is documented as generating candidates through a smaller assistant model for assisted generation and speculative decoding [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:73-104]().

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-140](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:60-74]()

### Diagram: Assisted decoding entities and information flow

This diagram maps the natural-language concepts of draft candidates and verification to the candidate-generator interface and assistant-model entity [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-70](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:73-140]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Prompt["Input token sequence"]
        Drafts["Proposed candidate tokens"]
        Matches["Candidate and prediction matches"]
        Output["Generated sequence"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        InputIds["input_ids"]
        Generator["CandidateGenerator"]
        GetCandidates["get_candidates"]
        AssistantGenerator["AssistedCandidateGenerator"]
        AssistantModel["assistant_model"]
        UpdateStrategy["update_candidate_strategy"]
    end
    Prompt --> InputIds
    InputIds --> GetCandidates
    Generator --> GetCandidates
    GetCandidates --> AssistantGenerator
    AssistantGenerator --> AssistantModel
    AssistantModel --> Drafts
    Drafts --> Matches
    Matches --> UpdateStrategy
    UpdateStrategy --> Generator
    Matches --> Output
```

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-70](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:73-140]()

| `MTPCandidateGenerator` | Imported as a candidate-generator implementation; detailed behavior is not shown. |
| `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator` | Imported as a candidate-generator implementation; detailed behavior is not shown. |
| `EarlyExitCandidateGenerator` | Imported as a candidate-generator implementation; detailed behavior is not shown. |
| `SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` | Imported as a candidate-generator implementation; detailed behavior is not shown. |
| `UniversalSpeculativeDecodingGenerator` | Imported as a candidate-generator implementation; detailed behavior is not shown. |

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:60-74](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-140]()

## Logits processing and stopping criteria

### `LogitsProcessorList`

`LogitsProcessor` is the base class for score processors. `LogitsProcessorList` is a list subclass that applies its processors sequentially to the input IDs and scores; it checks whether processors require additional keyword arguments and raises an error if required arguments are missing [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-98]().

`MinLengthLogitsProcessor` suppresses EOS-token scores while the sequence is shorter than its configured minimum length [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:101-159]().

### Stopping criteria

The generation module imports `StoppingCriteria`, `StoppingCriteriaList`, and criteria including `ConfidenceCriteria`, `EosTokenCriteria`, `MaxLengthCriteria`, `MaxTimeCriteria`, and `StopStringCriteria` [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:111-119]().

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-159](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:83-119]()

## KV-cache relationship to generation

The generation module imports `Cache`, `DynamicCache`, `EncoderDecoderCache`, `QuantizedCache`, and `StaticCache`, and defines a list of cache-related model-output names: `past_key_values`, `cache_params`, `state`, `mems`, and `past_buckets_states` [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:134-141]().

`CacheLayerMixin` is the abstract base for a single cache layer. Its required operations include lazy initialization, updating key/value states, reporting mask sizes and sequence length, and reporting maximum length [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-69](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-100]().

`DynamicLayer` is documented as a cache layer that grows as tokens are generated [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-137]().

### Diagram: Generation cache names and cache-layer operations

The diagram maps the generation-time cache concept to the names and cache interfaces present in the source [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:134-141](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-69](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-137]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        CacheState["Past generation state"]
        NewStates["New key and value states"]
        BeamOrder["Beam reorder indices"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        CacheNames["ALL_CACHE_NAMES"]
        PastKeyValues["past_key_values"]
        CacheParams["cache_params"]
        State["state"]
        CacheLayer["CacheLayerMixin"]
        DynamicLayerNode["DynamicLayer"]
        Update["update"]
        Reorder["reorder_cache"]
    end
    CacheState --> CacheNames
    CacheNames --> PastKeyValues
    CacheNames --> CacheParams
    CacheNames --> State
    NewStates --> Update
    DynamicLayerNode --> Update
    Update --> CacheLayer
    BeamOrder --> Reorder
    CacheLayer --> Reorder
```

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:134-141](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-69](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-137]()

## Summary

- `GenerationConfig` documents parameter combinations for greedy decoding, multinomial sampling, beam search, beam-search sampling, and assisted decoding [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:96-108]().
- `GENERATION_MODES_MAPPING` maps greedy and sampling modes to `_sample`, beam modes to `_beam_search`, assisted generation to `_assisted_decoding`, and several other modes to community identifiers [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:143-154]().
- `CandidateGenerator` defines interfaces for generating candidate sequences and updating strategy from match outcomes; `AssistedCandidateGenerator` uses an assistant model [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-70](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:73-104]().
- `LogitsProcessorList` applies score processors in sequence, and generation imports stopping-criteria types for termination behavior [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:63-98](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:111-119]().
- Generation imports multiple cache implementations and cache-related output names; `CacheLayerMixin` and `DynamicLayer` define cache-layer operations in the cache subsystem [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:134-141](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-69](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-137]().

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-154](), [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:78-150](), [src/transformers/generation/candidate_generator.py:35-140](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-159](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-137]()
