# Page: KV Cache Implementations

# KV Cache Implementations

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes the KV-cache abstractions and implementations used to retain attention keys and values during autoregressive generation. It covers the cache and layer APIs, `DynamicCache`, `StaticCache`, `QuantizedCache`, sliding-window cache layers, `EncoderDecoderCache`, and operations such as updating, reordering, and cropping cached state. A KV cache reuses attention key/value computations from earlier tokens instead of recomputing them at each generation step. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:19-23]()

Sources: `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:19-23`()

## Core abstractions

### Cache and CacheLayerMixin

The cache system separates a model’s cache from the implementation used for an individual layer. `CacheLayerMixin` is the abstract base for a single layer’s cache. It defines the layer-level initialization, update, mask-size, sequence-length, and maximum-length interfaces. Its state includes `keys`, `values`, and `is_initialized`; it also provides shared operations such as `reset`, `offload`, `prefetch`, and `reorder_cache`. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-100]()

`Cache` is the model-level cache abstraction used by generation and model code. The module also defines concrete cache implementations and layer types, including `DynamicLayer` and static and quantized layer variants. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:1-13]()

| Entity | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Cache` | Represents the cache passed between model forward passes and generation. |
| `CacheLayerMixin` | Defines the common interface and shared state for a single cache layer. |
| `DynamicLayer` | Appends new key/value states to dynamically growing tensors. |
| `StaticLayer` | A fixed-capacity layer implementation used by static caches. |
| `DynamicSlidingWindowLayer` / `StaticSlidingWindowLayer` | Sliding-window layer types used by cache implementations. |

The cache layer interface includes `lazy_initialization`, `update`, `get_mask_sizes`, `get_seq_length`, and `get_max_length`. The base mixin also provides `reset`, `reorder_cache`, `offload`, and `prefetch`; concrete layers may provide additional capabilities such as cropping. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-100]()

Sources: `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-100]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-170]`, `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79`()

### Natural-language concepts mapped to code entities

This diagram connects the user-facing choice of cache behavior to the generation and cache classes named in the codebase. `GenerationConfig` lists supported cache implementation names, and `generation.utils` imports cache types used by generation. [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37]()

**Diagram: Cache selection mapped to generation entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Request["Generation request"]
        Strategy["Choose cache strategy"]
        Reuse["Reuse prior token attention state"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Config["GenerationConfig"]
        Names["DYNAMIC_CACHE_IMPLEMENTATIONS"]
        GenUtils["generation/utils.py"]
        Cache["Cache"]
        Dynamic["DynamicCache"]
        Static["StaticCache"]
        Quantized["QuantizedCache"]
    end

    Request --> Strategy
    Strategy --> Config
    Config --> Names
    Config --> GenUtils
    GenUtils --> Cache
    Cache --> Dynamic
    Cache --> Static
    Cache --> Quantized
    Reuse --> Cache
```

Sources: `src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58]`, `src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37`()

## Concrete cache implementations

### DynamicCache

`DynamicCache` is the default cache class described by the cache guide. It grows as generation advances; for models with sliding-window or chunked-attention layers, those layers stop growing once their configured window or chunk limit is reached. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:33-39]()

At layer level, `DynamicLayer` initializes lazily from the first key/value inputs. Its `update` concatenates incoming states to the existing tensors along the sequence dimension (`dim=-2`) and returns the resulting key/value tensors. `get_seq_length` reports the cached sequence dimension, and `get_max_length` returns `-1`, meaning the dynamic layer has no fixed maximum. `DynamicLayer` is marked croppable. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-153]()

Use `use_cache=False` to disable caching for generation, or create a `DynamicCache` and pass it as `past_key_values` when more direct cache control is needed. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:39-66]()

Sources: `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:33-66]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-153`()

### StaticCache

`StaticCache` preallocates a fixed maximum cache size. A fixed shape can support compilation-oriented generation, but unused capacity may cause attention to process masked positions; the trade-off depends on the requested lengths and workload. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:68-76]()

The cache tests exercise `StaticCache` with multi-head attention (MHA), grouped-query attention (GQA), and multi-query attention (MQA), verifying that the allocated key/value head dimension follows the configured number of key/value heads. They also test early initialization and verify that layers which do not support early initialization remain lazily initialized. [tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:101-160]()

The generation configuration names `static` and `offloaded_static` as static cache implementations. [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58]()

Sources: `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:68-76]`, `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:101-160]`, `src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58`()

### QuantizedCache

`QuantizedCache` is a cache implementation intended to reduce memory use by storing cache state in quantized form. The cache guide’s comparison identifies its expected memory use as low and lists it as a dynamic cache implementation. Quantized-layer types in the cache tests include `QuantoQuantizedLayer` and `Fp8QuantizedLayer`; optional dependency checks for HQQ and Optimum Quanto appear in `cache_utils.py`. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:25-30](), [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:7-17](), [tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79]()

The available material identifies quantized cache layers and optional backends, but does not establish a single quantization layout or configuration that applies to every backend. Treat backend and cache configuration as implementation-specific. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:7-17]()

Sources: `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:25-30]`, `src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:7-17]`, `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79`()

### Sliding-window cache layers

Sliding-window behavior is represented by specialized cache layers, including `DynamicSlidingWindowLayer` and `StaticSlidingWindowLayer`. The cache guide notes that, for models using sliding-window attention, the corresponding cache layers stop growing when they reach the window limit. [tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79](), [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:35-38]()

The generation configuration retains names such as `sliding_window` among deprecated static-cache implementation names for backward compatibility. This configuration naming is distinct from the specialized sliding-window layer classes. [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58]()

Sources: `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79]`, `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:35-38]`, `src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58`()

### EncoderDecoderCache

`EncoderDecoderCache` is part of the cache API and is imported by generation utilities. Cache tests import it alongside `DynamicCache` and `StaticCache`, and the ExecuTorch integration imports it together with dynamic and static cache types. These references establish its role in the cache system, but the supplied excerpts do not show its internal fields or detailed update behavior. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [tests/generation/test_utils.py:84-95](), [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:18-26]()

Sources: `src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37]`, `tests/generation/test_utils.py:84-95]`, `src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:18-26`()

## Cache data flow and operations

### Update flow

For a dynamic layer, a cache update lazily initializes storage on the first call, appends the new key and value states along the sequence dimension, and returns the accumulated tensors. The cache interface exposes `update` at the layer level; `DynamicLayer.update` provides the concrete concatenation behavior. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:48-54](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:112-137]()

**Diagram: Update request mapped to cache code**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        Forward["Model forward pass"]
        NewKV["New key/value states"]
        Attend["Attend over cached and new states"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        Interface["CacheLayerMixin.update"]
        Lazy["DynamicLayer.lazy_initialization"]
        DynamicUpdate["DynamicLayer.update"]
        Cat["torch.cat dim=-2"]
        Return["Return keys and values"]
    end

    Forward --> NewKV
    NewKV --> Interface
    Interface --> DynamicUpdate
    DynamicUpdate --> Lazy
    DynamicUpdate --> Cat
    Cat --> Return
    Return --> Attend
```

Sources: `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:48-54]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:112-137`()

### Reordering for beam search

`CacheLayerMixin.reorder_cache` reorders cached state using beam indices. When the cached sequence length is nonzero, it applies `index_select` along batch dimension zero to both keys and values, moving the indices to each tensor’s device first. This aligns cache rows with the beams retained by beam search. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-101]()

Sources: `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-101`()

### Cropping

Cropping is useful when a generation strategy must discard cached tokens, such as when rolling back part of a speculative continuation. `CacheLayerMixin` exposes `is_croppable`, and `DynamicLayer` sets it to `True`. The shown beginning of `DynamicLayer.crop` documents removal of tokens and rejects positive `tokens_to_remove` values; the remainder of the method is not included in the supplied excerpt, so its full slicing semantics are not specified here. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-30](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-110](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:163-170]()

Sources: `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-30]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-110]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:163-170`()

### Reset, offload, and prefetch

The layer mixin provides shared lifecycle operations. `reset` clears initialized key/value tensors and resets a `cumulative_length` attribute when present. `offload` moves initialized keys and values to CPU, while `prefetch` moves them back to the layer’s device when needed. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:71-94]()

Sources: `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:71-94`()

## Cache selection and trade-offs

The generation configuration defines implementation-name groups: static implementations include `static` and `offloaded_static`; dynamic implementations include `dynamic`, `offloaded`, and `quantized`; several older sliding-window and hybrid names are retained as deprecated static implementations. [src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py:46-58]()

The cache guide compares several implementation properties. Dynamic cache is listed as medium memory use and not compile-compatible; static cache is listed as high memory use and compile-compatible; quantized cache is listed as low memory use and not compile-compatible. These are documented expectations, not guarantees for every model, device, or configuration. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:25-30]()

| Cache type | Documented memory expectation | Documented `torch.compile()` support | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Dynamic | Medium | No | Default; grows with generation, with window-limited layers for applicable attention patterns. |
| Static | High | Yes | Fixed capacity; may spend attention computation on masked unused positions. |
| Quantized | Low | No | Uses quantized cache state; backend details vary. |

Sources: `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:25-30]`, `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:33-38]`, `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:68-76`()

The diagram distinguishes the shared single-layer contract from the concrete layer behaviors. It also maps cache choices to the cache classes referenced by generation and tests. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-30](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-153](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37](), [tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79]()

**Diagram: Cache classes and layer implementations**

```mermaid

    }
    class StaticLayer

    class QuantizedCache
    class EncoderDecoderCache

    CacheLayerMixin <|-- DynamicLayer

    CacheLayerMixin <|-- DynamicSlidingWindowLayer
    CacheLayerMixin <|-- StaticSlidingWindowLayer
    Cache --> DynamicCache
    Cache --> StaticCache
    Cache --> QuantizedCache

```

Sources: `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-30]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-153]`, `src/transformers/generation/utils.py:31-37]`, `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py:68-79`()

## Summary

The cache API provides a shared layer contract and multiple storage strategies. `DynamicCache` is the documented default and grows with generation; `StaticCache` reserves a fixed capacity to support compilation-oriented execution; `QuantizedCache` targets lower memory use; and sliding-window layers bound cache growth for compatible attention patterns. Cache layers also expose operations for updating state, tracking sequence lengths, reordering batch entries, and—where supported—cropping cached tokens. [docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:25-38](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-30](), [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-170]()

Sources: `docs/source/en/kv_cache.md:25-38]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:22-30]`, `src/transformers/cache_utils.py:96-170`()

# Page: Logits Processors, Stopping Criteria & Watermarking

# Logits Processors, Stopping Criteria & Watermarking

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes the generation-time controls that adjust next-token scores, decide when generation should stop, and expose generated tokens as they are produced. It covers the `LogitsProcessorList` interface and representative built-in processors, stopping-criteria interfaces and examples, watermarking APIs, and streamers. The supplied source excerpts show the processor and individual stopping-criterion interfaces, but not the implementations of `StoppingCriteriaList`, watermarking, or streamer classes; those areas are therefore described only to the extent supported by the available references. 

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-98](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:48-90](), [tests/generation/test_utils.py:96-112](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:122-128]()

---

## Logits Processors and Warpers

A `LogitsProcessor` receives the current `input_ids` and a scores tensor, then returns processed scores. The scores have shape `(batch_size, vocab_size)` and may be logits or, in beam-search contexts, log probabilities. A `LogitsProcessorList` is a list subclass whose call applies its contained processors in sequence. 

### Core abstractions

| Entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `LogitsProcessor` | Base interface for score transformations. Its `__call__` accepts `input_ids` and `scores`; subclasses implement the transformation. It also declares `supports_continuous_batching`, whose default is `None`. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-60]() |
| `LogitsProcessorList` | Ordered processor container. Its `__call__` passes the current scores through each processor and returns the final tensor. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:63-98]() |
| Processor-specific keyword arguments | The list inspects each processor’s `__call__` signature. If it declares arguments beyond `input_ids` and `scores`, the corresponding values must be present in the list call’s keyword arguments or a `ValueError` is raised. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:86-97]() |

The generation module imports built-in processor and warper classes including `MinLengthLogitsProcessor`, `RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor`, `NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor`, `SuppressTokensLogitsProcessor`, `TemperatureLogitsWarper`, `TopKLogitsWarper`, and `TopPLogitsWarper`. These imports establish their availability to generation, while the detailed implementation of each class is outside the supplied excerpt. 

`MinLengthLogitsProcessor` is shown in detail. It validates that `min_length` is a non-negative integer, normalizes `eos_token_id` to a tensor when needed, and, while the sequence length is below the configured minimum, masks EOS-token scores. For decoder-only generation, the documented length includes the prompt. 

### Representative built-in processors

| Class | Purpose or behavior supported by the supplied source |
|---|---|
| `MinLengthLogitsProcessor` | Prevents EOS selection while the current sequence is shorter than `min_length`. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:101-111](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:154-159]() |
| `RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor` | Imported by generation utilities as a built-in processor. Its implementation is not included in the supplied excerpt. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:83-110]() |
| `NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor` | Imported by generation utilities as a built-in processor. Its implementation is not included in the supplied excerpt. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:83-110]() |
| `SuppressTokensLogitsProcessor` | Imported by generation utilities as a built-in processor. Its implementation is not included in the supplied excerpt. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:83-110]() |
| `TemperatureLogitsWarper`, `TopKLogitsWarper`, `TopPLogitsWarper` | Imported by generation utilities as built-in warpers. Their implementations are not included in the supplied excerpt. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:83-110]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:35-46](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-98](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:101-111](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:142-159](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:83-110]()

### Logits-processing data flow

The diagram maps the natural-language concepts of a prompt and next-token choice to the code-level inputs and interfaces visible in the supplied sources. 

**Diagram: Prompt context to processed next-token scores**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        PromptText["Prompt text"] --> CurrentSeq["Current sequence context"]
        NextToken["Next-token decision"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        InputIds["input_ids"] --> ProcessorList["LogitsProcessorList.__call__"]
        ScoresTensor["scores tensor"] --> ProcessorList["LogitsProcessorList.__call__"]
        ProcessorList["LogitsProcessorList.__call__"] --> ProcessorCall["LogitsProcessor.__call__"]
        ProcessorCall["LogitsProcessor.__call__"] --> ProcessedScores["processed scores"]
    end
    CurrentSeq --> InputIds
    ProcessedScores --> NextToken
```

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:35-46](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-68](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:70-98]()

### Ordered application and extra arguments

`LogitsProcessorList.__call__` walks the list in order, replacing `scores` with the output of each processor. A processor that needs extra inputs can declare them in its `__call__` signature; the list checks that those names are present in the supplied keyword arguments before invoking it. 

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:70-98]()

---

## Stopping Criteria

A `StoppingCriteria` is an abstract interface for deciding whether generation should stop. Its call receives `input_ids`, optional generation `scores`, and additional keyword arguments, and returns a boolean tensor with one stop flag per batch row. 

### Concrete criteria

| Class | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `MaxLengthCriteria` | Stops when the current sequence length is greater than or equal to `max_length`. Decoder-only sequence length includes the prompt. If `max_position_embeddings` is provided, it can also issue a warning when generation exceeds that model limit. [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:62-90]() |
| `MaxTimeCriteria` | Stops when elapsed time since its initial timestamp exceeds `max_time`. If no timestamp is supplied, initialization uses the current time. [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:93-115]() |
| `StopStringCriteria` | Stops when a generated token completes one of the configured stop strings at the end of the sequence. Its documented matching accounts for tokenization overhangs, where the string spans token boundaries or extends beyond the final token’s text. [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:118-149]() |

The generation utilities import `StoppingCriteria`, `StoppingCriteriaList`, `MaxLengthCriteria`, `MaxTimeCriteria`, `EosTokenCriteria`, `StopStringCriteria`, and `ConfidenceCriteria`. 

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:111-119](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:22-149]()

### Stopping-criteria data flow

Each criterion evaluates the current sequence and optional scores, and returns boolean stop flags.

**Diagram: Generation state to stop decision**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        GeneratedText["Generated text so far"]
        StopCondition["Stop condition reached"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        InputIds["input_ids"] --> StoppingCall["StoppingCriteria.__call__"]
        ScoresOpt["scores or None"] --> StoppingCall["StoppingCriteria.__call__"]
        MaxLengthCrit["MaxLengthCriteria.__call__"]
        MaxTimeCrit["MaxTimeCriteria.__call__"]
        StopStringCrit["StopStringCriteria.__call__"]
        StoppingCall --> StopFlags["BoolTensor stop flags"]
    end
    GeneratedText --> InputIds
    StopFlags --> StopCondition
```

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:22-59](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:62-90](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:93-115](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:118-149]()

### Stop strings and tokenization

`StopStringCriteria` identifies a stop string when completed by the latest generated token. The criterion module maintains a module-level `STOP_STRING_EMBEDDING_CACHE` for stop-string embedding vectors. 

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:17-20](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:118-149]()

## Summary

- `LogitsProcessor` defines the score-transform interface; `LogitsProcessorList` applies processors in sequence and validates required processor-specific arguments. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-98]()
- `MinLengthLogitsProcessor` masks EOS scores until the configured minimum sequence length is reached. [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:101-111](), [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:142-159]()
- `StoppingCriteria` returns per-row boolean stop flags; visible concrete criteria cover maximum length, elapsed time, and stop strings. [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:48-59](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:62-149]()
- The tests import `WatermarkingConfig`, `SynthIDTextWatermarkingConfig`, and `WatermarkDetector`. [tests/generation/test_utils.py:96-112]()
- `BaseStreamer` appears as a type-only reference in generation utilities. [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:122-128]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py:49-159](), [src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py:48-149](), [tests/generation/test_utils.py:96-112](), [src/transformers/generation/utils.py:122-128]()

# Page: Continuous Batching

# Continuous Batching

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/benchmark_v2.yml](.github/workflows/benchmark_v2.yml)
- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## 1. Purpose and Scope

Continuous batching combines generation requests into changing batches so requests can be scheduled and executed together. This page documents the implementation areas represented in the supplied source: request and output state, scheduling interfaces, paged KV-cache organization, static model inputs, model execution, configuration resolution, and distributed coordination. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:72-85](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/requests.py:49-86](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:23-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:70-98](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-78](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:52-64]()

The implementation separates scheduling and request lifecycle from device-side model execution. `Scheduler` selects work under token and cache budgets, `ContinuousBatchingIOs` prepares model inputs, and `ModelRunner` executes a forward pass and processes logits. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:63-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:81-105](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:126-145]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:72-85](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/requests.py:49-86](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:23-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:70-98](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-105](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:52-64]()

---

## 2. Continuous Batching API Overview

`continuous_api.py` imports the cache, scheduler, I/O, model-runner, offloading, distributed, and request abstractions used by the continuous-batching API. The file defines `ProtoPretrainedModel`, an `nn.Module` interface requiring `set_attn_implementation` and `_get_logits_processor`. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:32-48](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:72-85]()

`OutputRouter` routes each `GenerationOutput` to a per-request asynchronous callback when one is registered, using `call_soon_threadsafe`; otherwise it places the output on a shared `queue.Queue`. `deliver_batch` collects registered callbacks for batched dispatch and places outputs without handlers on the queue. `fail_and_deliver` marks a `RequestState` failed, stores the error text, and routes its output. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:87-108](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:110-138]()

The request lifecycle uses `RequestStatus` values `PENDING`, `PREFILLING`, `DECODING`, `FINISHED`, and `FAILED`. `GenerationOutput` holds request identity, prompt and generated tokens, log probabilities, status, error information, and timing fields. `RequestState` holds prompt-processing and generation state, including `tokens_to_process`, `generated_tokens`, `position_offset`, and allocated cache blocks. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/requests.py:49-86](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/requests.py:89-141]()

### Request-to-output mapping

**Diagram 1 — User request mapped to API entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    User["User submits generation request"] --> Manager["ContinuousBatchingManager"]
    Manager --> State["RequestState"]
    State --> Scheduler["Scheduler"]
    Scheduler --> Runner["ModelRunner"]
    Runner --> Output["GenerationOutput"]
    Output --> Router["OutputRouter"]
    Router -->|"registered callback"| AsyncLoop["asyncio event loop"]
    Router -->|"no callback"| Queue["output_queue"]
```

This diagram maps request handling concepts to named code entities: `RequestState` represents request data, `Scheduler` defines batch selection, `ModelRunner` is the device-execution entry point, and `OutputRouter` provides output destinations. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/requests.py:89-141](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:23-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:52-64](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:87-138]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:32-48](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:72-138](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/requests.py:49-141](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:23-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:52-64]()

---

## 3. Request Scheduling Subsystem

`Scheduler` is the abstract base class for request scheduling. It retains active and waiting request maps, a waiting-order deque, cancellation state, requests to fork, and requests that were starved during cache allocation. Its `schedule_batch` interface accepts token and cache budgets and returns scheduled `FutureRequestState` items, a decode-fast-path flag, the query-token total, and the maximum KV read size. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:23-72]()

`add_waiting_request` adds the request to the waiting map and appends its ID to the order deque. `finish_request` frees the request’s cache blocks and removes it from the active map. Cancellation requests are recorded under a lock; `clear_cancelled_requests` removes matching requests from active and waiting state and frees their cache blocks. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:47-61](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:78-111]()

The scheduler’s `safety_margin` defines a threshold for stopping admission of new prefill requests as free cache blocks become scarce. The base class validates that the margin is between zero and one and that `max_requests_per_batch` is at least one. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:30-45]()

When prefix sharing is enabled, `_infer_request_tokens` searches for a prefix match for a pending request that is not CPU-offloaded. A successful match promotes the request into active scheduling state and removes it from waiting state. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:119-129]()

The module defines `FIFOScheduler` and `SCHEDULER_MAPPING`; the supplied source excerpt does not show their implementation or the mapping entries, so strategy-specific behavior is not inferred here. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:46-48]()

### Scheduling data flow

**Diagram 2 — Scheduler entities and cache-budget path**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Waiting["waiting_requests"] --> Schedule["Scheduler.schedule_batch"]
    Active["active_requests"] --> Schedule
    Cancel["_requests_to_cancel"] --> Clear["Scheduler.clear_cancelled_requests"]
    Clear --> Free["PagedAttentionCache.free_blocks"]
    Schedule -->|"token_budget and cache_budget"| Batch["FutureRequestState batch"]
    Schedule --> Cache["PagedAttentionCache"]
    Cache -->|"allocation availability"| Schedule
    Batch --> IO["ContinuousBatchingIOs"]
```

The diagram associates the natural-language scheduling workflow with the actual queue, method, state, and cache names used by the scheduler and I/O classes. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:47-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:96-111](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:81-105]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:23-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:78-129](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:46-48](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:81-105]()

---

## 4. Paged KV Cache Management

### Cache hierarchy and attention groups

`PagedAttentionCache` owns the cache tensors and coordinates cache sectors among sub-allocators. Its documentation describes a hierarchy of layer-level pages, request-level blocks, and attention-type-level sectors. Allocators manage blocks; the top-level cache coordinates sectors. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:70-98]()

`group_layers_by_attn_type` groups layers using `config.layer_types` when available. Without that field, it treats all layers as sliding attention if `sliding_window` is configured, and otherwise treats them as full attention. The `ATTN_TYPE_TO_ALLOCATOR` mapping associates `FULL_ATTENTION` and `SLIDING_ATTENTION` with their allocator classes. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:37-67]()

The cache documentation explains why sectors are needed: allocators for different attention types can require different block sizes. Sector sizing allows multiple allocator block layouts to share the cache tensor while growing at compatible rates. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:84-108]()

### Cache entities and storage relationship

**Diagram 3 — `PagedAttentionCache` allocation structure**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Cache["PagedAttentionCache"] --> Sector["sector"]
    Sector --> Full["FullAttentionCacheAllocator"]
    Sector --> Sliding["SlidingAttentionCacheAllocator"]
    Full --> BlockFull["full-attention blocks"]
    Sliding --> BlockSliding["sliding-attention blocks"]
    BlockFull --> Tensor["flat cache tensor"]
    BlockSliding --> Tensor
    Config["PreTrainedConfig"] --> Group["group_layers_by_attn_type"]
    Group --> Cache
```

This diagram links attention types and allocator names to the cache’s documented sector, block, and tensor organization. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:37-41](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:44-67](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:70-108]()

### Allocation behavior

The cache module imports `FullAttentionCacheAllocator` and `SlidingAttentionCacheAllocator` and uses them as the allocator types for the two supported attention groups. The scheduler calls `cache.free_blocks(request_id)` when finishing or cancelling a request. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:24-41](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:78-83](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:96-110]()

The cache constructor receives the model configuration, continuous-batching configuration, target device, distributed helper, dtype, and a flag indicating model support for logits-to-keep behavior. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:118-134]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:37-108](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:118-134](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:78-110]()

---

## 5. Model Execution, I/O, and Static Tensor Management

### `ContinuousBatchingIOs`

`ContinuousBatchingIOs` owns inputs and outputs for a forward pass and is designed to update a batch using static tensor storage. Its initialization retains the cache, device, model configuration and dtype, request limit, graph setting, and logits-processing configuration. It also tracks query-token and KV-read sizes, requests in the batch, and whether the block-table path is active. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:81-129]()

`PagedAttentionArgs` documents the forward-pass data contract: input and position IDs, cumulative query and key sequence lengths, maximum lengths, cache read/write indices, logits indices, the `PagedAttentionCache`, optional block table, and logits-processor arguments. It specifies that continuous batching manages the cache externally and supplies `use_cache=False`. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-78]()

The I/O class allocates static tensors during initialization through `_setup_static_tensors` and resets them for use. On non-CPU devices it may create a compute stream. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:125-129]()

### `ModelRunner`

`ModelRunner` is described as the continuous-batching entry point for model execution, with device work intended to happen through this class. Its configuration determines whether to pad inputs and whether compiled forward paths are constructed for variable-length and decode execution. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:52-99]()

`maybe_pad_inputs` leaves dimensions unchanged when padding is disabled. When enabled, variable-length batches use configured query and KV intervals; decode-fast-path batches pad the query count to a power of two and set KV read length to zero. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:101-116]()

`compute_batch` obtains I/O tensors, optionally passes `logits_to_keep` to models that support it, selects a forward function, and invokes it on the compute stream when CUDA graphs are not in use. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:118-145]()

### End-to-end execution mapping

**Diagram 4 — Scheduled batch mapped to model inputs and execution**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Scheduler["Scheduler.schedule_batch"] --> Futures["FutureRequestState items"]
    Futures --> IO["ContinuousBatchingIOs"]
    Cache["PagedAttentionCache"] --> IO
    IO --> Args["PagedAttentionArgs"]
    Args --> Runner["ModelRunner.compute_batch"]
    Runner --> Forward["forward function"]
    Forward --> Logits["logits and next-token processing"]
```

The I/O contract and `ModelRunner.compute_batch` connect scheduled request state and paged-cache metadata to the model forward pass. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:63-72](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-78](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:126-145]()

### Graph padding and capture

The continuous-batching API documents fixed-size query and KV padding intervals as a way to constrain changing dimensions for CUDA graphs. `pad_to_interval` rounds a size up to an interval multiple, capped by a maximum; `ModelRunner.maybe_pad_inputs` applies the configured intervals on the variable-length path. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:51-68](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:92-98](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:101-116]()

`CudaGraphBuffer` stores graphs by tuple-shaped keys and resets stored graphs during destruction. `ContinuousBatchingIOs` owns a `CudaGraphBuffer` for graphs associated with its static inputs and outputs. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:55-71](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:121-127]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-129](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/model_runner.py:52-145](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:51-68](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:55-98](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/scheduler.py:63-72]()

---

## 6. Attention Backends and Offloading

### Paged attention arguments and backend selection

The forward argument documentation describes an optional `block_table`: when supplied, it uses `flash_attn_with_kvcache` for fused attention and cache update. It also documents `is_causal` behavior: SDPA and eager use a custom mask, while flash attention uses causal behavior without an explicit mask. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-62]()

The utility `attn_mask_is_needed` identifies `paged|eager` and `sdpa` as implementations needing an attention mask. The `build_attention_mask` documentation describes block-diagonal per-request masks formed from causal and optional sliding-window masks. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:87-90](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:115-125]()

The supplied source excerpts do not include the implementations of the `flash_paged` or `sdpa_paged` integration modules. Consequently, this page limits backend details to the argument contract and mask behavior documented in the available files. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-62](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:87-90]()

| Backend-related code name | What the supplied source establishes |
|---|---|
| `flash_attn_with_kvcache` | The optional block-table path is documented as using it for fused attention and cache update. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:56-58]() |
| `sdpa` | `attn_mask_is_needed` identifies it as requiring a mask; the forward-argument documentation describes SDPA as using a custom mask rather than causal mode. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:87-90](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:60-62]() |
| `paged|eager` | `attn_mask_is_needed` identifies this implementation name as requiring an attention mask. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:87-90]() |

### Offloading

`continuous_api.py` imports `OffloadingManager`, establishing it as a component of the continuous-batching API module. The available source does not show the manager’s implementation or call sites, so its offloading policy and data movement are not detailed here. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:43-48]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/input_outputs.py:40-62](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:87-90](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/utils.py:115-125](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:43-48]()

---

## 7. Configuration Resolution

`resolve_continuous_batching_config` deep-copies the supplied configuration and resolves it in a defined order: workload-hint values, fallback values, decode-fast-path availability, compile settings, CUDA-graph settings, asynchronous batching, memory percentage, and bounds checks. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/initialization.py:43-95]()

The fallback constants shown include `max_requests_per_batch`, `max_blocks_per_request`, `q_padding_interval_size`, and `kv_padding_interval_size`. Workload hints can determine a request’s block limit from the maximum prompt plus generated length and the configured page size, and can set the request batch limit. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/initialization.py:32-36](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/initialization.py:98-113]()

Decode-fast-path availability depends on whether every attention type returned by `group_layers_by_attn_type` has an allocator that supports block tables. If any type does not support that path, configuration resolution disables it unless the user explicitly requested it, in which case the shown code logs a warning. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/initialization.py:128-139]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/initialization.py:32-95](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/initialization.py:98-139](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/cache.py:37-67]()

---

## 8. Distributed Coordination and Async Management

`DistributedHelper` records whether distributed execution is initialized, holds the device mesh and tensor-parallel plan, and derives rank and mesh information. It rejects an FSDP mesh dimension of size greater than one and identifies a tensor-parallel mesh when present. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/distributed.py:39-59](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/distributed.py:96-120]()

The tensor-parallel driver is the rank whose local TP rank is zero. `tp_broadcast_from_rank_0` broadcasts a tensor within the TP group, and `tp_all_reduce_state` combines payload size, stop status, and pause requests using a max reduction on the CPU communication group. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/distributed.py:85-94](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/distributed.py:122-148]()

`BackgroundThreadStatus` defines increasing stop states (`DONT_STOP`, `FLUSH_AND_STOP`, `HARD_STOP`, and `STOPPED`) and tracks pause requests. These fields support coordinating stop and pause behavior for the background generation loop. [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:141-160]()

Sources: [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/distributed.py:39-59](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/distributed.py:85-148](), [src/transformers/generation/continuous_batching/continuous_api.py:141-160]()

---

## 9. Testing and Benchmarking

`tests/generation/test_continuous_batching.py` imports the manager, cache, allocators, scheduler-related state, distributed helper, I/O mask helper, offloading manager, and paged-attention reference function. These imports identify the continuous-batching components covered by that test module; the supplied excerpt does not include individual test cases. [tests/generation/test_continuous_batching.py:43-73]()

The benchmark script `continuous_batching_overall.py` describes an in-process benchmark suite covering task workloads, synthetic data, and rollout-style workloads, with results including generation time, wall-clock time, token throughput, peak memory, and optional accuracy. [benchmark_v2/benchmark_scripts/continuous_batching_overall.py:1-9]()

Sources: [tests/generation/test_continuous_batching.py:43-73](), [benchmark_v2/benchmark_scripts/continuous_batching_overall.py:1-9]()

# Training

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [README.md](README.md)

## Purpose and scope

Transformers’ training infrastructure provides a high-level workflow for training and fine-tuning models. This parent page maps the main components—`Trainer`, `TrainingArguments`, callbacks, optimization, and data utilities—to their roles; child pages cover implementation and usage details. [src/transformers/trainer.py:14-16]()

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:14-16]()

## Core Infrastructure

`Trainer` coordinates training and uses components for data batching, callbacks, optimization, and distributed execution. `TrainingArguments` centralizes training configuration, including optimization settings and infrastructure choices. [src/transformers/trainer.py:53-57]()[src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100]()[src/transformers/training_args.py:179-187]()

The overall relationship is: arguments configure the trainer; data utilities provide batches; callbacks and optimization components support the run. For details on training loops, evaluation, prediction, checkpointing, and configuration strategies, see [Trainer & TrainingArguments](#6.1).

### Trainer System Orchestration Diagram

```mermaid
title "Trainer System Orchestration"
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural_Language_Space"
        TA["TrainingArguments"]
        T["Trainer"]
        CB["CallbackHandler"]
        DC["DataCollator"]
        OPT["OptimizerContext"]
    end

    subgraph "Code_Entity_Space"
        TA_FILE["src/transformers/training_args.py"]
        T_FILE["src/transformers/trainer.py"]
        OPT_FILE["src/transformers/trainer_optimizer.py"]
        DC_FILE["src/transformers/data/data_collator.py"]
    end

    TA --> T
    T --> CB
    T --> DC
    T --> OPT
    TA --> TA_FILE
    T --> T_FILE
    OPT --> OPT_FILE
    DC --> DC_FILE
```

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100]()[src/transformers/training_args.py:179-187]()

## Callbacks, Optimizers & Schedulers

Callbacks provide extension points managed by `CallbackHandler`; the trainer also imports its default flow and progress callbacks. Optimizer identifiers are represented by `OptimizerNames`, while the trainer imports optimizer support and scheduler utilities. [src/transformers/trainer.py:85-100]()[src/transformers/trainer.py:186-192]()[src/transformers/training_args.py:113-160]()

These components separate training-event handling from optimization configuration. For callback types, optimizer choices, and scheduler details, see [Callbacks, Optimizers & Schedulers](#6.2).

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:85-100]()[src/transformers/trainer.py:186-192]()[src/transformers/training_args.py:113-160]()

## Data Collators & Datasets

The trainer accepts map-style and iterable datasets, and imports collator interfaces including `DataCollator`, `DataCollatorWithPadding`, and `default_data_collator`. Its PyTorch utilities include sampler and nested-batch helpers used around data loading and evaluation. [src/transformers/trainer.py:53-57]()[src/transformers/trainer.py:102-119]()[src/transformers/trainer_pt_utils.py:65-70]()

Collators and dataset handling connect input preprocessing to the training loop. For data collator classes, task-specific preprocessing, and argument parsing, see [Data Collators & Datasets](#6.3).

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:53-57]()[src/transformers/trainer.py:102-119]()[src/transformers/trainer_pt_utils.py:65-70]()

## Training Examples & Scripts

The `examples/` child page covers practical training workflows, including Trainer-based and no-trainer scripts, modular-transformers examples, and specialized quantization and scheduler examples. The trainer imports Accelerate components when available, reflecting its integration with accelerator-backed execution. [src/transformers/trainer.py:218-220]()

For script layouts and examples, see [Training Examples & Scripts](#6.4).

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:218-220]()

## Quantization-Aware Training & Fine-Tuning

Training utilities include `validate_quantization_for_training`, which checks conditions around quantized models, adapter configuration, and quantizer training support. In particular, it rejects certain compiled quantized models and purely quantized models without trainable adapters, subject to the checks implemented in the utility. [src/transformers/trainer_utils.py:102-143]()

This validation is one point of contact between training and the broader quantization and PEFT systems. For quantization backends, see [Quantization](#7); for adapter fine-tuning, see [PEFT & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning](#11.1).

        QM["Quantized model"]
        AD["Trainable adapters"]
        V["Training validation"]
    end

        TU["src/transformers/trainer_utils.py"]
    end

`Trainer` is presented as a high-level class for training or fine-tuning Transformers models. Its imports show the principal components it brings together: PyTorch data loaders, datasets, data collators, `TrainingArguments`, callback types, optimizer helpers, scheduler construction, evaluation output types, and utilities for distributed and checkpoint-related work. The available excerpt shows these dependencies, but not how individual methods call them. ## TrainingArguments

`TrainingArguments` is a dataclass described in its source as the configuration class for controlling model training with `Trainer`. Its documentation states that it centralizes hyperparameters, optimization settings, logging preferences, and infrastructure choices, and that `HfArgumentParser` can convert it into command-line arguments. The provided excerpt shows the class declaration and its documented purpose, but not the complete field definitions or validation behavior. [src/transformers/training_args.py:179-187]()

### Configuration Structure

`TrainingArguments` imports strategy types for evaluation intervals, saving, scheduling, and FSDP configuration. It also defines `OptimizerNames`, an explicit enumeration of optimizer identifiers, including PyTorch AdamW variants, Adafactor, SGD, Adagrad, and other optimizer options. [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]() [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-158]()

| Configuration area | Identifiers visible in the provided source |
|---|---|
| Optimizer selection | `OptimizerNames`, including `ADAMW_TORCH`, `ADAFACTOR`, `SGD`, and `ADAGRAD`. [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-158]() |
| Evaluation and logging intervals | `IntervalStrategy` is imported for use by training configuration. [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]() |
| Checkpoint saving | `SaveStrategy` is imported. [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]() |
| Scheduler selection | `SchedulerType` is imported. [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]() |
| FSDP configuration | `FSDPOption` is imported. [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]() |
| Parallel execution | `ParallelMode` is imported by `Trainer` from `training_args.py`; its definition is outside the supplied excerpt. [src/transformers/trainer.py:152-152]() |

The provided excerpt does not show the field declarations for common hyperparameters or strategies, so their exact defaults and interactions are not specified here. [src/transformers/training_args.py:179-190]()

# Page: Callbacks, Optimizers & Schedulers

# Callbacks, Optimizers & Schedulers

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes how `Trainer` connects training-loop events to callbacks, selects optimizers, and configures learning-rate schedulers. It focuses on the callback lifecycle and the code entities that connect these mechanisms to `TrainingArguments` and `Trainer`. [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100]()

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100]()

---

## Callback System

Callbacks let code observe and influence parts of the `Trainer` lifecycle without replacing the training loop. `TrainerCallback` defines lifecycle hooks, `CallbackHandler` dispatches events to the registered callbacks, and `TrainerControl` carries control flags used by the loop. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]()

### Core classes

| Entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `TrainerCallback` | Base class for callback hooks invoked during training, evaluation, prediction, logging, saving, and optimizer-related events. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]() |
| `CallbackHandler` | Holds the active callbacks and dispatches lifecycle events to them. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]() |
| `TrainerState` | Carries loop state, including progress and history, for the trainer and its callbacks. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]() |
| `TrainerControl` | Carries control requests such as whether to log, evaluate, save, or stop training. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]() |

Callbacks receive the arguments, state, and current control object at each hook. A callback can inspect state and update control flags; the trainer then uses those flags to determine requested loop actions. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]()

### Callback execution flow

**Diagram: lifecycle event dispatch**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Trainer as "Trainer"
    participant Handler as "CallbackHandler"
    participant Callback as "TrainerCallback"
    participant State as "TrainerState"
    participant Control as "TrainerControl"

    Trainer->>Handler: "dispatch lifecycle event"
    Handler->>Callback: "invoke matching hook"
    Callback->>State: "inspect progress and history"
    Callback->>Control: "update requested control flags"
    Handler-->>Trainer: "return updated control"
    Trainer->>Trainer: "apply requested loop actions"
```

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115](), [src/transformers/trainer.py:85-94]()

### Trainer integration

`Trainer` imports and uses `CallbackHandler`, `TrainerCallback`, `TrainerControl`, and `TrainerState`. Its default callback list includes `DefaultFlowCallback`; the progress callback defaults to `ProgressCallback`, with a notebook-specific progress callback selected when the runtime is in a notebook. [src/transformers/trainer.py:85-94] [src/transformers/trainer.py:186-192]()

The callback system is separate from the optimizer selection mechanism: callbacks receive lifecycle events, while `Trainer` imports optimizer construction helpers and scheduler selection separately. [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100]()

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100](), [src/transformers/trainer.py:186-192]()

---

## Built-in Callbacks

The callback base class provides hooks for initialization, training, epochs, steps, optimizer steps, evaluation, prediction, saving, and logging. Concrete callbacks can implement the hooks relevant to their purpose. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]()

| Callback | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DefaultFlowCallback` | Supplies the default flow-control behavior used by `Trainer`. It is included in `DEFAULT_CALLBACKS`. [src/transformers/trainer.py:186-187]() |
| `ProgressCallback` | Provides progress reporting; it is the default progress callback outside notebooks. [src/transformers/trainer.py:186-192]() |
| `NotebookProgressCallback` | Notebook-specific progress reporting, selected when `is_in_notebook()` is true. [src/transformers/trainer.py:189-192]() |
| `EarlyStoppingCallback` | Stops training when the configured evaluation metric does not improve according to its patience and threshold settings. [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]() |
| `TensorBoardCallback` | Reports training information to TensorBoard when a supported TensorBoard package is available. Availability is checked by `is_tensorboard_available()`. [src/transformers/integrations/integration_utils.py:149-151]() |
| `WandbCallback` | Integrates training reporting with Weights & Biases; `is_wandb_available()` checks for an importable package with a `run` attribute. [src/transformers/integrations/integration_utils.py:104-112]() |

Reporting integrations are connected to `Trainer` through `get_reporting_integration_callbacks`, which `Trainer` imports from the integrations package. The callback classes and their runtime behavior are implemented in the callback and integration modules. [src/transformers/trainer.py:38-43] [src/transformers/trainer.py:85-94] [src/transformers/integrations/integration_utils.py:97-112]()

Sources: [src/transformers/trainer.py:38-43](), [src/transformers/trainer.py:85-94](), [src/transformers/trainer.py:186-192](), [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115](), [src/transformers/integrations/integration_utils.py:97-112](), [src/transformers/integrations/integration_utils.py:149-151]()

## Optimizers

`TrainingArguments.optim` selects an optimizer by an identifier represented by `OptimizerNames`. The enum includes PyTorch AdamW variants, Adafactor, and several optional or specialized optimizer choices. [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-158]()

`Trainer` imports optimizer-related helpers from `trainer_optimizer.py`, including `_OPTIMIZER_HANDLERS`, `OptimizerContext`, `_parse_optim_args`, and `is_optimizer_factory`. These provide the connection between optimizer configuration and optimizer construction. [src/transformers/trainer.py:95-101]()

### Selected optimizer identifiers

| Identifier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `adamw_torch` | PyTorch AdamW option. [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-123]() |
| `adamw_torch_fused` | Fused PyTorch AdamW option. [src/transformers/training_args.py:118-123]() |
| `adafactor` | Adafactor option. [src/transformers/training_args.py:118-124]() |
| `adamw_bnb_8bit` / `adamw_8bit` | 8-bit AdamW identifiers; `adamw_8bit` is marked as an alias of `adamw_bnb_8bit`. [src/transformers/training_args.py:125-130]() |
| `galore_adamw` | GaLore AdamW option. [src/transformers/training_args.py:140-149]() |
| `lomo` / `adalomo` | LOMO-family identifiers. [src/transformers/training_args.py:149-152]() |

The enum also includes additional implementations and variants, such as SGD, Adagrad, RMSprop, Lion, schedule-free optimizers, and hardware- or integration-specific AdamW options. Availability and requirements can depend on optional dependencies and the chosen configuration. [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-158] [src/transformers/utils/import_utils.py:165-168]()

Sources: [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-158](), [src/transformers/trainer.py:95-101](), [src/transformers/utils/import_utils.py:165-168]()

### Optimizer selection and construction

**Diagram: optimizer configuration to trainer helper entities**

## Learning Rate Schedulers

`Trainer` imports `get_scheduler` and `GreedyLR` from `optimization.py`. Scheduler selection is connected to training arguments through `SchedulerType`, which is imported into `training_args.py` from `trainer_utils.py`. [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-83] [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]()

The scheduler implementation module provides scheduler construction and schedule functions; `get_scheduler` is the central factory used by the trainer. The available schedule names and their parameter requirements are defined by the scheduler enum and optimization implementation. [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-83] [src/transformers/training_args.py:28-34]()

### Scheduler data flow

**Diagram: scheduler configuration and factory path**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Arguments["TrainingArguments"]
    SchedulerType["SchedulerType"]
    Trainer["Trainer"]
    Factory["get_scheduler"]
    Schedule["learning-rate schedule"]
    Optimizer["optimizer"]

    Arguments --> SchedulerType
    Trainer --> Factory
    SchedulerType --> Factory
    Factory --> Schedule
    Schedule --> Optimizer
```

## End-to-end training subsystem map

The trainer connects callback dispatch, optimizer construction, and scheduler selection as distinct mechanisms. Callbacks receive lifecycle events and can request control actions; optimizer identifiers and arguments feed optimizer helpers; scheduler configuration is passed to `get_scheduler`. [src/transformers/trainer.py:82-100] [src/transformers/training_args.py:113-158] [src/transformers/trainer_callback.py:34-115]()

# Page: Data Collators & Datasets

# Data Collators & Datasets

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes the data-collation interface and the implementation details visible in the provided source: dispatching batches to PyTorch or NumPy, default collation, and tests for basic batching and input immutability. The supplied excerpts do not show the implementations of the specialized collators, dataset preprocessing utilities, processor classes, or `HfArgumentParser`; those topics cannot be documented in implementation detail from these sources. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:28-168]()

Sources: [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:28-168]()

---

## Data Collator Architecture

A data collator is a callable that accepts a list of dataset samples and returns a batch dictionary. The `DataCollator` type alias expresses that contract; the module documentation describes the result as PyTorch tensors or NumPy arrays. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:30-34]()

`DataCollatorMixin.__call__` selects a framework-specific method. If its `return_tensors` argument is omitted, it uses the collator instance’s `return_tensors` attribute. The shown dispatch supports `"pt"` through `torch_call` and `"np"` through `numpy_call`; other values raise `ValueError`. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:37-46]()

### Data Collator Call Dispatch

```mermaid
graph TD
  Features["list of dataset samples"] --> Mixin["DataCollatorMixin.__call__"]
  Mixin --> Default["use self.return_tensors when argument is None"]
  Default --> Framework{"return_tensors"}
  Framework -->|"pt"| Torch["torch_call(features)"]
  Framework -->|"np"| NumPy["numpy_call(features)"]
  Framework -->|"other"| Error["ValueError"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:37-46]()

### Padding helper

`pad_without_fast_tokenizer_warning` delegates to `tokenizer.pad`. If the tokenizer has no `deprecation_warnings` attribute, it calls `pad` directly. Otherwise, it temporarily suppresses the `"Asking-to-pad-a-fast-tokenizer"` warning state while padding, then restores the prior state in a `finally` block. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:49-68]()

This helper is a padding wrapper, not a batch-collator class. The excerpt establishes its behavior but does not show which specialized collators call it. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:49-68]()

Sources: [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:49-68]()

---

## Default Data Collation

`default_data_collator` is the function-based entry point for basic batching. It routes `"pt"` to `torch_default_data_collator` and `"np"` to `numpy_default_data_collator`. The excerpt shows no additional branch for other values in this function. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:71-92]()

`DefaultDataCollator` is the object-based alternative. It inherits from `DataCollatorMixin`, defines a `return_tensors` field defaulting to `"pt"`, and delegates its call to `default_data_collator`, using the instance default when no per-call override is supplied. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:94-120]()

The PyTorch implementation assumes the batch’s samples share the same attributes and uses the first sample to determine which keys to process. Non-mapping samples are converted with `vars`. For labels, a scalar `"label"` becomes `"labels"` with integer values represented as `torch.long` and other values as `torch.float`; `"label_ids"` is stacked if already a tensor, or tensorized with an inferred integer or floating dtype. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:122-142]()

For other keys, the PyTorch implementation skips `"label"` and `"label_ids"`, ignores `None` and strings, stacks tensor values, stacks NumPy arrays before converting them to tensors, and tensorizes other values. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:144-155]()

### Natural language to code: default collation

The conceptual operation “combine samples into a model batch” maps to `default_data_collator`, which selects a backend-specific implementation. The shown PyTorch path maps label fields to the model-facing `"labels"` key and converts eligible remaining fields into batched tensors. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:71-92]()[src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:122-155]()

```mermaid
graph TD
  Samples["list of dataset samples"] --> Entry["default_data_collator"]
  Entry --> Backend{"return_tensors"}
  Backend -->|"pt"| TorchFunc["torch_default_data_collator"]
  Backend -->|"np"| NumPyFunc["numpy_default_data_collator"]
  TorchFunc --> First["inspect first sample keys"]
  First --> Labels["label or label_ids to labels"]
  First --> Other["stack or tensorize eligible fields"]
  Labels --> Batch["batched dictionary"]
  Other --> Batch
```

Sources: [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:71-92](), [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:122-155]()

### Collation flow through the object interface

For the object form, the data flow is `DefaultDataCollator.__call__` → `default_data_collator` → backend-specific function. The mixin also provides framework dispatch for collators that implement `torch_call` and `numpy_call`; the excerpt does not show the implementations of those methods for the specialized collators. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:37-46]()[src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:94-120]()

```mermaid
graph LR
  FeatureList["features"] --> ObjectCall["DefaultDataCollator.__call__"]
  ObjectCall --> Function["default_data_collator"]
  Function --> Backend{"return_tensors"}
  Backend -->|"pt"| Torch["torch_default_data_collator"]
  Backend -->|"np"| NumPy["numpy_default_data_collator"]
  Torch --> Output["batch dictionary"]
  NumPy --> Output
```

Sources: [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:94-120](), [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:71-92]()

## Testing and Input Immutability

`DataCollatorTestMixin` creates a temporary vocabulary file for its test setup and provides `_check_immutability`. That helper deep-copies features, invokes the collator on the original features, then compares each original field with its post-call value. It handles NumPy arrays and, when PyTorch is available, tensors by comparing their list representations. [tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:53-80]()

The default-collator tests exercise dictionary batching, `"label"` and `"label_ids"` handling, NumPy-array inputs, tensor labels, integer-versus-float dtype inference, omission of `None` labels, and NumPy output. The tested PyTorch examples expect integer labels to use `torch.long`, floating labels to use `torch.float`, and batched inputs to have a leading batch dimension. [tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:87-171]()

### Sample test coverage mapped to code entities

```mermaid
graph TD
  TestSuite["tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py"] --> Mixin["DataCollatorTestMixin"]
  Mixin --> Setup["setUp: temporary vocabulary"]
  Mixin --> Check["._check_immutability"]
  TestSuite --> DefaultTests["TestDefaultDataCollator"]
  DefaultTests --> Entry["default_data_collator"]
  Entry --> Implementation["torch_default_data_collator"]
  DefaultTests --> Coverage["labels, arrays, dtype, None labels, NumPy output"]
```

Sources: [tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:53-80](), [tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:82-171](), [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:71-92](), [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:122-155]()

## Summary

- `DataCollator` defines the sample-list-to-batch-dictionary contract. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:30-34]()
- `DataCollatorMixin` dispatches to PyTorch or NumPy methods using `return_tensors`. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:37-46]()
- `default_data_collator` and `DefaultDataCollator` provide function and object entry points for basic collation. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:71-120]()
- The shown PyTorch implementation handles `"label"` and `"label_ids"` specially, and converts eligible other fields into batched tensors. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:122-155]()
- Tests cover core default-collation behavior and include a helper for checking that a collator leaves input features unchanged. [tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:53-80]()[tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:87-171]()
- Processor preprocessing, specialized-collator internals, dataset utilities, and `HfArgumentParser` are not visible in the supplied source excerpts. [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:1-168]()[tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:1-173]()

Sources: [src/transformers/data/data_collator.py:30-155](), [tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py:53-171]()
