# Page: Quantization

# Quantization

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

The quantization framework provides a shared interface for configuring quantization and integrating quantizers with model loading. The central abstraction, `HfQuantizer`, is designed for use in the `PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained` loading flow. This parent page outlines the framework and its backend families; detailed method coverage belongs in the child pages. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-84]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-84]()

## Core infrastructure

### The `HfQuantizer` base class

`HfQuantizer` holds a `QuantizationConfigMixin` configuration and defines shared hooks for environment validation, parameter selection, device-map and memory adjustments, and quantization lifecycle behavior. Backend-specific subclasses implement these hooks to adapt loading to their libraries, hardware requirements, and checkpoint formats. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:112-162]()

The base class also provides helpers such as `get_keys_to_not_convert`, which identifies tied weights, the last parameter, and output embeddings as candidates to leave unconverted. Backend implementations can use this when deciding which modules to quantize. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:39-63]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:39-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:112-162]()

### Quantization lifecycle overview

A backend-specific quantizer can validate its runtime environment, prepare the model before loading weights, identify parameters that need quantization, and finalize backend-specific state after loading. For example, the bitsandbytes 4-bit quantizer validates dependencies and backend availability, replaces eligible linear layers before loading, and sets a loaded-in-4-bit flag afterward. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-68](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-140]()

This lifecycle is shared at the interface level, while module replacement, checkpoint conversion, supported devices, and serialization details vary by backend. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-84](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-157]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-84](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-68](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-157]()

### Quantization dispatch flow

The diagram connects configuration and loading concepts to the corresponding quantizer classes. `HfQuantizer` is the shared base; the shown backend subclasses provide examples of implementations. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-50](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:44-50](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-61](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-25]()

**Diagram: Quantization configuration and backend entities**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        QuantConfig["Quantization configuration"]
        ModelLoad["Model loading with from_pretrained"]
        Backend["Backend-specific quantization"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        ConfigMixin["QuantizationConfigMixin"]
        Base["HfQuantizer"]
        Bnb4["Bnb4BitHfQuantizer"]
        Bnb8["Bnb8BitHfQuantizer"]
        TorchAo["TorchAoHfQuantizer"]
        Fp8["FineGrainedFP8HfQuantizer"]
    end

    QuantConfig -->|"represented by"| ConfigMixin
    ConfigMixin -->|"held by"| Base
    ModelLoad -->|"quantizer loading scope"| Base
    Bnb4 -->|"inherits"| Base
    Bnb8 -->|"inherits"| Base
    TorchAo -->|"inherits"| Base
    Fp8 -->|"inherits"| Base
    Base -->|"backend-specific implementation"| Backend
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:19-20](), [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-50](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:44-50](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-61](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-25]()

### Loading and backend hooks

Backend hooks connect the shared quantizer interface to model preparation and weight loading. In the bitsandbytes implementation, `_process_model_before_weight_loading` calls `replace_with_bnb_linear`; its loading operations also expose backend-specific deserialization. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-135](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:171-174]()

Other backends may use different preparation or conversion paths. For instance, the fine-grained FP8 quantizer replaces linear layers before loading and applies a post-loading adjustment. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:112-141]()

**Diagram: Quantizer hooks and loading entities**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Load as "PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained"
    participant Quantizer as "HfQuantizer"
    participant Bnb as "Bnb4BitHfQuantizer"
    participant Replace as "replace_with_bnb_linear"
    participant Weights as "Checkpoint weights"

    Load->>Quantizer: "quantizer lifecycle"
    Quantizer->>Bnb: "backend implementation"
    Bnb->>Replace: "_process_model_before_weight_loading"
    Replace->>Weights: "prepare model structure for loading"
    Weights->>Bnb: "backend-specific loading operations"
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-84](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-135](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:171-174]()

## Supported backends

### BitsAndBytes, GPTQ & AWQ

Bitsandbytes has dedicated 4-bit and 8-bit quantizers, `Bnb4BitHfQuantizer` and `Bnb8BitHfQuantizer`. Both extend `HfQuantizer`, validate required dependencies and backend availability, and provide backend-specific handling for model loading. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-68](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:44-68]()

GPTQ and AWQ are covered with this backend family in the child page. For details, see [BitsAndBytes, GPTQ & AWQ](#7.1).

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-68](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:44-68]()

### FP8, GGUF/GGML & Other Quantization Backends

The broader backend family includes `TorchAoHfQuantizer`, `FineGrainedFP8HfQuantizer`, and `Mxfp4HfQuantizer`. Their implementations illustrate the framework’s range: TorchAO checks its dependency and selects parameters for quantization; fine-grained FP8 validates device requirements and prepares FP8 layers; MXFP4 validates runtime support for its format. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-70](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-46](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py:42-75]()

The child page covers these and other backends, including GGUF/GGML loading, in more detail. For details, see [FP8, GGUF/GGML & Other Quantization Backends](#7.2).

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-70](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-46](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py:42-75]()

## Child pages for details

- **[BitsAndBytes, GPTQ & AWQ](#7.1)** — 4-bit and 8-bit bitsandbytes, GPTQ and AWQ quantizers and configs, and linear-layer replacement during loading.
- **[FP8, GGUF/GGML & Other Quantization Backends](#7.2)** — Fine-grained FP8, MXFP4, FBGEMM-FP8, TorchAO, HQQ, Quanto, EETQ, AQLM, CompressedTensors, VPTQ, SpQR, and GGUF/GGML loading.

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-84](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-50](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-61](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-25](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py:42-48]()

# Page: BitsAndBytes, GPTQ & AWQ

# BitsAndBytes, GPTQ & AWQ

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This section describes how Transformers integrates 4-bit and 8-bit bitsandbytes quantization, and outlines the GPTQ and AWQ quantizer entry points. It focuses on the quantizer lifecycle and the bitsandbytes linear-layer replacement and checkpoint-loading hooks visible in the provided source excerpts. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-162]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-162]()

---

## Quantization framework architecture

`HfQuantizer` is the abstract base for quantizers used by `PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained`. It holds a quantization config and the `pre_quantized` flag, and provides hooks for validating the environment, updating dtype or device mapping, estimating parameter size, and deciding whether a parameter needs quantization. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-156]()

The base class also provides default hooks for memory adjustment and materialization dtype selection. In the latter case, it returns the requested dtype for floating-point checkpoint tensors unless a load operation handles the tensor; otherwise it returns `None`. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:129-150]()

The bitsandbytes quantizers implement backend-specific checks and model-preparation hooks. Their loading path replaces modules before weight loading, then exposes backend-specific deserialization operations for checkpoint tensors. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:56-68]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-135]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:171-174]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:56-68]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:117-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:161-164]()

### Diagram: Quantizer lifecycle mapped to code entities

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    User["from_pretrained(quantization_config=...)"] --> Quantizer["HfQuantizer"]
    Quantizer --> Validate["validate_environment()"]
    Validate --> Before["._process_model_before_weight_loading()"]
    Before --> Replace["replace_with_bnb_linear()"]
    Replace --> Weights["Model weight loading"]
    Weights --> Deserialize["Bnb4bitDeserialize or Bnb8bitDeserialize"]
    Deserialize --> After["._process_model_after_weight_loading()"]
    After --> Ready["Quantized model"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-162]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:171-174]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:117-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:161-164]()

---

## BitsAndBytes quantization (4-bit and 8-bit)

Transformers provides `Bnb4BitHfQuantizer` and `Bnb8BitHfQuantizer`, both parameterized by `BitsAndBytesConfig`. The 4-bit quantizer reports a quantized element size of 0.5 bytes; the 8-bit quantizer reports 1 byte. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:44-54]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:44-54]()

### Environment and device-map checks

Both quantizers require Accelerate and bitsandbytes, then call `validate_bnb_backend_availability` to check the backend. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:56-68]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:56-68]()

For either quantizer, a missing `device_map` is filled using the current CUDA, NPU, HPU, or XPU device when available, with CPU as the fallback. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:94-111]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:88-105]()

When `llm_int8_enable_fp32_cpu_offload` is disabled, a device map that mixes CPU or disk placement with other devices is rejected. The 4-bit and 8-bit implementations both apply this check. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:70-81]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:70-81]()

### Linear replacement and parameter selection

Before loading weights, both quantizers determine modules to leave unconverted using `get_modules_to_not_convert`, passing the config’s `llm_int8_skip_modules` and the model’s `_keep_in_fp32_modules`. If FP32 CPU offload is enabled and the device map is a dictionary, modules mapped to CPU or disk are added to the skip list. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-129]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:117-133]()

They then call `replace_with_bnb_linear`, passing the model, skip list, quantization config, and `pre_quantized` state. The 4-bit quantizer identifies quantizable parameters by checking whether the owning module is `bnb.nn.Linear4bit` and the tensor is not its bias. The 8-bit quantizer uses the corresponding `bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt` check. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:130-135]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:83-87]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:134-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:107-111]()

### Checkpoint operations and post-load state

The 4-bit quantizer registers `Bnb4bitDeserialize` as its load deserializer and declares serialized weight names that include quantization metadata such as `weight.quant_state.bitsandbytes__nf4` and `weight.quant_state.bitsandbytes__fp4`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:159-174]()

The 8-bit quantizer registers `Bnb8bitDeserialize` and lists `weight`, `SCB`, and `weight_format` as serialized names. After weight loading, it marks the model with `is_loaded_in_8bit`; the 4-bit quantizer similarly sets `is_loaded_in_4bit`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:113-115]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:159-164]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:137-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:159-174]()

Both quantizers expose dequantization through `dequantize_and_replace`, and both report themselves as serializable and trainable. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:141-157]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:141-157]()

### Diagram: bitsandbytes replacement and checkpoint loading

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Config["BitsAndBytesConfig"] --> Quantizer["Bnb4BitHfQuantizer or Bnb8BitHfQuantizer"]
    Quantizer --> Skip["get_modules_to_not_convert()"]
    Skip --> Replace["replace_with_bnb_linear()"]
    Replace --> Layer["bnb.nn.Linear4bit or bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt"]
    Checkpoint["Checkpoint tensors"] --> Deserialize["Bnb4bitDeserialize or Bnb8bitDeserialize"]
    Deserialize --> Params["Quantized module parameters"]
    Layer --> Params
    Params --> Post["is_loaded_in_4bit or is_loaded_in_8bit"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:113-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_4bit.py:159-174]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:117-139]()[src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_bnb_8bit.py:159-164]()

### Typical loading shape

The test suite exercises 4-bit and 8-bit loading through `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained`, supplying `BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True)` or `BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_8bit=True)` and `device_map="auto"`. [tests/quantization/bnb/test_4bit.py:121-133]()[tests/quantization/bnb/test_mixed_int8.py:122-134]()

Sources: [tests/quantization/bnb/test_4bit.py:121-133]()[tests/quantization/bnb/test_mixed_int8.py:122-134]()

## GPTQ and AWQ quantizers

GPTQ and AWQ are represented in the quantizer package by `GptqHfQuantizer` and `AwqHfQuantizer`. Their implementations are located in `src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_gptq.py` and `src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_awq.py`; the corresponding integration modules are `src/transformers/integrations/awq.py` and the GPTQ integration tests are under `tests/quantization/gptq/`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_gptq.py]() [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_awq.py]() [src/transformers/integrations/awq.py]() [tests/quantization/gptq/test_gptq.py]() [tests/quantization/autoawq/test_awq.py]()

The provided source excerpts do not include the contents or line ranges for those GPTQ and AWQ implementation files. Consequently, this page does not infer their specific layer-replacement calls, config fields, backend dispatch, or checkpoint tensor transformations.

# FP8, GGUF/GGML & Other Quantization Backends

- [README.md](README.md)

## Purpose and Scope

Section 7.2 covers quantization backends beyond BitsAndBytes, GPTQ, and AWQ (section 7.1). It describes how quantizers participate in model loading, how FP8 and MXFP4 integrations prepare weights and dispatch kernels, and how GGUF metadata and tensors map into Transformers model structures. It also surveys TorchAO, FBGEMM-FP8, HQQ, Quanto, EETQ, AQLM, CompressedTensors, VPTQ, and SpQR. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-25](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:39-63]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-25](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:39-63]()

---

## Quantizer Lifecycle and Shared Loading Hooks

`HfQuantizer` is the common abstraction for quantization methods integrated with `PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained`. A quantizer carries its configuration and a `pre_quantized` flag; subclasses can validate the runtime environment, adjust memory estimates and device maps, and decide whether individual parameters need quantization. The base class also provides parameter-size and dtype hooks used during materialization. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:100-156](), [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:158-162]()

A backend may prepare or replace modules before checkpoint weights are loaded, then use parameter-level logic or conversion operations to interpret checkpoint tensors. For example, the fine-grained FP8 quantizer replaces linear layers before loading and identifies parameters belonging to FP8 modules; TorchAO prepares module exclusions and can read checkpoint metadata. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-89](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:112-134](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-107](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:109-134]()

| Lifecycle concern | Base hook or mechanism | Example backend behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Environment checks | `validate_environment` | Fine-grained FP8 checks Accelerate and device support; TorchAO checks that its dependency is installed. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:158-162](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:31-58](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:67-80]() |
| Memory accounting | `quantized_element_size`, `param_element_size`, `adjust_max_memory` | TorchAO reports an estimated element size and reserves additional memory for quantization parameters. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:124-132](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:63-65](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:88-91]() |
| Module preparation | `_process_model_before_weight_loading` | Fine-grained FP8 replaces eligible linear modules; TorchAO builds a module skip list and reads checkpoint metadata when available. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:112-134](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-107]() |
| Parameter selection | `param_needs_quantization` | Fine-grained FP8 selects parameters from FP8 modules; TorchAO selects weights in supported linear or embedding modules. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-89](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:109-134]() |
| Tensor conversion | `get_new_dtype`, conversion operations | The base dtype hook avoids casting inputs handled by a quantizer load operation; MXFP4 uses `ConversionOps` classes for conversion and deserialization. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:134-146](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-61](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:132-177]() |

### Quantizer lifecycle: natural-language concepts mapped to code entities

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Load["Model loading with quantization"]
    Base["HfQuantizer"]
    Env["validate_environment"]
    Prep["process model before weight loading"]
    Select["param_needs_quantization"]
    Materialize["get_new_dtype and tensor materialization"]
    Backend["Backend-specific modules or conversion operations"]

    Load --> Base
    Base --> Env
    Env --> Prep
    Prep --> Select
    Select --> Materialize
    Materialize --> Backend

    PrepFP8["FineGrainedFP8HfQuantizer._process_model_before_weight_loading"]
    SelectFP8["FineGrainedFP8HfQuantizer.param_needs_quantization"]
    Prep --> PrepFP8
    Select --> SelectFP8
    PrepMX["Mxfp4Deserialize.convert"]
    Materialize --> PrepMX
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90](), [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:134-162](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-89](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:112-134](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:132-177]()

## Fine-Grained FP8 and FBGEMM-FP8

### Fine-grained FP8 quantizer

`FineGrainedFP8HfQuantizer` integrates fine-grained FP8 into model loading. Its reported quantized element size is one byte. Environment validation requires Accelerate; for non-dequantized loading it checks for a CUDA or XPU device. A pre-quantized checkpoint can be configured to dequantize to bfloat16 on unsupported hardware, while on-the-fly quantization without a suitable device raises an error. CUDA devices below compute capability 8.9 also cause the configuration to switch to dequantization. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-58]()

Before weight loading, the quantizer remaps configured skip-list names through the model’s conversion mappings, derives the final modules-to-exclude list, optionally replaces selected embeddings for pre-quantized checkpoints, and calls `replace_with_fp8_linear`. After loading, it disables DeepGEMM for multi-device models because the kernels are bound to one CUDA context. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:91-110](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:112-141]()

For on-the-fly quantization, `param_needs_quantization` recognizes `FP8Linear` and `FP8Experts`; it excludes pre-quantized parameters and biases from that conversion path. The integration defines FP8 dtype constants and `FineGrainedFP8`, a bundle of 2D, batched, and grouped matrix multiplication functions. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-89](), [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:44-78]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:18-58](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-89](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:91-141](), [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:44-78]()

### Fine-grained FP8 kernel loading and execution path

`load_finegrained_fp8_kernel` delegates to `_load_finegrained_fp8_kernel`, which lazily loads the `finegrained-fp8` kernel through `lazy_load_kernel`. The loader checks for the `kernels` package, requires the kernel to expose `matmul_2d`, `matmul_batched`, and `matmul_grouped`, then caches those functions in the module-level `_FINEGRAINED_FP8` bundle. The internal loader is marked `torch._dynamo.allow_in_graph` and returns `None`; the public wrapper reads the cached bundle. [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:80-143]()

The integration also defines allocation helpers for expert projections. `_alloc_expert_proj` creates weight and inverse-scale parameters with configurable storage and scale granularities; `weight_k_div` supports packed storage such as two FP4 values per byte. [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:151-176]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:80-143](), [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:151-176]()

### Fine-grained FP8 data flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Request["Quantized model load"]
    Quantizer["FineGrainedFP8HfQuantizer"]
    Validate["validate_environment"]
    Replace["replace_with_fp8_linear"]
    Modules["FP8Linear or FP8Experts"]
    Loader["load_finegrained_fp8_kernel"]
    Hub["lazy_load_kernel finegrained-fp8"]
    Bundle["FineGrainedFP8"]
    Matmul["matmul or batched_matmul or grouped_matmul"]
    Output["Model forward result"]

    Request --> Quantizer
    Quantizer --> Validate
    Validate --> Replace
    Replace --> Modules
    Modules --> Loader
    Loader --> Hub
    Hub --> Bundle
    Bundle --> Matmul
    Matmul --> Output
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:31-58](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:112-141](), [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:80-143]()

### FBGEMM-FP8

FBGEMM-FP8 is exposed through `FbgemmFp8HfQuantizer` and the `integrations/fbgemm_fp8.py` integration. The quantizer provides the Transformers quantizer interface, while the integration contains backend-specific code. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_fbgemm_fp8.py:41-151](), [src/transformers/integrations/fbgemm_fp8.py:1-20]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_fbgemm_fp8.py:41-151](), [src/transformers/integrations/fbgemm_fp8.py:1-20]()

---

## MXFP4

MXFP4 support is split between `Mxfp4HfQuantizer` and conversion operations in `integrations/mxfp4.py`. The integration declares the representable `FP4_VALUES` and defines `Mxfp4Quantize`, `Mxfp4Dequantize`, `Mxfp4Deserialize`, and `Mxfp4ReverseDeserialize` as conversion operations. [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:30-47](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-61](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:98-129](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:132-180]()

`Mxfp4Quantize.convert` retrieves the target module and, for `Mxfp4GptOssExperts`, quantizes a transposed input tensor, swizzles the resulting weight and scale, and installs the converted tensor and precision configuration on the module. It removes the original parameter registration, marks the module initialized, and returns an empty mapping so the loader does not rematerialize the original parameter. [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-95]()

`Mxfp4Dequantize.convert` reads the relevant projection blocks and scales and passes them to `dequantize_convertops`. `Mxfp4Deserialize.convert` instead swizzles the blocks and scales into the module in place, removes the key from `missing_keys`, marks the module initialized, and returns an empty mapping. [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:98-125](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:132-173]()

The quantizer implementation is in `quantizer_mxfp4.py`; its loading, environment, and configuration behavior are distinct from the integration’s tensor conversion operations. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py:42-162]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:30-47](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-95](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:98-125](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:132-180](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py:42-162]()

### MXFP4 conversion flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Checkpoint["MXFP4 checkpoint tensors"]
    Deserialize["Mxfp4Deserialize.convert"]
    Swizzle["swizzle_mxfp4_convertops"]
    Module["Mxfp4GptOssExperts projection"]
    Ready["Module marked initialized"]

    FloatWeights["Floating-point projection tensor"]
    Quantize["Mxfp4Quantize.convert"]
    QuantizeBlocks["quantize_to_mxfp4"]
    Configure["PrecisionConfig with weight_scale"]
    QuantizedModule["Module with Triton tensor and precision config"]

    Dequantize["Mxfp4Dequantize.convert"]
    Dequantized["dequantize_convertops"]

    Checkpoint --> Deserialize
    Deserialize --> Swizzle
    Swizzle --> Module
    Module --> Ready
    FloatWeights --> Quantize
    Quantize --> QuantizeBlocks
    QuantizeBlocks --> Configure
    Configure --> QuantizedModule
    Checkpoint --> Dequantize
    Dequantize --> Dequantized
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-95](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:98-125](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:132-173]()

## TorchAO

TorchAO is integrated through `TorchAoHfQuantizer`. Its implementation checks that TorchAO is installed, handles certain CPU or disk device-map combinations, flattens tensor-subclass state dictionaries for safetensors serialization, and adjusts memory estimates to account for quantization parameters. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-91]()

Before loading weights, `_process_model_before_weight_loading` determines modules to exclude from conversion and can include input and output embeddings when configured. If checkpoint files are supplied, it reads safetensors metadata for later use. `param_needs_quantization` limits the standard path to weights of `nn.Linear` modules and, optionally, `nn.Embedding`; it also supports `FqnToConfig` matching for per-module configurations. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-134]()

`TorchAoHfQuantizer.get_quantize_ops` returns a `TorchAoQuantize` operation. The class reports itself as serializable and compileable; its `is_trainable` property depends on whether the configured TorchAO quantization type is an 8-bit variant. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:136-161]()

The TorchAO documentation describes quantization configurations including float8 dynamic activation/weight and float8 weight-only options. It also describes module-level configuration using fully qualified module names. [docs/source/en/quantization/torchao.md:33-43](), [docs/source/en/quantization/torchao.md:75-90]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-91](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-161](), [docs/source/en/quantization/torchao.md:33-43](), [docs/source/en/quantization/torchao.md:75-90]()

### TorchAO parameter-selection flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Config["TorchAoConfig"]
    Quantizer["TorchAoHfQuantizer"]
    Exclusions["modules_to_not_convert"]
    Module["get_module_from_name"]
    Match["FqnToConfig matching or supported module check"]
    Linear["nn.Linear weight"]
    Embedding["nn.Embedding weight when enabled"]
    Ops["TorchAoQuantize"]

    Config --> Quantizer
    Quantizer --> Exclusions
    Exclusions --> Module
    Module --> Match
    Match --> Linear
    Match --> Embedding
    Quantizer --> Ops
```

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-65](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-134](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:158-161]()

---

## GGUF and GGML Interoperability

Transformers represents GGUF metadata through mappings in `integrations/ggml.py` and loads GGUF tensors through utilities in `modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py`. `GGUF_CONFIG_MAPPING` maps GGUF architecture metadata to Transformers configuration attributes; for example, Llama and Mistral mappings associate `context_length`, `block_count`, and `embedding_length` with model configuration fields. The mapping also covers tokenizer special-token IDs and multiple model architectures. [src/transformers/integrations/ggml.py:28-69](), [src/transformers/integrations/ggml.py:152-157]()

`modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py` builds `GGUF_TO_TRANSFORMERS_MAPPING` for metadata categories including configuration and tokenizer settings, and derives `GGUF_SUPPORTED_ARCHITECTURES` from the configuration mapping. Its `GGUFTensor` tuple carries an array, tensor name, and metadata. [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:39-60]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/ggml.py:28-69](), [src/transformers/integrations/ggml.py:152-157](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:39-60]()

### Tensor processing and model-specific transformations

`TensorProcessor` is the base class for GGUF tensor handling. It provides a name preprocessing hook, a fallback mapping hook for unresolved Hugging Face-to-GGUF tensor mappings, and a default `process` method that wraps a tensor as a `GGUFTensor`. [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:62-86]()

`LlamaTensorProcessor` reverses the GGUF-side permutation for attention query and key weights when the required head counts are present. Its `_reverse_permute_weights` reshapes the array by head and dimension, swaps axes, and restores the original shape. [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:88-116]()

`Qwen2MoeTensorProcessor` handles MoE parameter naming and mappings. Its fallback hook maps a Hugging Face `gate_up_proj` parameter to separate GGUF gate and up expert tensors. When processing those tensors, `_set_moe_expert_tensor` stores down projections directly and places gate and up weights into their corresponding regions of a combined tensor. [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:118-149](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:151-169]()

Sources: [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:62-86](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:88-116](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:118-169]()

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    Mapping --> Config

```

### GGUF loading through Auto classes

The GGUF integration tests demonstrate loading both a tokenizer and a causal language model with `gguf_file` passed to `from_pretrained`, followed by generation. The tests cover standard quantization types, K-quants, and importance-matrix quantization variants. [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:44-77](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:79-113]()

The same test suite checks tokenizer compatibility against the original model tokenizer, including matching encodings and decoded text for test inputs. [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:119-168]()

Sources: [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:44-77](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:79-113](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:119-168]()

## Other Quantization Backends

Transformers includes separate quantizer modules for several external quantization libraries and checkpoint formats. They share the `HfQuantizer` integration surface but have backend-specific configuration and weight-loading behavior. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-90]()

| Backend | Quantizer implementation | Integration or scope |
|---|---|---|
| FBGEMM-FP8 | `FbgemmFp8HfQuantizer` | Backend-specific integration is in `integrations/fbgemm_fp8.py`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_fbgemm_fp8.py:41-151](), [src/transformers/integrations/fbgemm_fp8.py:1-20]() |
| TorchAO | `TorchAoHfQuantizer` | Applies TorchAO quantization operations and supports selection by module name. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:55-65](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:109-161]() |
| HQQ | `HqqHfQuantizer` | Quantizer implementation is in `quantizer_hqq.py`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_hqq.py:46-79]() |
| Quanto | `QuantoQuantizer` | Quantizer implementation is in `quantizer_quanto.py`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_quanto.py:1-20]() |
| EETQ | `EetqQuantizer` | Quantizer implementation is in `quantizer_eetq.py`. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_eetq.py:1-20]() |
| AQLM | AQLM quantizer | AQLM quantizer implementation is part of the quantizer package. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_aqlm.py:1-20]() |
| CompressedTensors | `CompressedTensorsHfQuantizer` | Handles compressed checkpoint schemes and their loading behavior. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_compressed_tensors.py:38-133]() |
| VPTQ | VPTQ quantizer | VPTQ quantizer implementation is part of the quantizer package. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_vptq.py:1-20]() |
| SpQR | SpQR quantizer | SpQR quantizer implementation is part of the quantizer package. [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_spqr.py:1-20]() |

The available excerpts identify the quantizer files for Quanto, EETQ, AQLM, VPTQ, and SpQR but do not show their implementation bodies. Their internal algorithms and runtime behavior are therefore not detailed here. ## Testing and Operational Boundaries

GGUF tests are decorated to require the GGUF dependency and a Torch accelerator; they are also marked slow. They exercise loading and generation for multiple GGUF quantization families and tokenizer compatibility. [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:27-47](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:65-113](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:119-168]()

TorchAO tests verify configuration serialization and exercise loading quantized models through `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained` with a `TorchAoConfig`. The tests include int4 weight-only loading and a dynamic-activation int8 configuration. [tests/quantization/torchao_integration/test_torchao.py:58-88](), [tests/quantization/torchao_integration/test_torchao.py:104-155]()

Sources: [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:27-47](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:65-113](), [tests/quantization/ggml/test_ggml.py:119-168](), [tests/quantization/torchao_integration/test_torchao.py:58-88](), [tests/quantization/torchao_integration/test_torchao.py:104-155]()

---

## Summary

The shared `HfQuantizer` interface provides hooks for environment validation, parameter selection, memory accounting, and weight-loading behavior. Fine-grained FP8 uses module replacement and lazily loaded matrix-multiplication kernels; MXFP4 uses conversion operations to quantize, deserialize, or dequantize projection weights; TorchAO selects modules and supplies TorchAO-specific quantization operations; and GGUF loading maps metadata and processes model-specific tensor layouts. Other backends are represented by dedicated quantizer modules, with detailed behavior depending on their backend-specific implementations. [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-156](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-141](), [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:80-143](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-177](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-161](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:39-169]()

Sources: [src/transformers/quantizers/base.py:74-156](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_finegrained_fp8.py:79-141](), [src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py:80-143](), [src/transformers/integrations/mxfp4.py:50-177](), [src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_torchao.py:93-161](), [src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py:39-169]()

# Page: Distributed & Parallel Inference

# Distributed & Parallel Inference

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page maps the main distributed strategies exposed by Transformers and how they relate to the model-level orchestration API. It is an overview; for setup, configuration options, and implementation details, see the child pages linked below. `DistributedConfig` describes native tensor, expert, pipeline, and FSDP parallelism, while `DistributedMixin` holds the model plans and connects them to the distributed implementations.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69]()

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69]()

## High-Level Parallelism Overview

Distributed execution combines strategies that partition different dimensions of model execution. Tensor parallelism shards dense layer operations; expert parallelism distributes MoE experts; pipeline parallelism partitions model stages; and FSDP shards parameters. `DistributedConfig` represents these sizes and plans, and `DistributedMixin` maintains the model’s `tp_plan`, `ep_plan`, `pp_plan`, and `fsdp_plan`.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69]()

| Strategy | Code entities | High-level role |
|---|---|---|
| Tensor parallelism (TP) | `tp_size`, `tp_plan`, `ColwiseParallel`, `RowwiseParallel` | Shard dense layer operations across ranks.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:31-38]() [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-161]() |
| Expert parallelism (EP) | `ep_size`, `ep_plan`, `apply_expert_parallelism` | Distribute MoE expert computation; `ep_plan` is kept distinct from `tp_plan`.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:106-114]() |
| Pipeline parallelism (PP) | `pp_size`, `pp_plan`, `apply_pipeline_parallelism` | Partition execution across pipeline stages.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:54-55]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:120-122]() |
| FSDP | `fsdp_size`, `fsdp_plan`, `apply_fully_sharded_data_parallelism` | Shard model parameters; configuration also exposes CPU-offload and mixed-precision options.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:44-53]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39]() |
| Device mapping | `device_map`, `prepare_distribute_model` | A separate model-placement input accepted by the distributed preparation interface.[src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:167-174]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:106-122](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:167-174](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-161]()

### Strategy names mapped to code entities

This diagram connects strategy names to the plan fields, orchestration class, mesh abstraction, and implementation functions used in the distributed package.[src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:29-48]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69]() [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

```mermaid
graph TD
    TP["Tensor parallelism"] --> TPPlan["tp_plan"]
    EP["Expert parallelism"] --> EPPlan["ep_plan"]
    PP["Pipeline parallelism"] --> PPPlan["pp_plan"]
    FSDP["FSDP"] --> FSDPPlan["fsdp_plan"]
    TPPlan --> Mix["DistributedMixin"]
    EPPlan --> Mix
    PPPlan --> Mix
    FSDPPlan --> Mix
    Mix --> Mesh["TransformersDeviceMesh"]
    Mix --> ApplyTP["apply_tensor_parallelism"]
    Mix --> ApplyEP["apply_expert_parallelism"]
    Mix --> ApplyPP["apply_pipeline_parallelism"]
    Mix --> ApplyFSDP["apply_fully_sharded_data_parallelism"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:29-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

## Tensor & Expert Parallelism (TP/EP)

TP and EP address different parts of a model and can be configured independently through `tp_plan` and `ep_plan`. The tensor-parallel implementation includes `ColwiseParallel` and related styles; the configuration documentation describes EP plans for expert sharding and token-dispatch choices. `TransformersDeviceMesh` supports distinct dense and expert mesh views.[src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-161]() [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64]() [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

For details, see [Tensor Parallelism & Expert Parallelism](#8.1).

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-161](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

## DeepSpeed & FSDP Integration

FSDP is one of the native strategies represented in `DistributedConfig`: its size, plan, CPU-offload flag, and mixed-precision flag are configurable. The distributed package connects `DistributedMixin` to `apply_fully_sharded_data_parallelism`; the child page covers FSDP and DeepSpeed integration in more detail.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:44-53]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39]()

For details, see [DeepSpeed & FSDP Integration](#8.2).

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:44-53](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39]()

## Accelerate & Device Mapping

`DistributedMixin.prepare_distribute_model` accepts `device_map` alongside `distributed_config`, providing the connection point for model placement and distributed setup. Device mapping is distinct from plans such as `tp_plan` and `fsdp_plan`, which describe parallel strategies.[src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:167-174]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:79-85]()

For details, see [Accelerate & Device Mapping](#8.3).

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:79-85](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:167-174]()

### Configuration and model preparation

`DistributedConfig` specifies parallelism sizes and plans; `DistributedMixin.prepare_distribute_model` accepts that configuration and a `device_map`. The diagram shows these as inputs to preparation without implying that they are interchangeable strategies.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:167-174]()

```mermaid
graph TD
    Config["DistributedConfig"] --> Prepare["prepare_distribute_model"]
    DeviceMap["device_map"] --> Prepare
    Prepare --> TP["tp_plan"]
    Prepare --> EP["ep_plan"]
    Prepare --> PP["pp_plan"]
    Prepare --> FSDP["fsdp_plan"]
    TP --> Mesh["TransformersDeviceMesh"]
    EP --> Mesh
    PP --> Mesh
    FSDP --> Mesh
```

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:167-174](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

## Pipeline Parallelism

Pipeline parallelism has its own `pp_size` configuration field and `pp_plan` model plan. `DistributedMixin` imports and connects `apply_pipeline_parallelism` as part of the distributed orchestration layer.[src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:54-55]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39]() [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:120-122]()

For details, see [Pipeline Parallelism](#8.4).

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:54-55](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:35-39](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:120-122]()

# Page: Tensor Parallelism & Expert Parallelism

# Tensor Parallelism & Expert Parallelism

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.circleci/create_circleci_config.py](.circleci/create_circleci_config.py)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes the native distributed parallelism interfaces relevant to tensor parallelism (TP), expert parallelism (EP), and their interaction with FSDP2. It covers plan configuration, device-mesh layouts, DTensor-based TP styles, MoE routing approaches, and the code entities that connect these concepts. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-65](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-65](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

---

## Overview & design philosophy

### `DistributedMixin` and `DistributedConfig`

`DistributedMixin` provides distributed orchestration and save/load hooks for `PreTrainedModel`, and holds the model’s parallel plans, sizes, and mesh state. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69]()

The plans represent separate responsibilities: `tp_plan` maps modules or parameters to tensor-parallel styles, `ep_plan` maps MoE-related modules to expert-parallel styles, `fsdp_plan` specifies FSDP behavior, and `pp_plan` describes pipeline stages. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:64-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:106-122]()

`init_parallel_plans()` copies class-level plans onto the model instance, merges plan contributions from the base-model configuration, and prefixes plans contributed by child modules with the child name. When the base model has a TP plan and an `embed_tokens` embedding, it adds an `embedding_rowwise` rule unless an explicit plan already covers that embedding. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:79-104]()

`DistributedConfig` is the dataclass for native distributed inference and training configuration. Its fields include `tp_size`, `tp_plan`, `ep_size`, `ep_plan`, `fsdp_size`, `fsdp_plan`, and `pp_size`, along with FSDP offload and mixed-precision options. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77]()

`DistributedConfig` resolves missing sizes and validates the mesh configuration during initialization. In particular, when `tp_size` is absent but a TP plan is provided, it derives `tp_size` from `WORLD_SIZE` after accounting for FSDP and pipeline parallel sizes. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:102-126]()

| Plan or setting | Role |
|---|---|
| `tp_plan` | Selects TP styles for module or parameter paths; class and base-model plans are merged onto the instance. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:79-109]() |
| `ep_plan` | Selects EP styles separately from `tp_plan`; EP rules can take precedence for the same modules. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:111-114](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:60-65]() |
| `fsdp_plan` | Selects FSDP plan styles; it is applied only when `fsdp_size > 1`. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:116-118](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:44-49]() |
| `pp_plan` | Holds pipeline-parallel plan entries on the model. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:121-122]() |
| `tp_size`, `ep_size`, `fsdp_size`, `pp_size` | Define parallel group sizes and participate in mesh-size validation. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:31-65](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:102-126]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:79-122](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:102-126]()

### Plan setters and validation

The `tp_plan`, `ep_plan`, and `fsdp_plan` setters accept dictionaries or `None`; `None` clears the respective plan, and a non-dictionary value raises `ValueError`. The TP and EP setters validate their styles against `ALL_PARALLEL_STYLES`, while the FSDP setter validates against `ALL_FSDP_STYLES`. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:124-155]()

TP plan validation can report invalid style names, and it warns when a rule matches no model layers. Tests exercise wildcard paths such as `model.layers.*.self_attn.q_proj` and confirm that class-level `lm_head` plans survive instance plan initialization. [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:61-76](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:93-120](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:135-145]()

`verify_tp_plan()` checks expected parameter keys against the supplied TP plan and warns about unused rules or layers that remain unsharded. [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:53-79]()

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:124-155](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:53-79](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:61-76](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:93-120](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:135-145]()

---

## DeviceMesh and DTensor topologies

`TransformersDeviceMesh` manages mesh views for different parameter classes. Dense layers use the `(pp, fsdp, tp)` view, while experts use `(pp, efsdp, ep)`. These views span the same world size, so `pp * fsdp * tp == pp * efsdp * ep`. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

The expert FSDP size is `efsdp = fsdp * tp / ep`. EP distributes distinct experts across its group; `efsdp` is the FSDP axis for expert weights. The implementation documentation states that there is no separate expert tensor-parallel (`etp`) axis: with EP enabled, experts are not tensor-sharded. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:171-181](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:79-100]()

`is_dtensor()` identifies PyTorch `DTensor` instances when distributed support is available. TP styles use DTensor placements such as `Shard`, `Replicate`, and `Partial`; for example, `ColwiseParallel` defaults to replicated inputs and an output sharded on its last dimension. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:54-60](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:45-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-151]()

| Mesh view | Axes | Parameters or computation represented |
|---|---|---|
| Dense | `pp`, `fsdp`, `tp` | Attention, dense MLPs, embeddings, and language-model heads. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:171-176]() |
| Expert | `pp`, `efsdp`, `ep` | Expert parameters, with expert ownership distributed across EP and optional expert FSDP. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:171-181]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:54-60](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:79-100](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:45-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-151]()

---

## System architecture: plan-driven execution and sharding

The following diagram maps configuration concepts to the corresponding code entities. `DistributedMixin` owns and merges model plans; `DistributedConfig` supplies sizes and plan overrides; the TP implementation defines the style machinery and DTensor operations. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-104](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:45-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:96-140]()

### Configuration and plan flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        UserConfig["DistributedConfig"]
        DenseRules["Dense tensor sharding rules"]
        ExpertRules["MoE expert and router rules"]
        MeshSizes["TP / EP / FSDP / PP sizes"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        ConfigClass["configuration_utils.py::DistributedConfig"]
        MixinClass["mixin.py::DistributedMixin"]
        InitPlans["DistributedMixin.init_parallel_plans"]
        ValidateTP["DistributedMixin._validate_parallel_plan"]
        TPApply["tensor_parallel.py::apply_tensor_parallelism"]
        EPApply["expert_parallel.py::apply_expert_parallelism"]
    end

    subgraph DistributedTensorSpace["Distributed Tensor Space"]
        MeshManager["TransformersDeviceMesh"]
        DenseMesh["(pp, fsdp, tp)"]
        ExpertMesh["(pp, efsdp, ep)"]
        DTensor["torch.distributed.tensor.DTensor"]
    end

    UserConfig --> ConfigClass
    MeshSizes --> ConfigClass
    DenseRules --> InitPlans
    ExpertRules --> InitPlans

    MixinClass --> InitPlans

    ValidateTP --> TPApply
```

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:25-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-104](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:45-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:96-140](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

### Distributed process and device setup

When distributed initialization is needed, `_ensure_torch_distributed()` obtains `RANK`, `LOCAL_RANK`, and `WORLD_SIZE`, selects a backend for the device type, binds an accelerator device where applicable, and initializes the process group. The backend mapping includes `nccl` for CUDA, `gloo` for CPU, and device-specific entries for several other accelerator types. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:84-99](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:102-148]()

The distributed mesh model then distinguishes dense and expert views over the same world. This lets dense TP and expert EP have different axes without changing the total world size. [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:84-99](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:102-148](), [src/transformers/distributed/utils.py:167-181]()

---

## Tensor parallelism (TP)

Tensor parallelism divides layer computation and parameter storage across multiple devices. Transformers describes TP as slicing a model layer so multiple accelerators work on it simultaneously, with communication needed for partial results. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:16-20]()

A model can provide a predefined TP plan through its base-model configuration. `DistributedConfig` can use that plan, or accept a dictionary that overrides selected rules while retaining unspecified rules. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:20-20](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:31-37]()

Plan keys are module or parameter paths, and `*` can represent layer indices. Invalid style names are rejected by plan validation; rules that match nothing and parameters with no applicable rule can be reported as warnings. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:73-77](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:124-144](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:53-79]()

### DTensor styles and forward transformation

`TensorParallelLayer` defines the style hooks: parameter validation and sharding, pre-forward input transformation, a context around the original forward, and post-forward output transformation. `install_forward()` wraps a module’s existing `forward` with those stages. [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:96-140]()

`ColwiseParallel` represents column-wise linear sharding: weight and bias are sharded on dimension 0, inputs are replicated by default, and outputs are sharded on the last dimension by default. The output width need not divide evenly by the TP size; the final rank can hold a shorter slice. [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-151]()

The public strategy registry includes names for column-wise, row-wise, packed, embedding, sequence, replicated, and MoE-related styles. The registry maps plan strings to configured strategy instances; `ALL_PARALLEL_STYLES` is the authoritative collection of supported names. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:102-124]()

| Plan style | Layout or intent described by the code/docs |
|---|---|
| `colwise` | Replicated input and last-dimension-sharded output for column-wise linear layers. [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:143-151](), [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:104-113]() |
| `rowwise` | Sharded input and replicated output in the documented strategy registration. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:109-114]() |
| `colwise_gather_output` | Column-wise linear strategy configured to replicate its output. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:109-110]() |
| `packed_colwise`, `packed_rowwise` | Strategies for packed projection layouts. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:115-116]() |
| `embedding_rowwise`, `embedding_colwise` | Embedding strategies sharding the configured embedding dimension. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:104-108]() |
| `sequence_parallel` | Registered sequence-parallel strategy. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:117-118]() |
| `replicated_with_grad_allreduce` | Registered replicated-parameter strategy with gradient all-reduce. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:117-119]() |
| `moe_tp_experts`, `moe_identity_expert` | Registered MoE-related styles used in expert plan configurations. [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:121-123]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:96-161](), [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:16-20](), [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:73-77](), [docs/source/en/perf_infer_gpu_multi.md:102-124]()

### TP and EP interaction

With both TP and EP enabled, the documented model plan applies TP to dense modules and EP to experts. EP rules take precedence over TP rules for the same modules, so the expert weights are not sharded twice. When TP is enabled but EP is disabled, the TP plan applies, including any expert rules it contains. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:42-45]()

`DistributedConfig` documents that `ep_size` must be a multiple of `tp_size` and divide `fsdp_size * tp_size`. All-reduce expert plans require `ep_size=tp_size`, while token dispatch also allows `ep_size > tp_size`. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64]()

`get_kv_heads_per_rank()` returns the original KV head count unless the TP plan uses column-wise sharding on a key projection; when such sharding applies, it returns the per-rank count if the head count divides evenly by the TP size, or `None` otherwise. [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:82-93]()

Sources: [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:42-45](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64](), [src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py:82-93]()

---

## Expert parallelism (EP) and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)

Expert parallelism distributes MoE feed-forward experts across accelerators. The router directs tokens to experts, and the expert results are combined. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:16-18]()

A model can define separate `base_model_tp_plan` and `base_model_ep_plan` configuration plans. The loaded model exposes the merged plans as `tp_plan` and `ep_plan`; EP plan rules take precedence over TP rules for a module when both plans apply. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:42-45](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:79-104](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:106-114]()

`ep_size` enables EP explicitly. The legacy `enable_expert_parallel` option is deprecated; when used without `ep_size`, it resolves to an EP-only configuration across `tp_size` ranks by setting `ep_size=tp_size` and an empty TP plan. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:40-43](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:128-135]()

### Token dispatch versus masking and all-reduce

The EP plan selects how tokens reach experts. The two documented approaches are masking with all-reduce and token dispatch with all-to-all communication. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:46-52]()

| EP approach | Plan rules | Data movement and constraints |
|---|---|---|
| Masking and all-reduce | `moe_tp_experts` for experts and `ep_router` for the router. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:46-52]() | Every rank processes the full batch with its local experts; router masking excludes experts on other ranks, and all-reduce combines the outputs. Requires `ep_size=tp_size`. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:46-52]() |
| Token dispatch | `ep_dispatch_experts`. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:46-52]() | Ranks exchange routed token–expert pairs with all-to-all collectives, run local experts, and return the results with a second all-to-all. `ep_size` may exceed `tp_size` subject to the documented divisibility constraints. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:46-52](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64]() |

For token dispatch, each rank begins with its own batch portion. At an MoE layer, it routes tokens, sends each routed pair to the expert owner, runs the local experts, receives the outputs, and combines them using routing weights. [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:92-95]()

The expert FSDP axis is `efsdp_size = fsdp_size * tp_size // ep_size`. Under token dispatch, the documentation describes expert parameters as sharded across EP and, when `efsdp_size > 1`, additionally FSDP-sharded across `efsdp`. [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:79-100](), [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:108-111]()

Sources: [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:16-18](), [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:42-52](), [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:92-111](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:40-43](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:56-64](), [src/transformers/distributed/configuration_utils.py:79-100]()

### MoE routing and expert-compute flow

The diagram associates the EP concepts with the named plan styles and implementations. `batched_mm_experts_forward()` flattens token–expert selections into a sample axis, selects the corresponding expert weights, computes expert projections, and handles EP sentinel IDs by clamping them to valid local indices for the batched matrix multiplication path. [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:112-159]()

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        RoutedTokens["Router-selected token / expert pairs"]
        OwnerExchange["Send routed pairs to expert owners"]
        ExpertCompute["Compute with local expert weights"]
        ReturnResults["Return expert outputs and combine"]
        MaskAndReduce["Mask non-local experts and all-reduce"]
    end

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        EPDispatch["ep_dispatch_experts"]
        EPRouter["ep_router"]
        MoETPExperts["moe_tp_experts"]
        ExpertForward["batched_mm_experts_forward"]
        ExpertWeights["gate_up_proj / up_proj / down_proj"]
        DeepGEMM["deepgemm_bf16_experts_forward"]
        SonicMoE["sonicmoe_experts_forward"]
    end

    RoutedTokens --> EPDispatch
    EPDispatch --> OwnerExchange
    OwnerExchange --> ExpertForward
    ExpertForward --> ExpertWeights
    ExpertWeights --> ReturnResults
    RoutedTokens --> EPRouter
    EPRouter --> MoETPExperts
    MoETPExperts --> MaskAndReduce
    ExpertForward -. "integration kernels" .-> DeepGEMM
    ExpertForward -. "integration kernels" .-> SonicMoE
```

Sources: [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:46-52](), [docs/source/en/expert_parallelism.md:92-95](), [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:27-28](), [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:112-159]()

### Expert forward implementation details

`batched_mm_experts_forward()` expands each token once per top-k selection, flattens routing weights and expert IDs, then indexes the appropriate gate/up or up-projection weights. It applies either the configured gate or activation function, selects down-projection weights, and continues the expert output calculation. [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:112-159]()

When `_is_expert_parallel` is set, IDs outside the local expert range are treated as sentinels and clamped for safe weight indexing. The implementation notes that those routing weights are zeroed by router masking, so their weighted contributions are dropped, although the batched matrix multiplication still performs the corresponding compute. [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:128-136]()

`_batched_linear()` performs the batched matrix multiplication for either transposed or non-transposed weights and adds an optional bias. [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:78-109]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:78-109](), [src/transformers/integrations/moe.py:112-159]()

---

## Loading, saving, and compatibility

`DistributedMixin` includes state for distributed model loading and imports distributed checkpoint load/save and consolidation functions, as well as TP and EP application functions. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:29-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:58-69]()

The `is_distributed_loading_by_transformers` property distinguishes loading where Transformers shards the model at load time—each rank reads its shard through `DtensorShardOperation`—from cases where a wrapper such as Accelerate shards the model afterward. [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:71-77]()

The module `transformers.integrations.tensor_parallel` is a backward-compatibility shim; its docstring identifies `transformers.distributed.tensor_parallel` as the canonical TP implementation and `transformers.distributed.expert_parallel` as the canonical location for EP styles. The legacy `shard_and_distribute_module()` helper emits a `FutureWarning` and raises `RuntimeError`, directing users to `apply_tensor_parallelism` with `from_pretrained(..., tp_plan=...)`. [src/transformers/integrations/tensor_parallel.py:14-18](), [src/transformers/integrations/tensor_parallel.py:57-66]()

Sources: [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:29-48](), [src/transformers/distributed/mixin.py:71-77](), [src/transformers/integrations/tensor_parallel.py:14-18](), [src/transformers/integrations/tensor_parallel.py:57-66]()

---

## Testing and verification

The TP plan tests cover plan property access and updates, invalid style rejection, unmatched layer-pattern warnings, valid wildcard patterns, `None` handling, and preservation of class-level plans. [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:32-59](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:61-120](), [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:122-145]()

Distributed TP tests load a model with `DistributedConfig(tp_size=dist.get_world_size())` and a non-TP reference model, then compare parameter shapes to identify and check sharded parameters. [tests/test_tensor_parallel_mixin.py:118-168]()

The test suite’s selected distributed TP model types include dense architectures and MoE model types, as well as selected multimodal and audio model types. [tests/test_tensor_parallel_mixin.py:46-72]()

Sources: [tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel.py:32-145](), [tests/test_tensor_parallel_mixin.py:46-72](), [tests/test_tensor_parallel_mixin.py:118-168]()
