# Page: Text & Conversational Pipelines

# Text & Conversational Pipelines

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes the text-generation and conversational pipeline layer: `TextGenerationPipeline`, `ImageTextToTextPipeline`, and `AnyToAnyPipeline`. It covers how pipeline task names connect to implementation classes, how generation pipelines handle text and chat inputs, and how chat templates, tool schemas, response parsing, and streaming relate to inference. The pipeline API provides a high-level interface that preprocesses inputs and returns task-appropriate outputs. [README.md:124-128]()[src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:49-77]()[src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:23-28]()[src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:53-58]()

Sources: [README.md:124-128](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:49-77](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:23-28](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:53-58]()

---

## 1. Pipeline routing and shared execution model

The pipeline package imports concrete pipeline classes and associates task names with implementations through `SUPPORTED_TASKS`. For example, the package imports `TextGenerationPipeline` and `ImageTextToTextPipeline`; the task registry maps task identifiers to implementation classes and model auto classes. The registry also defines task aliases such as `text-to-speech` for `text-to-audio`. [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:49-89]()[src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:134-169]()

Pipeline implementations share the `Pipeline` base class. Its batching utilities collate preprocessed input dictionaries, padding token and feature fields according to tokenizer or feature-extractor configuration. The collator rejects mismatched batch keys and requires a tokenizer or feature extractor when batching. [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:75-85]()[src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:88-123]()[src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:126-180]()

### Natural-language task names mapped to pipeline entities

**Diagram: Task routing from task names to pipeline implementations**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        TextTask["text-generation"]
        ImageTask["image-text-to-text"]
        Prompt["Text prompt or chat messages"]
        ImagePrompt["Image and text or multimodal chat"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Registry["SUPPORTED_TASKS"]
        TextClass["TextGenerationPipeline"]
        ImageClass["ImageTextToTextPipeline"]
        BaseClass["Pipeline"]
        ModelMap["MODEL_FOR_CAUSAL_LM_MAPPING_NAMES"]
        ImageModelMap["MODEL_FOR_IMAGE_TEXT_TO_TEXT_MAPPING_NAMES"]
    end

    TextTask --> Registry
    ImageTask --> Registry
    Registry --> TextClass
    Registry --> ImageClass
    Prompt --> TextClass
    ImagePrompt --> ImageClass
    TextClass --> BaseClass
    ImageClass --> BaseClass
    TextClass --> ModelMap
    ImageClass --> ImageModelMap
```

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:49-77](), [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:134-169](), [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:126-180](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:23-28](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:99-107](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:53-58](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:126-130]()

---

## 2. `TextGenerationPipeline`

`TextGenerationPipeline` is the pipeline implementation for autoregressive language generation. It accepts a text prompt or, when the model is conversational, a chat represented as a list of message dictionaries containing `role` and `content`. Chat-mode output continues the conversation by adding the generated response. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:23-28]()

The class declares that it calls generation, loads a tokenizer, and does not load a processor, image processor, or feature extractor by default. It defines a default generation configuration of `max_new_tokens=256`, `do_sample=True`, and `temperature=0.7`. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:86-97]()

### Initialization and parameter handling

On initialization, the pipeline checks that its model type is supported by `MODEL_FOR_CAUSAL_LM_MAPPING_NAMES`. For decoder-only models, it changes a right-padding tokenizer to left padding; the implementation avoids doing so when a feature extractor is present, since multimodal cases may require a different padding convention. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:99-107]()

`_sanitize_parameters` separates pipeline-call arguments into preprocessing, forward/generation, and postprocessing parameters. Its signature includes chat-related controls such as `continue_final_message`, tool and document inputs, tokenizer encoding options, and standard generation arguments. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:128-145]()

For XLNet and Transformer-XL, initialization can set the `XL_PREFIX` as a default prefix when no explicit prefix was supplied. The prefix is passed through `_sanitize_parameters` so its associated preprocessing and generation parameters are updated together. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:72-84]()[src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:108-126]()

### Input, generation, and output

A plain string is the text-completion input form. A chat is a list of messages; the pipeline’s documented contract describes each message as a dictionary with `role` and `content`, and the returned generated text can be represented as an updated chat. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:23-28]()[tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:73-116]()

The tests exercise both a chat ending with a user message and a chat ending with an assistant message. In the latter case, the final assistant message is continued rather than replaced with a new assistant turn. They also test explicitly setting `continue_final_message=True`. [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:118-180]()

The `ReturnType` enum distinguishes tensor output, newly generated text, and full text. The documented interface includes `return_full_text=False` for returning only newly generated text and `return_tensors=True` for returning generated token IDs. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:16-20]()[tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:64-71]()

### Text-generation data flow

**Diagram: Text prompt and chat flow through `TextGenerationPipeline`**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Prompt["Text prompt"]
        Messages["Chat messages with role and content"]
        Result["Generated text or updated chat"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Pipeline["TextGenerationPipeline"]
        Sanitize["_sanitize_parameters"]
        Mapping["MODEL_FOR_CAUSAL_LM_MAPPING_NAMES"]
        Template["Chat template processing"]
        Generate["Model generation"]
        ReturnType["ReturnType"]
    end

    Prompt --> Pipeline
    Messages --> Pipeline
    Pipeline --> Mapping
    Pipeline --> Sanitize
    Sanitize --> Template
    Template --> Generate
    Generate --> ReturnType
    ReturnType --> Result
```

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:16-28](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:99-107](), [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:128-145](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:73-180]()

---

## 3. Image-text and any-to-any generation

### 3.1 `ImageTextToTextPipeline`

`ImageTextToTextPipeline` uses an `AutoModelForImageTextToText`-compatible model to generate text conditioned on image and text inputs. Like the text-generation pipeline, it supports conversational input for conversational models; chat messages can include multimodal content. [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:52-58]()

The class loads a processor rather than loading a tokenizer, image processor, or feature extractor independently. It declares that it calls generation and sets `max_new_tokens=256` as its default generation configuration. Initialization requires the vision backend and checks model compatibility against `MODEL_FOR_IMAGE_TEXT_TO_TEXT_MAPPING_NAMES`. [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:115-130]()

Its `_sanitize_parameters` routes general processing arguments, `timeout`, `continue_final_message`, and `processor_kwargs` to preprocessing. Generation options are collected separately. When `stop_sequence` is provided, it is converted to `stop_strings` and the processor tokenizer is attached to generation arguments. [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:131-170]()

The documented chat example uses message content items with types such as `image` and `text`, and shows a prior assistant message as part of the conversational context. [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:74-103]()

### 3.2 `AnyToAnyPipeline`

`AnyToAnyPipeline` is imported and exposed by the pipeline package. Its implementation is in `src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py`; the pipeline uses a `Chat` wrapper and provides initialization and parameter-handling paths. [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:49-50]()[src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:54-65]()[src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:67-128]()[src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:143-177]()

The implementation supports multimodal inputs and outputs for models that declare input modalities. Its pipeline interface uses chat-shaped inputs and the internal `Chat` type to distinguish conversations from batches. Modality requirements are checked during initialization based on the model’s declared input modalities. [src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:54-65]()[src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:143-149]()

### Natural-language inputs mapped to multimodal pipeline classes

**Diagram: Image-text and any-to-any pipeline entity map**

```mermaid

    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        ImageTextInput["Image plus text prompt"]
        ImageChat["Chat containing image and text"]
        MixedInput["Multimodal chat or input"]
        TextOutput["Generated text"]
        MixedOutput["Generated multimodal response"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        ImagePipeline["ImageTextToTextPipeline"]
        AnyPipeline["AnyToAnyPipeline"]
        Processor["processor"]
        ImageMap["MODEL_FOR_IMAGE_TEXT_TO_TEXT_MAPPING_NAMES"]
        MultiModel["AutoModelForMultimodalLM"]
        ChatWrapper["Chat"]
    end

    ImageTextInput --> ImagePipeline
    ImageChat --> ImagePipeline
    MixedInput --> ChatWrapper
    ChatWrapper --> AnyPipeline
    ImagePipeline --> ImageMap
    ImagePipeline --> Processor
    AnyPipeline --> MultiModel
    ImagePipeline --> TextOutput
    AnyPipeline --> MixedOutput
```

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:49-50](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:27-39](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:52-58](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:115-130](), [src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:54-65](), [src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:67-128](), [src/transformers/pipelines/any_to_any.py:143-149]()

---

## 4. Chat templates, tool schemas, and response parsing

### 4.1 Chat templates and tool schemas

Chat templates convert structured message lists into the serialized form expected by a conversational model. The text-generation and image-text-to-text pipelines accept chat-shaped inputs; the common pipeline tests import the `Chat` type used in pipeline handling. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:6-7]()[src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:27-28]()[tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:60-60]()

The chat-template utilities include helpers for message validation and tool schema generation. `get_json_schema()` can derive a JSON schema from a callable’s signature and annotations, allowing tool descriptions to be supplied in a structured form to a template. [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:35-46]()[src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:80-173]()

### 4.2 Response parsing and streamed output

Response parsing is a separate utility layer from the pipeline classes. `ResponseParser` and `parse_response()` are associated with `src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py`; the parser uses response templates to identify structured regions in generated text, including content, reasoning content, and tool calls. [src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py:66-147]()

The parser’s interface supports incremental parsing of generated text as well as parsing a complete response. A response template describes how model-specific output markers map to structured response fields; this is distinct from the input-side chat template used to serialize messages. [src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py:66-147]()[src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_templates.py:1-1]()

**Diagram: Input templating and output parsing as separate stages**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Messages["Structured chat messages"]
        Tool["Tool callable"]
        Stream["Generated text stream"]
        Parsed["Structured response and tool calls"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        ChatType["Chat and is_valid_message"]
        Template["apply_chat_template"]
        Schema["get_json_schema"]
        Generate["Model generation"]
        Parser["ResponseParser"]
        ParseResponse["parse_response"]
    end

    Messages --> ChatType
    ChatType --> Template
    Tool --> Schema
    Schema --> Template
    Template --> Generate
    Generate --> Stream
    Stream --> Parser
    Parser --> ParseResponse
    ParseResponse --> Parsed
```

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/base.py:56-57](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:35-46](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:80-173](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py:66-147]()

### 4.3 Streaming and tool-call extraction

Streaming generation produces text incrementally; response parsing can consume generated text incrementally and identify structured regions as their boundaries become available. This allows downstream consumers to distinguish ordinary response content from fields such as tool calls without treating the entire output as unstructured prose. [src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py:66-147]()

Tool-call parsing should be understood as output interpretation, not automatic tool execution. The chat-template utilities support constructing tool schemas, while response parsing extracts structured output; these operations do not, by themselves, invoke the described callable. [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:80-173]()[src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py:66-147]()

Sources: [src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:80-173](), [src/transformers/utils/chat_parsing/response_parser.py:66-147]()

---

## 5. Parameter sanitization and pipeline boundaries

Pipeline `_sanitize_parameters` methods divide user arguments according to where they apply in the inference lifecycle:

| Parameter group | Purpose | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `preprocess_params` | Configure conversion of user inputs into model-ready inputs. | `timeout`, `processor_kwargs`, `continue_final_message` |
| `forward_params` | Configure the model call or generation. | `generate_kwargs`, `max_new_tokens`, `stop_strings` |
| `postprocess_params` | Configure the returned representation. | Full-text or tensor output controls |

`TextGenerationPipeline._sanitize_parameters` accepts chat-related and generation-related inputs, including `continue_final_message`, `tools`, and `documents`. [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:128-145]()

`ImageTextToTextPipeline._sanitize_parameters` explicitly adds preprocessing arguments such as `timeout`, `continue_final_message`, and `processor_kwargs`; generation options and stop sequences are routed to forward parameters. [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:131-170]()

Sources: [src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py:128-145](), [src/transformers/pipelines/image_text_to_text.py:131-170]()

---

## 6. Tests and behavioral checks

Pipeline tests cover task construction, model compatibility, and expected return structures. Text-generation tests exercise plain prompts, batched prompts, generated token IDs, chat inputs, and continuation of the last assistant message. [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:39-71]()[tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:73-180]()

Common pipeline tests check task inference from a model and verify that task aliases or removed task names are handled by task routing. They also instantiate and inspect `TextGenerationPipeline` and `ImageTextToTextPipeline`. [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:29-41]()[tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:113-117]()[tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:166-182]()

Sources: [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:39-71](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_text_generation.py:73-180](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:29-41](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:113-117](), [tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py:166-182]()

# Page: Vision, Audio & Multimodal Pipelines

# Vision, Audio & Multimodal Pipelines

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

Section 10.2 covers the Transformers pipeline API for audio transcription and generation, image, video, and audio classification, zero-shot prediction, depth estimation, object detection, table and document question answering, and mask generation. Pipelines are high-level inference classes: they handle input preprocessing and return task-appropriate outputs. [README.md:124-128]()

The available source excerpt documents the general pipeline API, but not the implementations of these individual tasks. Accordingly, this page describes their scope and shared entry point without inferring task-specific model routing, preprocessing, or postprocessing behavior. [README.md:124-128]()

Sources: [README.md:124-128]()

## Shared pipeline entry point

The README presents `pipeline` as the high-level API for inference across text, audio, vision, and multimodal tasks. Its example selects a task and model when constructing the pipeline, then passes an input to the returned object. [README.md:124-135]()

At this level, the interaction has three steps: select a task and model, create a pipeline, and supply task input. The excerpt does not specify how individual task pipelines load processors or models, transform inputs, or format results. [README.md:124-135]()

### Task scope

| Task area | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Automatic speech recognition (ASR) | Transcribe audio into text. |
| Text-to-audio | Generate audio from text. |
| Image, video, and audio classification | Assign labels to visual or audio inputs. |
| Zero-shot prediction | Make predictions for supplied candidate labels or descriptions. |
| Depth estimation | Estimate depth from visual input. |
| Object detection | Identify objects and their locations. |
| Table and document question answering | Answer questions about structured tables or documents. |
| Mask generation | Generate masks for visual input. |

These task areas are the scope of this wiki section; the available README excerpt establishes general audio, vision, and multimodal pipeline support but does not describe the implementation details of these specific tasks. [README.md:124-128]()

Sources: [README.md:124-128]()

### Pipeline interaction

Diagram: Public pipeline interaction mapped to the documented API

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Task["task"] --> Pipeline["pipeline"]
    Model["model"] --> Pipeline
    Pipeline --> Callable["pipeline_object"]
    Input["task_input"] --> Callable
    Callable --> Output["task_appropriate_output"]
```

The diagram captures only the general interaction documented for `pipeline`; task-specific code entities and processing stages are not established by the available excerpt. [README.md:124-135]()

Sources: [README.md:124-135]()

## Implementation details and limits of the available source

The README describes pipelines as high-level inference classes that preprocess inputs and return appropriate outputs. It also states that the API supports text, audio, vision, and multimodal tasks. [README.md:124-128]()

The available source does not include pipeline package exports, task registries, task-specific pipeline classes, model mappings, or tests. Therefore, details such as ASR chunking, audio decoding, image and video processor selection, zero-shot candidate handling, detection output formats, and document QA preprocessing cannot be substantiated here. [README.md:124-128]()

Sources: [README.md:124-128]()

# Page: Integrations & Deployment

# Integrations & Deployment

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



This page maps the main integration and deployment paths in Transformers: connecting model definitions to the wider ecosystem, using PEFT adapters, exporting models, and serving them through the CLI. It is an overview; follow the child pages for implementation details. Transformers describes itself as a model-definition framework used across training frameworks, inference engines, and adjacent modeling libraries. [README.md:71-80]()

## Integration and deployment paths

These paths address different stages of using a model: PEFT supports adapter-based workflows, exporters target deployment formats and runtimes, and the CLI provides commands including serving. The child pages cover each area, plus downstream ecosystem CI. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:57-93]() [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:120-152]() [README.md:71-77]()

**Diagram: Deployment topics mapped to code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace["Natural Language Space"]
        PEFT_TASK["Adapter fine-tuning"]
        EXPORT_TASK["Model export"]
        SERVING_TASK["CLI serving"]
        ECOSYSTEM_TASK["Downstream ecosystem compatibility"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace["Code Entity Space"]
        PEFT_MIXIN["PeftAdapterMixin"]
        EXPORTERS["exporters/"]
        SERVE["transformers serve"]
        MODEL_MANAGER["ModelManager"]
        ECOSYSTEM["Training frameworks and inference engines"]
    end
    PEFT_TASK --> PEFT_MIXIN
    EXPORT_TASK --> EXPORTERS
    SERVING_TASK --> SERVE
    SERVE --> MODEL_MANAGER
    ECOSYSTEM_TASK --> ECOSYSTEM
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:57-93]() [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:120-152]() [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:96-123]() [README.md:71-77]()

## 11.1. PEFT & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

`PeftAdapterMixin` is the model-facing integration point for adapter operations. The PEFT integration tests exercise adapter workflows, including loading and managing adapter state. For details, see [PEFT & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning](#11.1). [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:46-93]() [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:63-81]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:46-93]() [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:63-81]()

## 11.2. Model Export

Export is a deployment path for targeting formats and runtimes such as ONNX, ExecuTorch, and OpenVINO. The child page covers the `exporters/` subpackage, `ExportConfigMixin`, `TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM`, and `exporter_openvino.py`. For details, see [Model Export](#11.2).

Sources: `exporters/` and `exporter_openvino.py` are identified in the child-page scope; line-specific file contents were not provided.

The CLI’s `transformers serve` command connects model loading with serving infrastructure, including `ModelManager` and the `cli/serving/` subpackage. Downstream ecosystem CI covers caller workflows that run vLLM, SGLang, and TRL test suites against Transformers main to detect compatibility regressions. For details, see [Downstream Ecosystem CI (vLLM, SGLang, TRL)](#11.4). Transformers positions its model definitions as a compatibility point for inference engines and training frameworks. # Page: PEFT & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

# PEFT & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.circleci/create_circleci_config.py](.circleci/create_circleci_config.py)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This section documents the Transformers integration with PEFT: the `PeftAdapterMixin` API, adapter loading and lifecycle, LoRA hotswapping, and the integration tests visible in the supplied source excerpts. PEFT methods fine-tune a small set of adapter parameters on top of a pretrained model, reducing the number of parameters being trained and making adapter artifacts lightweight to share and load. [docs/source/en/peft.md:12-18]()

Sources: [docs/source/en/peft.md:12-18](), [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:57-78]()

## Architecture and mixin

`PeftAdapterMixin`, defined in `src/transformers/integrations/peft.py`, provides model-level adapter operations. The documentation says the mixin is added to `PreTrainedModel` classes, so users can manage adapters through the Transformers model API rather than wrapping the model in a separate `PeftModel`. The mixin supports non-prompt-learning methods, including LoRA and IA³; prompt-learning methods are out of scope because they are not injectable into a Torch module. The integration declares PEFT `0.20.0` as its minimum supported version. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:46-74](), [docs/source/en/peft.md:14-18]()

The mixin’s class attributes include `_hf_peft_config_loaded`, `_prepare_peft_hotswap_kwargs`, and `peft_config`. Its documented responsibilities include loading adapters from local paths or Hub repositories, attaching adapters for training, managing multiple adapters, enabling or disabling them, and retrieving the active adapter’s state dict. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:67-78]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:46-78](), [docs/source/en/peft.md:14-18]()

## Adapter loading and lifecycle

`load_adapter()` accepts an adapter repository or local path, a name, an optional PEFT configuration and state dict, and loading options. Its signature also includes `is_trainable`, `hotswap`, `local_files_only`, `adapter_kwargs`, and a `LoadStateDictConfig`. The method documentation describes loading adapter weights and injecting them into the model; it also distinguishes inference-only loading from trainable loading. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-93](), [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:94-127]()

Adapters can enter the model through two documented paths:

- `from_pretrained()` can detect an adapter configuration and load the base model named by `base_model_name_or_path`, then attach the adapter. [docs/source/en/peft.md:117-131]()
- `load_adapter()` can attach an adapter to a model that has already been loaded. [docs/source/en/peft.md:134-143]()

A PEFT adapter repository or directory must contain `adapter_config.json` and adapter weights. The integration tests exercise loading a remote adapter through `from_pretrained()`, check that adapter tuner layers are present, and perform a generation call. [docs/source/en/peft.md:117-124](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:68-81](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:89-109]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-127](), [docs/source/en/peft.md:117-143](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:68-109]()

## Integration data flow

The diagram connects the user-facing adapter artifacts and model-loading operation to the named Transformers entities shown in the supplied sources. The available excerpt establishes the `load_adapter()` entry point and its arguments, but does not show the method’s full implementation. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-93](), [docs/source/en/peft.md:117-143]()

**Adapter loading: user artifacts to code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Natural_Language_Space["Natural Language Space"]
        Hub_or_local["Adapter Hub repository or local directory"]
        Adapter_config["adapter_config.json"]
        Adapter_weights["Adapter weights"]
        Existing_model["Already-loaded base model"]
    end

    subgraph Code_Entity_Space["Code Entity Space"]
        From_pretrained["PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained"]
        Mixin["PeftAdapterMixin"]
        Load_adapter["load_adapter"]
        Config_arg["peft_config"]
        State_dict_arg["adapter_state_dict"]
    end

    Hub_or_local --> From_pretrained
    Adapter_config --> From_pretrained
    From_pretrained --> Mixin
    Existing_model --> Load_adapter
    Hub_or_local --> Load_adapter
    Adapter_weights --> Load_adapter
    Load_adapter --> Config_arg
    Load_adapter --> State_dict_arg
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-93](), [docs/source/en/peft.md:117-143]()

## Key API surface

The PEFT reference page lists the public adapter-management methods exposed by `PeftAdapterMixin`. The supplied test excerpt directly demonstrates `get_adapter_state_dict()`, `disable_adapters()`, and `enable_adapters()`; the other listed methods are documented as part of the mixin API, but their implementation bodies are not included in the supplied excerpt. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:12-25](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:110-123](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:146-173]()

| API | Role indicated by the supplied sources |
|---|---|
| `load_adapter()` | Loads adapter weights from a local path or Hub folder; its arguments support adapter configuration, state dicts, trainability, and hotswapping. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-93]() |
| `add_adapter()` | Attaches a PEFT configuration to a model; the documentation illustrates this with a `LoraConfig`. [docs/source/en/peft.md:24-43]() |
| `set_adapter()` | Listed as a mixin method for selecting an adapter. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:16-25]() |
| `enable_adapters()` / `disable_adapters()` | Listed as mixin methods; the integration test checks their effect on forward-pass logits. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:16-25](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:146-173]() |
| `enable_peft_hotswap()` | Listed as a mixin method; the `load_adapter()` documentation describes preparing for hotswapping with a target rank. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:16-25](), [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:121-142]() |
| `active_adapters()` | Listed as a mixin method for reporting active adapters. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:16-25]() |
| `get_adapter_state_dict()` | Returns the adapter state dict; the test checks that its keys contain `lora`. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:16-25](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:110-123]() |
| `delete_adapter()` | Listed as a mixin method for deleting an adapter. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:16-25]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-93](), [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:121-142](), [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:12-25](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:110-123](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:146-173]()

## LoRA hotswapping

`load_adapter()` accepts `hotswap` as either a boolean or `"auto"`, with `"auto"` as the documented default. The method documentation describes hotswapping as replacing the weights of an existing LoRA adapter rather than loading an additional adapter. The target `adapter_name` must already exist. The documentation identifies avoiding recompilation after `torch.compile()` as a principal benefit. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:80-93](), [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:121-127]()

When adapters differ in rank or LoRA alpha, the documented sequence calls `enable_peft_hotswap(target_rank=...)` before loading the adapter and before compiling the model. The initial adapter is loaded under a name that can be reused for subsequent swaps. The excerpt establishes this guidance but does not include the implementation body of `enable_peft_hotswap()` or the rest of `load_adapter()`. [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:129-142]()

**Hotswap sequence: API names and ordering**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Model as "PreTrainedModel"
    participant Mixin as "PeftAdapterMixin"
    participant Compiler as "torch.compile"

    User->>Mixin: "enable_peft_hotswap(target_rank)"
    User->>Mixin: "load_adapter(adapter_name)"
    User->>Compiler: "Optionally compile model"
    User->>Mixin: "load_adapter(same adapter_name, hotswap)"
    Mixin-->>Model: "Replace existing adapter weights in-place"
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/peft.py:121-142]()

## Adapter saving and merging

The supplied documentation and test excerpt establish adapter-only saving: after loading an adapter, `save_pretrained()` is tested to write `adapter_model.safetensors` and `adapter_config.json`, without writing the base model’s `config.json` or base weight files. [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:124-145]()

The supplied file excerpts do not show an adapter-merging method or its implementation, so this page does not specify merge behavior or merge-related APIs. The reference page lists the mixin methods covered by the available excerpt, and merging is not among them. [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:12-25]()

Sources: [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:124-145](), [docs/source/en/main_classes/peft.md:12-25]()

## Integration tests

`PeftTesterMixin` gates the tests on PEFT and Torch availability and specifies tiny PEFT and Transformers model identifiers. `PeftIntegrationTester` contains checks for adapter loading, state-dict contents, saving, and adapter enable/disable behavior in the supplied excerpt. [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:55-67]()

| Test | Verification |
|---|---|
| `test_peft_from_pretrained` | Loads a model from a PEFT model identifier, checks for unexpected or missing-key warnings, confirms a PEFT tuner layer is present and `_hf_peft_config_loaded` is true, then runs generation. [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:89-109]() |
| `test_peft_state_dict` | Calls `get_adapter_state_dict()` and checks that each returned key contains `lora`. [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:110-123]() |
| `test_peft_save_pretrained` | Saves the PEFT model and checks for adapter weights and configuration, while checking that base-model configuration and weights were not written to the adapter directory; it then reloads the saved directory. [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:124-145]() |
| `test_peft_enable_disable_adapters` | Adds a LoRA adapter, compares logits with adapters enabled and disabled, and checks that re-enabling restores the original adapter-enabled logits. [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:146-173]() |

Sources: [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:55-67](), [tests/peft_integration/test_peft_integration.py:89-173]()

# Model Export

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

Model export converts a Transformers model into a representation suitable for a deployment runtime. This page covers the `exporters/` package and the ExecuTorch integration path visible in the available implementation references. The references identify `ExportConfigMixin`, `TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM`, and `exporter_openvino.py`, but do not expose enough implementation to describe their internals in detail. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:32-40]()

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:32-40]()

---

## 1. Export package and backend boundaries

The `exporters/` package contains backend-specific exporter modules, including `exporter_onnx.py`, `exporter_openvino.py`, and `exporter_executorch.py`, alongside shared files such as `base.py`, `auto.py`, `configs.py`, and `utils.py`. The available references identify these files but do not establish their dispatch behavior, backend APIs, or the precise responsibilities of `ExportConfigMixin`. [src/transformers/exporters/base.py:1-1]()

The ExecuTorch integration shown here uses a model-wrapper path: `TorchExportableModuleForVLM` selects components and invokes `torch.export.export` for them, while delegating text-decoder export to `TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM`. This describes the shown implementation; it does not establish that ONNX or OpenVINO use the same wrapper or call sequence. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:32-40] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:56-64] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:81-86] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:105-111] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]()

### Diagram: Deployment names mapped to code entities

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        ONNX["ONNX export"]
        OV["OpenVINO export"]
        ET["ExecuTorch export"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        ONNXFile["exporter_onnx.py"]
        OVFile["exporter_openvino.py"]
        ETFile["exporter_executorch.py"]
        ETWrapper["TorchExportableModuleForVLM"]
        DecoderWrapper["TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM"]
        TorchExport["torch.export.export"]
    end

    ONNX --> ONNXFile
    OV --> OVFile
    ET --> ETFile
    ETFile --> ETWrapper
    ETWrapper --> DecoderWrapper
    ETWrapper --> TorchExport
    DecoderWrapper --> TorchExport
```

Sources: [src/transformers/exporters/exporter_onnx.py:1-1]() [src/transformers/exporters/exporter_openvino.py:1-1]() [src/transformers/exporters/exporter_executorch.py:1-1]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:32-40]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:81-86]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:105-111]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]()

---

## 2. ExecuTorch wrappers and component flow

### `TorchExportableModuleForVLM`

`TorchExportableModuleForVLM` is documented as a wrapper for exporting vision-language models. Its initializer stores the model, limits, and configuration, then selects `model.model.vision_model`, `model.model.connector`, and `model.model.text_model` as the vision encoder, connector, and text decoder. It also initializes fields for exported programs. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:32-64]()

The wrapper provides separate export methods for those components:

- `export_vision_encoder()` switches the vision encoder to evaluation mode, creates a sample `pixel_values` tensor, specifies dynamic height and width dimensions, and calls `torch.export.export` with `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:66-88]()
- `export_connector()` switches the connector to evaluation mode, derives a sample patch count from the vision configuration, creates sample `image_hidden_states`, marks the patch dimension dynamic, and exports the connector with `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:90-113]()
- `export_text_decoder()` constructs a `TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM` around the selected text model, prepares sample `input_ids` and `cache_position`, bounds the sequence dimension using cache and model-position limits, then calls the wrapper’s `export()` method. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]()

The top-level `export()` method invokes the three component export methods and returns a dictionary keyed by `vision_encoder`, `connector`, and `text_decoder`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:142-151]()

### `TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM`

`TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM` is declared as a `torch.nn.Module` and is used by `TorchExportableModuleForVLM.export_text_decoder()` as the text-decoder export wrapper. The available reference does not show the wrapper’s initializer, cache setup, forward implementation, or `export()` implementation. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:184-185]()

### Diagram: Natural-language export components mapped to wrapper methods

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Image["Image input"]
        VisualFeatures["Visual features"]
        TextGeneration["Text generation"]
        VLMExport["Export a vision-language model"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        PixelValues["pixel_values"]
        VisionEncoder["vision_encoder"]
        ImageHiddenStates["image_hidden_states"]
        Connector["connector"]
        TextDecoder["text_decoder"]
        ExportVision["export_vision_encoder()"]
        ExportConnector["export_connector()"]
        ExportText["export_text_decoder()"]
        ExportAll["export()"]
    end

    Image --> PixelValues
    PixelValues --> ExportVision
    ExportVision --> VisionEncoder
    VisionEncoder --> ImageHiddenStates
    ImageHiddenStates --> ExportConnector
    ExportConnector --> Connector
    Connector --> TextDecoder
    TextGeneration --> ExportText
    ExportText --> TextDecoder
    VLMExport --> ExportAll
    ExportAll --> ExportVision
    ExportAll --> ExportConnector
    ExportAll --> ExportText
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:32-40]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:56-64]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:66-88]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:90-113]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-151]()

---

## 3. Dynamic shapes and decoder inputs

The shown VLM export path supplies example inputs and dynamic-shape declarations to `torch.export.export`. For the vision encoder, `pixel_values` has dynamic dimensions at indices 2 and 3. For the connector, `image_hidden_states` has a dynamic dimension at index 1; the example uses a batch size of one. Both component exports pass `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:66-86] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:90-113]()

For the text decoder, the wrapper creates sample `input_ids` with sequence length three and a corresponding `cache_position`. It sets `max_seq_length` to the smaller of `max_cache_len` and `text_config.max_position_embeddings`, then defines a `torch.export.Dim` named `seq_length_dim` with a maximum of `max_seq_length - 1`. That dimension is applied to the sequence axis of `input_ids` and the first axis of `cache_position`. The resulting dynamic-shape mapping is passed to the decoder wrapper’s `export()` call with `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]()

These references show the boundary and shape constraints supplied by `TorchExportableModuleForVLM`; they do not show how the decoder wrapper consumes `cache_position` or manages cache state internally. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:184-185]()

### Component-to-export input mapping

| Component | Example input shown | Dynamic dimensions shown | Export call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vision encoder | `pixel_values` | Dimensions 2 and 3 use `torch.export.Dim.AUTO`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:70-85]() | `torch.export.export` with `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:81-86]() |
| Connector | `image_hidden_states` | Dimension 1 uses `torch.export.Dim.AUTO`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:94-110]() | `torch.export.export` with `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:105-111]() |
| Text decoder | `input_ids`, `cache_position` | Shared `seq_length_dim`, bounded by `max_seq_length - 1`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:122-132]() | `TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM.export(...)` with `strict=False`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:133-138]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:66-86]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:90-113]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]()

### Diagram: Export data flow and shape constraints

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Pixels["pixel_values"] --> VisionShapes["dynamic_shapes: dimensions 2 and 3"]
    VisionShapes --> VisionExport["torch.export.export(vision_encoder, strict=False)"]
    VisionExport --> HiddenStates["image_hidden_states"]
    HiddenStates --> ConnectorShapes["dynamic_shapes: dimension 1"]
    ConnectorShapes --> ConnectorExport["torch.export.export(connector, strict=False)"]
    ConnectorExport --> Decoder["TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM"]
    InputIds["input_ids: sequence axis"] --> SequenceDim["seq_length_dim"]
    CachePosition["cache_position: axis 0"] --> SequenceDim
    SequenceDim --> DecoderExport["export(input_ids, cache_position, dynamic_shapes, strict=False)"]
    Decoder --> DecoderExport
    DecoderExport --> Programs["exported component programs"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:66-86]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:90-113]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]()

## 4. Export configuration and cache-related limits

`ExportConfigMixin` is identified in the export package’s configuration module, `src/transformers/exporters/configs.py`. The available references do not show its definition or call sites, so its fields, validation behavior, and relationship to backend-specific configuration cannot be established here. [src/transformers/exporters/configs.py:1-1]()

In the shown ExecuTorch VLM path, `max_cache_len` is stored by `TorchExportableModuleForVLM` and used to calculate the text decoder’s maximum sequence length. The calculation also considers `text_config.max_position_embeddings`; the smaller limit determines the bound used to create `seq_length_dim`. The references do not establish that this wrapper instantiates or passes a `StaticCache`. [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:42-54] [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:122-132]()

The generic cache implementation defines `DynamicLayer` as a cache layer that grows by concatenating new key and value states. This is background on a generation-cache implementation, not evidence that the export wrapper shown here uses `DynamicLayer` or `StaticCache`. [src/transformers/cache_utils.py:103-137]()

### Diagram: Export limits and code references

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CacheLimit["max_cache_len"] --> VLMWrapper["TorchExportableModuleForVLM"]
    PositionLimit["text_config.max_position_embeddings"] --> MinLimit["min(max_cache_len, max_position_embeddings)"]
    VLMWrapper --> MinLimit
    MinLimit --> SequenceBound["seq_length_dim max = max_seq_length - 1"]
    SequenceBound --> DynamicShapes["dynamic_shapes for input_ids and cache_position"]
    DynamicShapes --> DecoderExport["TorchExportableModuleForDecoderOnlyLM.export()"]
    ExportConfig["ExportConfigMixin"]
    ExportConfig --> ConfigFile["exporters/configs.py"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:42-54]() [src/transformers/integrations/executorch.py:115-140]() [src/transformers/exporters/configs.py:1-1]()

---

Those details require the corresponding exporter implementations and tests. [src/transformers/exporters/exporter_onnx.py:1-1] [src/transformers/exporters/exporter_openvino.py:1-1]()

## 6. Tests and verification scope

The available test reference shows that `tests/generation/test_utils.py` imports `ExportGenerateTesterMixin` from `tests.exporters.test_export` and makes `GenerationTesterMixin` inherit from it. This establishes a test integration point for export-related generation behavior, but the exporter test implementation and its assertions are not shown. [tests/generation/test_utils.py:123-130]()

The exporter test files are identified as `tests/exporters/test_export.py` and `tests/exporters/test_utils.py`; their coverage cannot be described in detail from the available references. [tests/exporters/test_export.py:1-1] [tests/exporters/test_utils.py:1-1]()

Sources: [tests/generation/test_utils.py:123-130]() [tests/exporters/test_export.py:1-1]() [tests/exporters/test_utils.py:1-1]()

# Page: CLI & Serving

# CLI & Serving

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml](.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml)

## Purpose and scope

This page covers the Transformers command-line interface and serving layer, including the `chat` and `serve` commands, the OpenAI-compatible serving API, and the `download`, `env`, and `add-new-model-like` utilities. The supplied implementation excerpts give details about serving and chat; the add-model-like workflow is also visible in a GitHub Actions job. The command registry and the implementations of `download`, `env`, and `add_new_model_like` are not included in the available excerpts. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:72-82](), [.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml:61-71]()

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:14-16](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:72-82](), [.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml:61-71]()

## 1. CLI Entry Points & Subcommands

The CLI surface in scope includes `serve`, `chat`, `download`, `env`, and `add-new-model-like`. The provided source excerpts show the Typer-facing `Serve` class and the terminal chat client. They do not show the command registry or the implementations for `download`, `env`, and `add_new_model_like`, so their internal dispatch and behavior cannot be described here. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:24-42](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:14-31]()

| Command | Role | Implementation evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `serve` | Starts the serving application and configures model, batching, and server options. | `Serve` accepts these options and checks serving dependencies. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:41-42](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:54-119](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:120-132]() |
| `chat` | Provides an interactive client interface, including streamed output rendering. | `RichInterface` and its `stream_output` method are defined in `chat.py`. [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:112-128]() |
| `download` | CLI utility in the requested command scope; its implementation is not shown in the supplied excerpts. | — |
| `env` | CLI utility in the requested command scope; its implementation is not shown in the supplied excerpts. | — |
| `add-new-model-like` | Model-scaffolding utility in the requested command scope. A CI workflow invokes it with a config file and repository path. | [.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml:61-66]() |

The `chat` module defines help text for session commands including `!help`, `!status`, `!clear`, `!exit`, `!example`, `!set`, and `!save`. `RichInterface.stream_output` consumes streamed chat-completion chunks, accumulates text, tracks completion usage and finish reason when available, and renders the accumulated output through Rich. [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:72-102](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:112-160]()

The add-model-like CI workflow invokes `transformers add-new-model-like` with `tests/fixtures/add_distilbert_like_config.json` and the repository root, then runs style and copy-fixing commands. It subsequently runs the generated model’s PyTorch modeling tests and repository quality checks. This describes how the command is exercised by CI, not the command’s internal implementation. [.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml:61-76]()

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:24-42](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:54-132](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:72-102](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:112-160](), [.github/workflows/add-model-like.yml:61-76]()

## 2. Serving Architecture & Endpoints

`Serve` is the `transformers serve` entry point. It checks whether serving dependencies are installed and raises an installation hint if they are unavailable. When serving is available, it imports the serving handlers, `ModelManager`, and `build_server`; it can also set a default Torch seed and configure the Transformers logger. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:41-42](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:120-140]()

The serving documentation describes a local or self-hosted server compatible with the OpenAI SDK. Documented APIs include chat completions, legacy completions, Responses, audio transcriptions, SystemOne, model listing, and model-load progress streaming. [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:17-32]()

### System Data Flow: Request to Inference

The diagram associates documented API names with handler and model-management entities. The supplied excerpts show the handler imports and the documented endpoints, but do not show route registration; the endpoint-to-handler mapping is therefore indicative rather than a claim about exact route wiring. [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:24-32](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:123-132]()

Diagram: Request-to-Inference Entities

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client["OpenAI-compatible client"] --> ChatRoute["/v1/chat/completions"]
    Client --> ResponsesRoute["/v1/responses"]
    Client --> CompletionRoute["/v1/completions"]
    ChatRoute --> ChatHandler["ChatCompletionHandler"]
    ResponsesRoute --> ResponseHandler["ResponseHandler"]
    CompletionRoute --> CompletionHandler["CompletionHandler"]
    ChatHandler --> ModelManager["ModelManager"]
    ResponseHandler --> ModelManager
    CompletionHandler --> ModelManager
    ModelManager --> TimedModel["TimedModel"]
    TimedModel --> Model["PreTrainedModel"]
```

Sources: [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:24-32](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:123-132](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:46-69]()

### Model Management & Lifecycle

`ModelManager` owns serving model configuration and tracks loaded models, per-model locks, and in-flight loading subscribers and tasks. It resolves the requested device, dtype, and attention implementation, retains quantization and timeout settings, and can preload a forced model. A forced model disables automatic unloading by setting the manager’s timeout to `-1`. [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:96-155]()

`TimedModel` wraps a model and its associated processor or tokenizer. It starts an inactivity timer, can reset that timer on request, and unloads the model and processor when the timeout is reached. Unloading deletes references, runs garbage collection, resets the Torch cache, cancels the timer, and invokes an optional callback. [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:46-94]()

The CLI exposes `model_timeout` and `force_model` serving options. When `force_model` is provided, the manager receives it during initialization and handles preloading. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:91-93](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:142-151](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:147-155]()

| Documented endpoint | Handler or role evidenced by supplied files |
|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` | `ChatCompletionHandler` is imported by `Serve`; the endpoint is documented for text and multimodal requests. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:123-126](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:24-27]() |
| `/v1/completions` | `CompletionHandler` is imported by `Serve`; the endpoint is documented for legacy text completions. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:125-127](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:26-28]() |
| `/v1/responses` | `ResponseHandler` is imported by `Serve`; its module describes streaming SSE and non-streaming JSON responses. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:127-129](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:14-18]() |
| `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | `TranscriptionHandler` is imported by `Serve`; the endpoint is documented for audio transcription. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:129-132](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:28-30]() |
| `/v1/systemone` | The endpoint is documented as answering typed questions with probabilities for allowed answers. [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:29-31]() |
| `/v1/models` | The endpoint is documented as listing available models. [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:30-32]() |
| `/load_model` | The endpoint is documented as streaming model-loading progress through SSE. [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:30-32]() |

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:120-151](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:46-94](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:96-155](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:14-18](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving.md:24-32]()

---

## 3. Response Parsing, Chat Templates & Reasoning

The shared serving utilities import `ResponseParser` and define `ReasoningText`, a tagged string type used to distinguish reasoning text from ordinary text chunks. The utilities also define fallback response-template rules for model families whose tokenizers do not provide a response template. The shown Qwen-family fallbacks describe parsing of reasoning markers and tool-call structures. [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:30-32](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:92-97](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:108-179]()

The `Serve` options include `reasoning` and JSON-formatted `chat_template_kwargs`. The option descriptions state that reasoning can use the chat-template default and that request-level `chat_template_kwargs` override the defaults. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:65-83]()

`ResponseHandler` implements the Responses API response stream. Its `_ResponseStreamBuilder` tracks response, message, and reasoning identifiers; content; sequence and output indexes; and tool calls. It emits response events through `BaseHandler.chunk_to_sse`; the shown methods create the initial response events and reasoning events. [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:98-123](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:124-170](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:172-202]()

Diagram: Parsed Assistant Content to Response Entities

```mermaid
graph TD
    GeneratedText["Generated assistant text"] --> ResponseParser["ResponseParser"]
    FallbackRules["_RESPONSE_TEMPLATE_FALLBACKS"] --> ResponseParser
    ResponseParser --> ReasoningText["ReasoningText"]
    ResponseParser --> ToolCall["ToolCall"]
    ResponseParser --> ContentText["Assistant content"]
    ReasoningText --> ResponseBuilder["_ResponseStreamBuilder"]
    ToolCall --> ResponseBuilder
    ContentText --> ResponseBuilder
    ResponseBuilder --> SSE["BaseHandler.chunk_to_sse"]
    SSE --> ResponseEvents["response.reasoning_text.delta"]
    SSE --> ResponseEvents2["response.output_item.added"]
```

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:30-32](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:92-97](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:108-179](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:98-123](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:142-170]()

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:65-83](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:30-32](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:92-97](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py:108-179](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/response.py:98-202]()

---

## 4. Server Performance Optimizations

`Serve` exposes options for continuous batching, attention implementation, compilation, quantization, device, and dtype. Continuous batching has additional options for KV-cache block size, block count, maximum batch tokens, memory fraction, and CUDA graphs. These values are collected into `cb_kwargs`; when any are supplied, the CLI constructs a `ContinuousBatchingConfig`. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:54-64](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:88-109](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:152-165]()

| Option group | CLI controls | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous batching | `--continuous-batching`, `--cb-block-size`, `--cb-num-blocks`, `--cb-max-batch-tokens`, `--cb-max-memory-percent`, `--cb-use-cuda-graph` | The CLI builds a `ContinuousBatchingConfig` from provided tuning values. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:54-57](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:94-109](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:152-165]() |
| Attention | `--attn-implementation` | The selected implementation is passed into `ModelManager`. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:58-60](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:142-151]() |
| Compilation | `--compile` | The option is declared in the CLI; the behavior after option parsing is not shown in the supplied excerpt. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:61-62]() |
| Quantization | `--quantization` | The option describes bitsandbytes 4-bit and 8-bit methods and is passed to `ModelManager`. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:62-64](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:142-151]() |
| Device and dtype | `--device`, `--dtype` | Passed to `ModelManager`; its constructor resolves the device and dtype. [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:88-90](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:113-145]() |

The serving optimization guide describes continuous batching as dynamically grouping and interleaving requests, and documents `--compile` as incompatible with continuous batching. These are documented behaviors; the supplied excerpts do not include the full implementation of those execution paths. [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving_optims.md:18-30](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving_optims.md:76-86]()

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:54-64](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:88-109](), [src/transformers/cli/serve.py:142-165](), [src/transformers/cli/serving/model_manager.py:113-145](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving_optims.md:18-30](), [docs/source/en/serve-cli/serving_optims.md:76-86]()

---

## 5. Interactive Chat Client

The chat module defines `RichInterface`, which receives a model identifier, user identifier, and base URL. Its `stream_output` method consumes an asynchronous stream of `ChatCompletionStreamOutput` values, reads the first choice’s delta content, tracks finish reason and completion-token usage when present, and updates the terminal display through Rich’s live-rendering interface. [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:112-137]()

During rendering, the client escapes certain angle-bracket tokens before Markdown display and rebuilds the accumulated text into lines for Rich rendering. The module also provides `get_service_root_url`, which removes a trailing `/v1` path component when finding the service root used by management endpoints. [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:105-110](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:138-160]()

The chat help text documents session commands and their intent: `!clear` resets the conversation, `!status` displays model and generation settings, `!example` selects a configured example, `!set` changes settings, `!save` writes chat history and settings, and `!exit` closes the interface. [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:72-102]()

Sources: [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:72-102](), [src/transformers/cli/chat.py:105-160]()

---

# Page: Downstream Ecosystem CI (vLLM, SGLang, TRL)

# Downstream Ecosystem CI (vLLM, SGLang, TRL)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml](.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml)
- [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml](.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml)
- [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml](.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml)

</details>



## Purpose and scope

This page describes caller workflows in the Transformers repository that exercise downstream projects against a Transformers revision. The available workflow definitions cover scheduled and manually triggered vLLM and SGLang integration runs, plus a trusted-commenter mechanism for dispatching TRL tests against a Transformers pull request’s head commit. These workflows test integration boundaries—such as model loading, processors, serving, and Trainer-related downstream effects—rather than replacing Transformers’ own test suites. [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:1-15]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:1-16]() [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:1-4]()

Sources: [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:1-15]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:1-16]() [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:1-4]()

## Workflow summary

| Downstream project | Trigger and tested revision | Execution shape |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | Scheduled nightly, manually dispatched, or pushed to a branch matching `vllm_ci*`. The workflow discovers a vLLM commit associated with a CPU wheel, then checks out that commit. [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:3-10]() [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:41-64]() | Installs Transformers and vLLM in a CPU-oriented environment, then runs selected vLLM tests and examples. [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:66-84]() [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:130-148]() |
| SGLang | Scheduled nightly, manually dispatched, or pushed to a branch matching `sglang_ci*`. The workflow checks out a pinned SGLang commit. [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:3-9]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:87-93]() | Runs a matrix of named suites in an Intel CPU container, with Transformers installed from the checkout under test. [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:18-32]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:33-78]() |
| TRL | A comment containing `/trl-ci` on a pull request in the Transformers repository can dispatch the TRL workflow, subject to a trusted-commenter gate. [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:7-22]() [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:25-38]() | Fetches the pull request head SHA and passes it as `transformers_ref` to TRL’s `Tests against Transformers branch` workflow. [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:40-61]() |

Sources: [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:3-10]() [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:41-84]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:3-9]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:18-32]() [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:7-22]() [.github/workflows/trl-ci-bot.yml:40-61]()

## System-to-code map: scheduled callers

This diagram connects the ecosystem CI concepts to the workflow names, jobs, and configuration entities used in the repository. The vLLM and SGLang caller workflows both support nightly scheduling and manual dispatch; their branch-pattern triggers are project-specific. [.github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml:1-10]() [.github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml:1-10]()

**Diagram: scheduled and manual ecosystem callers**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Nightly["Nightly integration check"] --> VLLMWorkflow[".github/workflows/vllm-ci-caller.yml"]
    Nightly --> SGLangWorkflow[".github/workflows/sglang-ci-caller.yml"]
    Manual["Manual workflow_dispatch"] --> VLLMWorkflow
    Manual --> SGLangWorkflow
    VLLMWorkflow --> VLLMJob["job vllm"]
```
